items.desc: Job Summary At the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT), we're on a mission to translate scientific discovery into real world impact. We bring together visionary scientists, technologists, policy makers, and entrepreneurs to tackle humanity's greatest challenges. We are looking for visionary Research Scientists in the Molecular Simulations and Design team who balance machine learning innovation with a mission-driven bias toward execution. Molecular Simulations and Design accelerates the design of biomolecules, with an initial focus on enzymes, by combining generative models, physical simulation, and learning from experimental data. You will push the frontier where these three meet. You will have the unique opportunity to translate your research innovations directly to experimental campaigns with a rapidly accelerating feedback cycle. We are particularly excited about physics-based methods working together with generative models to lead to generalizable and robust predictions of experimental outcomes and designs. Innovative research in new methodologies e.g.,: Boltzmann samplers, long-timestep molecular dynamics, machine learned interatomic potentials, generative models (including flow matching, diffusion). Full-stack research, from pre-training to fine-tuning to design-build-test loops. Key Challenge: Predictive simulation-based workflows, accelerated by machine learning. Merging physics and machine learning for robust generalization. Robust evaluations that translate to downstream impact on campaigns. Research innovations that go beyond performance on evals and have measurable acceleration of experimental campaigns. Ideal Background: PhD in a relevant field with a track record of excellence at the intersection of machine learning, biomolecules and simulations. Expertise building simulation-based pipelines to predict experimental outcomes and using machine learning to accelerate those pipelines. Experience with production grade pipelines for small molecules, biomolecules design and simulations. Agentic engineering skills and ability to build and validate end-to-end machine learning pipelines and in-silico design-build-test loops. Ability to ship at a high velocity. Requirements Responsibilities You will be expected to: Innovate & Lead: Conceptualize and develop original evals, training algorithms and fine-tuning recipes and connect them to ongoing design-build-test-loops End-to-end impact: Translate your work to experimental campaigns with a rapid feedback cycle. Publish & Present: Contribute to the global AI community through mentoring PhD students, co-authoring high-impact publications (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, etc.) and technical reports. Collaborate: Partner with cross-disciplinary squads of experimentalists, scientific domain experts, data domain experts and infrastructure to quickly move innovation to impact. Qualifications & Skills PhD in Machine Learning, AI, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field (Physics, Math, Computational Biology), or equivalent experience. Research Excellence: A proven track record of impactful research demonstrated by e.g. publications in top-tier AI venues or scientific journals. Technical Mastery: Deep expertise in deep learning frameworks and the ability to write high-quality, reproducible research code. Mission Mindset: A strong desire to apply advanced research to solve tangible, real-world problems in a fast-paced environment. Benefits We offer the following salary and benefits: Enhanced holiday pay Pension Life Assurance Income Protection Private Medical Insurance Hospital Cash Plan Therapy Services Perk Box Electric Car Scheme -- Why work for EIT: At the Ellison Institute, we believe a collaborative, inclusive team is key to our success. We are building a supportive environment where creative risks are encouraged, and everyone feels heard. Valuing emotional intelligence, empathy, respect, and resilience, we encourage people to be curious and to have a shared commitment to excellence. Join us and make an impact!

SuMaCer’s vision is to develop and optimise the entire value chain of functional ceramics, such as solid oxide fuel cells and metal-supported sodium batteries for energy storage solutions, with a holistic approach to sustainability with the incorporation of eco-design principles and circular economy strategies – covering the full loop from manufacturing to recycling. Researchers at the University of Birmingham will be focused on delivering the sustainability assessment including the determination of recycling pathways of these functional ceramics. To help us achieve our ambitious goal we are looking to recruit a post-doctoral staff member within the Metallurgy and Materials department. The postholder will play a leading role in these recycling activities and be responsible for assessing the elemental quantities of the materials as part of initial characterisation studies, to the safe disassembly and recovery of materials. The successful candidate will apply a range of recycling tools to separate the feedstocks and to restore functionality of the materials. The candidate will play an active role in data collection inputs/outputs to support the life cycle assessments to evaluate the recycling pathway of these functional materials. The postholder will be part of a vibrant and dynamic recycling team, as part of the Energy Materials Group (EMG) within the School of Metallurgy and Materials. Sustainability is a critical and interdisciplinary research theme at the University, and as such, the postholder will have amble opportunity to collaborate with colleagues across the Faculty of Engineering and Physical Sciences. As part of this role the postholder will work within the EMG and contribute to writing future bids; operating within area of specialism. items.desc: About The Company Zonneplan is a forward-thinking energy company committed to creating a sustainable future by eliminating fossil energy dependence in the Netherlands. Our mission, known as plan Zero, aims to achieve zero emissions, zero waste, and zero reliance on fossil fuels. We specialize in innovative energy trading and optimization, leveraging cutting-edge AI and machine learning technologies to make the energy grid smarter, cleaner, and more efficient. By integrating renewable energy sources such as solar panels, batteries, and electric vehicle charging stations into a Virtual Power Plant (VPP), we empower customers to maximize the value of their green energy while contributing to a more stable and sustainable energy network. About The Role As a Data Scientist within our Trading & Optimization team, you will work at the intersection of energy and artificial intelligence, developing and deploying advanced forecasting and optimization models that directly influence real-time trading decisions on the energy market. Your forecasts will immediately impact trading actions and are reflected in our live dashboards, creating a short and measurable feedback loop. You will collaborate closely with data scientists, engineers, and traders in a highly autonomous environment with minimal hierarchy, where ownership and accountability for live models are paramount. Your role involves designing interconnected models that incorporate probabilistic forecasting, market price signals (day-ahead, intraday, imbalance), customer behavior, and the physical dynamics of our VPP assets. You will be responsible for bringing models into production, monitoring performance, ensuring reliability, and continuously optimizing to maximize commercial impact. Your work will directly reduce trading costs, improve the return on our home battery product, and enable customers to benefit from solar bonuses rather than penalties. Additionally, you will prepare our systems for a post-subsidy future by adapting models to evolving market regulations and customer consumption patterns. We encourage proactive adoption of the latest AI and machine learning advancements, translating them into practical experiments and prototypes that enhance our forecasting capabilities and trading strategies. Qualifications Minimum of 3 years’ experience as a data scientist with strong foundations in statistics and machine learning. Proven expertise in forecasting and time series analysis. Proficiency in Python at a production level, including experience with deploying and monitoring live models. Experience with or strong affinity for AI-supported development tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar AI assistants. Ability to translate model quality into measurable commercial impact and data-driven decision making. Strong sense of ownership and responsibility for live-running models, including proactive intervention and optimization. Curiosity and proactivity in following and applying the latest AI and machine learning developments. Professional proficiency in Dutch is mandatory. Responsibilities Design and build integrated forecasting and optimization models that drive energy trading decisions. Manage multiple interconnected systems, including weather forecasts, market prices, customer behavior, and physical VPP asset performance. Deploy models to production in collaboration with engineers ensuring seamless integration and operation. Continuously monitor model performance, maintain reliability, and apply optimizations to improve outcomes. Translate forecasting accuracy into commercial benefits such as reduced trading costs and increased battery returns. Adapt models to evolving market regulations and customer consumption trends to maximize value. Lead experimentation with new AI and machine learning techniques, delivering working prototypes rather than theoretical concepts. Collaborate closely with traders and engineers in a fast-paced, low-hierarchy team environment. Benefits Competitive monthly salary ranging from €4,000 to €6,000 gross, commensurate with experience and seniority. 25 vacation days with the option to purchase additional days. Travel expense reimbursement. Subscription to Claude Code Max 20x to support daily work and personal development projects. Personal choice budget for sports, groceries, or other personal needs. Access to the Zonneplan Academy from day one, offering continuous learning and growth opportunities. Clear career progression towards senior data scientist roles specializing in energy trading, battery optimization, or forecasting. A pragmatic, no-nonsense work atmosphere with short communication lines and close collaboration with traders and engineers. Equal Opportunity Zonneplan is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Job Title
Research Scientist – Physics of Computed Tomography (all genders) 
 Job Description
 In this role, you will work in the field of systems and physics of computed tomography to help address unmet clinical needs in precision diagnosis.
 You will contribute to clinical CT systems and solutions focused on image quality, spectral results, radiation dose reduction and image reconstruction to increase diagnostic confidence and enable new clinical insights.
 Your role: 
 Develop, implement and validate innovative technologies for processing and calibration of non-spectral, spectral and photon-counting x-ray detectors in medical CT.
 Apply your know-how in x-ray physics, solid-state physics, medical imaging, algorithm development, advanced signal processing and AI to modern computed tomography.
 Develop and drive your own ideas for technological advances in CT and adjacent domains.
 Collaborate in interdisciplinary projects with business partners and clinical partners to transfer research results into clinically meaningful innovation.
 You should bring the following: 
 Master degree in physics, electrical engineering or data science/AI.
 Expertise in medical imaging physics, including generation, interaction with matter and detection of x-rays, with in-depth knowledge of computed tomography.
 Technical and clinical understanding of medical imaging, predominantly CT.
 Proficiency in modern programming, especially C/C++ and Python, including data science and AI tooling such as NumPy or PyTorch.
 Familiarity with deep learning, for example training neural networks, is an asset.
 Ability to provide technical consultation and subject-matter expertise to cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
 Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts, influence technical decisions and collaborate in global interdisciplinary R&D environments.
 Proficiency in English; German would be a plus.
 Doing meaningful work should come with fair, transparent rewards. The base salary range for this role is €75.336,00 – €85.744,64 and is governed by the applicable Collective Labour Agreement. The stated salary range reflects the salary progression within the relevant pay grade under the Collective Labour Agreement. New employees are generally hired at the entry level of the respective pay grade.
 Benefits include: 
 Annual leave: 30 days
 Mobility and devices: subsidized Germany ticket, leasing opportunities for private use (bicycles, cars, smartphones, ...)
 Philips University & Philips in Balance: wide range of professional training courses for personal development and healthcare
 Philips Pension Fund: employer-funded pension plan
 Philips Partnerzeit: two paid weeks off after your partner has given birth
 Philips MyShop: discount on Philips products
 Meals: free drinks and low prices in our canteen and Café Philistro
 Culture: informal culture, a paid day for voluntary work, various team and cultural activities, etc.
 How We Work Together 
 We believe that we achieve better results when we work together rather than apart. For this role this means to be on-site at least 3 days a week.
 About Philips 
 We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. With patient safety and Quality as our fundamental premise, we focus on regulatory requirements and quality standards in our daily work. Do the work of your life to help the lives of others.
 Learn more about our business .
 Discover our rich and exciting history .
 Learn more about our purpose .
 If you are interested in this role and have many, but not all, of the experiences needed, we encourage you to apply. You may still be the right candidate for this or other opportunities at Philips. Learn more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion on our careers site.

items.desc: About the job Can you see yourself revolutionising the Agentic AI industry? We are a multi-award-winning AI and SaaS provider based in Manchester, dedicated to boosting productivity and efficiency across our global customer base spanning five continents. As an ASR Researcher, you will be the architect of how our agents "hear" and understand speech. Conduct cutting-edge research on LLM-based speech recognition and audio-tokenisation, and push core conformer-based ASR architectures to their limit. Pair with junior team members to drive research goals and foster collaborative learning Contribute to original research, publish papers, and represent the company at global AI conferences. Maintain steady biweekly progression within our sprint-based research environment. Write concise technical documentation and research papers. Requirements PhD in Computer Science, Speech & Signal Processing, or a related field. Alternatively, an MSc and 2+ years of commercial or academic research experience in Speech or LLMs. Strong foundational understanding of Neural Networks, Large Language Models, and Conformer/Transformer architectures. Expert-level proficiency in Python and PyTorch. Proven ability to drive independent research with minimal supervision. Strong oral and written communication skills.

items.desc: Faculty of Engineering and Applied Sciences Aerospace and Aviation Research Fellow in AI-Enabled Flight Deck Systems Integration and Validation Fixed Term Contract for 37 months or until 30 April 2030, whichever is sooner Full time starting salary is normally in the range of £38,655 to £46,492 per annum, with potential progression up to £53,108 per annum Location: Cranfield, Bedfordshire Help us bring four strands of AI research together into one working flight-deck assistant, and test it with airline pilots in our research flight simulator. About the Role TRUST-IA is a research project funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme and coordinated by Cranfield, with university partners in Germany and France, and Rolls-Royce. It is developing an intelligent assistant to help airline pilots manage the engines, both in normal flight and when an engine fails. The assistant has four parts, each developed by a different partner: software that decides how the assistant should behave; monitoring of aircraft and engine condition; monitoring of the pilots; workload and trust from physiological and behavioural measures; and interaction through voice, gesture and mixed reality. You will bring these parts together in Cranfield’s Future Systems Simulator. You will build the software platform and automated tests that let them run as one system in real time, set up the flight scenarios, and run simulator trials with pilots to show that the integrated assistant works and is safe to use. You will also manage the day-to-day running of the simulator laboratory and publish the results. About You You will have a PhD in aerospace engineering or a related engineering subject, or equivalent research experience, and a background in aircraft modelling and simulation, flight dynamics or flight control. You will be a capable programmer (for example in C#, C++ or Python), and experience with Unity would be a real advantage. You will need enough understanding of artificial intelligence and machine learning to integrate and test AI software written by others. Experience of running simulator trials with pilots would be useful but is not essential, as training will be given. We are looking for someone with a good publication record for their career stage, who is well organised, enjoys working with industry and university partners, and is willing to take responsibility for a shared research facility. About Us As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield’s world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here. The Centre for Aeronautics, Propulsion and Power has been at the heart of aerospace research and education at Cranfield University since 1946. Its staff and researchers work across aircraft design, aerodynamics, flight dynamics, propulsion and sustainable power, with large-scale experimental facilities and long-standing links with industry. Our flight dynamics and simulation work covers fixed-wing, rotorcraft and eVTOL aircraft, and draws on the University’s research flight simulators, its own airport, and the National Flying Laboratory Centre. Find out more about our work here. Our Values and Commitments Our shared, stated values help to define who we are and underpin everything we do: Ambition; Impact; Respect; and Community. Find out more here. We aim to create and maintain a culture in which everyone can work and study together and realise their full potential. We are a Disability Confident Employer. We are committed to actively exploring flexible working options for each role and have been ranked in the Top 30 family friendly employers in the UK by the charity Working Families. Find out more about our key commitments to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion and Flexible Working here. Working Arrangements Collaborating and connecting are integral to so much of what we do. Our Working Arrangements Framework provides many staff with the opportunity to flexibly combine on-site and remote working, where job roles allow, balancing the needs of our community of staff, students, clients and partners. How to apply For an informal discussion about this opportunity, please contact Dr Linghai Lu, Reader in Flight Dynamics, Simulation and Control, on (T): 01234 754838 or (E): L.Lu@cranfield.ac.uk Apply online now. Please do not hesitate to contact us for further details on (E): peoplerecruitment@cranfield.ac.uk. Please quote reference number 5419. Therefore, we would encourage you to complete and submit your application as soon as possible.

items.desc: JOB DESCRIPTION About the Project SAFER PLUS is a £1.25 million Innovate UK-funded project developing Pakistan's first full-scale plant for converting agricultural waste cotton stalks and sugarcane bagasse into engineered bio-coal pellets through torrefaction. The bio-coal directly replaces imported fossil coal in textile mill boilers and brick kilns at 40–50% lower cost, with substantially reduced emissions. The demonstration hub is being established at the University of Kamalia, South Punjab, in partnership with Eco Research Limited and Pakistani textile industry partners. Northumbria University is now recruiting two Research Associates to join the SAFER PLUS team. These are distinct but complementary roles, and candidates should clearly indicate in their application which post they are applying for. Post 1: Research Associate in Thermochemical Conversion and Biomass Processing The Role You will lead the scientific characterisation and optimisation of the torrefaction process for Pakistani agricultural waste feedstocks. Working directly with the Principal Investigator, you will design and conduct experiments, produce validated fuel quality data, and generate the technical evidence base that underpins SAFER PLUS's commercial and regulatory case. Key Responsibilities Conduct thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) at multiple heating rates to characterise cotton stalk and sugarcane bagasse pyrolysis and torrefaction kinetics Develop and validate kinetic and thermodynamic models for the torrefaction process under industrially relevant conditions Characterise feedstocks and bio-coal products using XRD, FTIR, BET surface area analysis, SEM-EDS and proximate/ultimate analysis Determine gross calorific value (GCV), moisture, ash, volatile matter and sulphur content of bio-coal products under varying process conditions Investigate the effect of feedstock blend, moisture content, torrefaction temperature and residence time on bio-coal quality and consistency Contribute to peer-reviewed publications and project reports Support knowledge transfer activities with the University of Kamalia and industrial partners in Pakistan Essential Requirements MS/PhD in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Energy Engineering or a closely related discipline (or equivalent research experience) Demonstrated experience in thermochemical conversion of biomass, specifically pyrolysis, torrefaction or gasification Proficiency in TGA, kinetic modelling and thermodynamic analysis Experience with materials characterisation techniques including FTIR, XRD, SEM-EDS or BET Strong publication record commensurate with career stage Ability to work independently and manage experimental programmes Excellent written and verbal communication in English Desirable Requirements Experience with agricultural residue feedstocks particularly cotton stalk, sugarcane bagasse or wheat straw Familiarity with Pakistani or South Asian agricultural and industrial contexts Experience with proximate and ultimate fuel analysis for industrial applications Knowledge of cement, textile or brick kiln combustion requirements Further information about the requirements of the role is available in the person specification . Post 2: Research Associate in Machine Learning and Systems Integration for Clean Energy The Role You will develop and apply machine learning and data-driven modelling approaches to optimise the integrated SAFER PLUS energy system from feedstock characterisation through torrefaction to downstream combustion performance. You will work with experimental data generated by the project team and operational data from the demonstration plant to build predictive models that maximise bio-coal quality and system performance. Key Responsibilities Develop ML predictive models (including but not limited to Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Neural Networks) to predict bio-coal quality from feedstock properties and process parameters Build and validate process optimisation models integrating torrefaction conditions, feedstock blend and downstream combustion performance Design and implement a data acquisition and management framework for the SAFER PLUS demonstration plant at the University of Kamalia Develop real-time process monitoring tools and dashboards for plant operators in Pakistan Apply Python-based data science tools for model training, validation and deployment Collaborate with the thermochemical team (Post 1) to identify key process variables and translate model outputs into actionable operating guidance Contribute to peer-reviewed publications, particularly at the intersection of ML and biomass energy systems Support digital capacity building with Pakistani partner institutions Essential Requirements MS/PhD in Chemical Engineering, Data Science, Energy Systems, Computer Science or a closely related discipline (or equivalent research experience) Demonstrated experience in machine learning applied to engineering or energy systems classification, regression and …

items.title: AI/ML Engineer
items.card: What You'll Be Doing Build and ship AI features and systems end to end into live games and internal tools, at production quality and under real deadlines. Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice. Own evaluation as a first-class deliverable. Write and maintain the benchmarks, evals, and regression suites that tell you whether something is genuinely good, across the modalities you're working in.
items.desc: Supercell Helsinki Ohjelmointi Lisätty: 26.10.2026 Voimassa: 24.1.2027 Hae tästä Vanhentunut? Our AI team is looking for an individual who is exceptional at the applied end of the craft: taking modern models and turning them into features and tools that hold up in production, at Supercell scale, under real deadlines. The challenge at the centre of this role is the distance between a demo and a product. A model that works in a notebook is not a feature that works for hundreds of millions of players, or a tool a game team trusts with their daily work. Help us Close that gap: the evaluation that tells you it's actually good, the latency and cost envelope that makes it viable, the failure modes you find before players do, and the plumbing that makes it boring to operate. We're not looking for someone who wants to train a frontier model. We're looking for someone who gets unreasonable results out of the ones that exist. We are looking for someone to build and ship: AI features in live games, and the internal tools that give superpowers to Supercellians. Some of that work will take you inside a game or central team for a while, close enough to their craft to build the right thing with them. In our team, you'll work closely with our AI Platform Engineers, AI/ML engineers, Clients Programmers, Cloud Engineers. You’ll also collaborate with other teams including Data, QA, Engine and game teams. What You'll Be Doing Build and ship AI features and systems end to end into live games and internal tools, at production quality and under real deadlines. Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice. Own evaluation as a first-class deliverable. Write and maintain the benchmarks, evals, and regression suites that tell you whether something is genuinely good, across the modalities you're working in. Fine-tune, adapt, and distill models where it pays off, and have the judgment to know when a better prompt, better retrieval, or a smaller model beats training anything. Make sound trade-offs on inference, including on-device where it matters, against real parameter, latency, and battery targets, without losing the feel players expect. Take on the harder applied problems, such as making autonomous agents reliable and accurate enough to trust with real work. Work close to game and central teams, sometimes embedded with them for a stretch, and build things that stay in use after you move on. Mentor our more junior AI/ML engineers through code review, pairing, and design discussion, and raise the technical bar around you. Stay at the frontier by reading the literature and following the major conferences, and bring back what is genuinely useful. What You Have Strong, current command of modern generative methods at the applied level: you know what today's models are actually good at, where they break, and how to build reliably on top of them. A track record of shipping LLM or generative AI applications that real users used, in production, not prototypes. We value this far above a publication record. Real software engineering depth. You write code others can maintain, and you own things in production rather than handing them off. Hands-on experience writing and maintaining benchmarks and evaluation frameworks, ideally across more than one modality. Practical fine-tuning and model adaptation experience, and the judgment to know when not to reach for it. Sound judgment on inference trade-offs under tight compute, latency, and cost constraints, including local or on-device deployment. The ability to work from broadly defined goals, set your own objectives, and drive work forward without waiting to be handed a spec. High EQ and credibility with makers. You can sit inside a protective, high-craft team and earn their trust fast. A generous mentor to less experienced engineers, with high ownership, comfort taking risks and learning from failure, and the humility to do excellent work with kindness. Would Be Nice if You Also Have Experience with agent frameworks, orchestration, or evaluation tooling at production scale. Game industry experience, or a real appreciation for mobile. Experience working alongside a platform or infrastructure team as an internal customer. Where You'll Be The role requires close collaboration with the other central teams and game teams, so ideally, you'd be based in Helsinki. That's it about the role! Below, we've gathered some things we feel are important for you to know. Totally optional, but a highly recommended read. Once you're ready to apply, just send us your application through the form on the bottom of the page. ––– Hae tästä

items.desc: Who we are Born in 2014, Yoti is a digital identity and biometric technology company that makes it safer for people to prove who they are. The Yoti app was designed with privacy at its core, giving people a secure way to prove their identity and share third-party credentials with organisations and other people. Today, we have over twenty million app downloads around the world. We’ve expanded our offering to a suite of business solutions that span identity verification, age verification and estimation, e-signing, AI anti-spoofing technologies and we continue to think of innovative new offerings. From day one, we’ve been working to fix an outdated identity system. This is not a journey we make on our own but with policy advisors, think tanks, researchers, academics, humanitarian bodies, our users and everyday people. We are committed to solving identity problems through grassroots research and social purpose initiatives. Our dedication to our mission and our team is why Yoti was proudly named one of the Sunday Times Best Places to Work 2026 in the UK. More about the Team and the Role This role is part of our internal R&D team, working on innovative projects in computer vision, deep learning, and face biometrics. Some of the work the team is doing includes developing our in-house facial age estimation model, our facial anti-spoofing models and other AI-driven solutions. We’re seeking a mid level Machine Learning engineer with 2-4 years of experience working with a similar tech stack. You will be responsible for preparing, optimizing, and organizing large-scale multimodal datasets for deep learning, including building pipelines for image and video processing. This is a fantastic opportunity to work alongside experienced researchers in a fast-moving and innovative environment. Working Arrangements: This will be a hybrid role and you will be expected to work from our Aldgate office atleast 1 day a week. Responsibilities Build upon our existing preprocessing system to add functionality for new data modalities, and automation of data preprocessing tasks in Python and SQL. Manage large scale datasets, ensuring data integrity, quality and usability for research initiatives. Collaborate with research scientists to establish efficient experimentation and model training workflows. Develop tools that accelerate experimentation and streamline research processes. Support model evaluation conducting regression and performance tests to ensure model reliability and accuracy. Monitor and troubleshoot data pipelines, ensuring smooth operation and timely delivery of research data. items.desc: About The Role An exciting opportunity is available for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the School of Psychology at the University of Sussex and contribute to cutting-edge research on the neural basis of misophonia. This full-time position is available from January 2027 and will run until 30 September 2028. Misophonia is a poorly understood condition in which specific everyday sounds, such as chewing, breathing, or tapping, trigger intense emotional and physiological reactions that can profoundly affect quality of life. This project aims to transform our understanding of misophonia by revealing how the brain processes and represents the acoustic and semantic properties of sounds, and how these neural representations differ between individuals with and without the condition. Working as part of a world-leading research team studying anomalous perceptual experiences, you will contribute to a project funded by the Ream Foundation that combines cognitive neuroscience and advanced neuroimaging methods. The successful candidate will contribute independently to all stages of the project, publish high-quality research, and advance understanding of an important but underexplored condition. About You You will hold a PhD in cognitive neuroscience, psychology, audiology, or a related discipline, with expertise in sensory perception (e.g. hearing or vision), attention, or a closely related area. You will have experience in the acquisition and analysis of EEG data and a strong interest in understanding the neural mechanisms that give rise to perceptual experience. The ideal candidate will be a motivated and collaborative researcher capable of working independently. You will be excited by the opportunity to contribute to an emerging field, work as part of an internationally recognised research team, and help advance our understanding of the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying misophonia. About Our Faculty Our Psychology school has a rich history extending over half-a-century, marked from the start by our variety of research and courses. From the ground-breaking work of scholars such as Stuart Sutherland and Marie Jahoda, we've grown to cover all areas of psychology. The School was formally established in 2009, bringing together academics across biological, cognitive, developmental, clinical and social psychology into one School. We've now entered the second decade of our existence as one of the largest and most influential academic communities for psychology in the country! Anchored by our core values of kindness, integrity, inclusion, collaboration and courage, our research and teaching address societal challenges to create a better world. Please find further information regarding the School of Psychology. The School of Psychology is proud to hold a Silver Athena Swann Award. Why work here Our university is situated off the A27, next to the beautiful South Downs where you will enjoy everything that our 150-acre campus has to offer. We are accessible by public transport; Falmer train station is a five-minute walk to campus and several bus stops are located within campus. We also have dedicated cycling paths and encourage our staff to use these with our offering of a cycle to work scheme. Sussex is a renowned, multi-accredited, research-led International University and this is only possible because of the people that work here. Whether you are a member of Faculty, part of a Professional Services team or a Student, it’s our people that make us great and we want you to be part of that. Find Out More About Our Reward And Benefits Package. Find out about our equality, diversity and inclusion. Further Key Information Please contact Ediz Sohoglu (E.Sohoglu@sussex.ac.uk) for informal enquiries. The University of Sussex values the diversity of its staff and students, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds. items.desc:
Meta is looking for Research Interns to join our Fundamental AI Research (FAIR) organization, within Meta Superintelligence Labs. The role of FAIR is to drive long-term research for Meta. We publish groundbreaking papers and release frameworks/libraries that are widely used in the open-source community. We closely collaborate with other organizations at Meta to bring the latest research findings to production.
The team where this role sits is exploring new approaches to making AI more inclusive of all communities around the world, by strengthening performance across all languages. Past work in that space includes projects such as No Language Left Behind, Seamless Communication, Omnilingual ASR and Omnilingual Machine Translation. The mission is to develop state-of-the-art algorithms that ensure AI performance is sustained across languages, both in classic chat experiences as well as agentic workflows.
This is a 2026 internship opportunity with start dates from May to September. To learn more about our research, visit https://research.facebook.com.
Perform research to advance the science and technology of intelligent systems. Develop novel, accurate and efficient multimodal generative models for text, image, and other media. Contribute research that can be applied to Meta products. Analyze and improve efficiency, scalability, and stability of various deployed systems.

Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.
Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our Meta Superintelligence Lab in one of the post-training modeling teams, with a focus on Agentic AI, Muse and personal superintelligence. We are committed to advancing the field of artificial intelligence by making fundamental advances in technologies that help interact with and understand our world. We are seeking individuals passionate about agentic AI, including but not limited to LLM agentic tool use, personalized AI agents, LLM agentic post-training, LLM reasoning/coding, and related areas. Our interns have an opportunity to make core algorithmic advances, prototype agentic features for Meta products, and apply their ideas at an unprecedented scale.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.
Develop novel state-of-the-art agentic AI algorithms and corresponding systems, leveraging machine learning and reinforcement learning techniques. Conduct research on agentic LLMs, agentic RL environments, LLM post-training, and related topics. Analyze and improve the efficiency, scalability, and stability of agentic AI algorithms and deployed systems. Advance the science and technology of intelligent, agentic machines capable of reasoning, tool use, and personalized interactions. items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.



The Role

 

As an Applied Engineering Intern, you will work closely with our Applied AI Engineering team to facilitate the adoption of Mistral AI products among customers and collaborate with them to address complex technical challenges. This role is based in Paris, with an internship duration of 6 months. We are open to CIFRE programs as a continuation after the internship.

 

What you will do

 

• Contribute to the deployment of state-of-the-art GenAI applications, driving technological transformation with our customers.

• Collaborate with researchers, AI engineers, and product engineers on complex customer projects.

• Work with the product and science team to continuously improve our product and model capabilities based on customer feedback.

 

How We Work in Applied AI

 

- We care about people and outputs.

- What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it

- Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week.

- Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before

- We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care.

- No politics. Low ego, high standards.

- We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it.

 

About you

 

• You are currently pursuing a degree in AI, data science, or a related field from a tier 1 engineering school or university.

• You have strong programming skills in Python.

• You are familiar with machine learning algorithms and natural language processing techniques.

• You hold basic understanding of MLOps and deploying machine learning use cases.

• You have good communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

 

Ideally you have:

• Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch.

• Familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git) and Linux shell environment.

• Experience working in HPC Environments

• Publication record in AI or a related field

Job Title
Internship: Synthetic Data Generation for Dental AI (Master) 
 Job Description
 Start Date: January/February 2027
 Duration: minimum 6 months
 Type: Internship
 Weekly Presence: 40h (minimum 32h)
 Location: Eindhoven
 Internship: Synthetic Data Generation for Dental AI (Master) 
 Philips has a long history of successfully introducing innovative products to the market (lamps, CD players, medical imaging equipment, patient monitors, etc). Today, Philips is 100% health technology company with Data and AI being an integral part of Philips strategy. This internship develops a scalable pipeline for generating photorealistic synthetic intraoral images and automatic ground-truth labels from 3D jaws. Tooth detection and instance segmentation are the primary validation case. The same approach should also support other intraoral AI algorithms, such as gumline localization and detection of cavities or other oral conditions. Building on previous work in 3D jaw reconstruction and SAM mask generation/distillation, the project will quantify how synthetic data affects accuracy, robustness and the synthetic-to-real domain gap. 
 Your challenge: We are looking for an enthusiastic candidate who is passionate about computer vision, 3D graphics and deep learning. 
 Your team: You will be working in the R&D department of Philips Oral Healthcare in Eindhoven. The department works on cross-domain competences required to develop cutting-edge oral healthcare innovations, like machine learning, microbiology, sensors, optical imaging. 
 Your role: 
 Review 3D/synthetic dental data, rendering and domain-randomization methods.
 Build a data-generation pipeline from reconstructed or parametric 3D jaws.
 Vary anatomy, camera pose, lighting, materials and oral conditions.
 Export images with masks, depth, normals and tooth labels.
 Train/evaluate tooth detection and identification models; report conclusions.
 Draft a technical note or paper; present results at a Philips R&D forum.
 You're the right fit if: 
 MSc. in Data Science, CS, AI, Mathematics, Physics or Biomedical Engineering.
 Experience with Python programming is essential.
 Good knowledge of deep learning and computer vision in PyTorch.
 Passion for 3D modelling, rendering and synthetic data generation.
 Experience with Blender, 3D reconstruction or generative AI is a plus.
 Language: good written and spoken English.
 Previous internship experience is not necessary but is a plus.
 Good communication skills and enthusiasm to work in an international team.
 How we work together 
 We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week. Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.
 Monthly full-time allowance between €500 - €700 gross, depending on your education level. If you need to relocate to The Netherlands specifically for the internship there will be a different allowance. Part-time internships receive the allowance pro-rata.

To be eligible, your usual home-work travel distance needs to be more than 50 km or 1.5 hours of travel time (one way). Afterwards, you need to provide the rental contract from your (new) landlord.
 Travel compensation, if you are not eligible for a free public transport (OV chipkaart - student travel product); you can receive max. €192,- net depending on your location. Paid holidays per internship term.

items.desc:
Si vous avez déjà porté des lunettes, nous nous sommes déjà rencontrés. 
 Nous sommes un leader mondial dans la conception, la fabrication et la distribution de verres ophtalmiques, de montures et de lunettes de soleil. Nous offrons à nos partenaires de l’industrie dans plus de 150 pays l’accès à une plateforme mondiale de produits de soins de la vue de haute qualité (tels que la marque Essilor, avec Varilux, Crizal, Eyezen, Stellest et Transitions), des marques emblématiques que les consommateurs adorent (telles que Ray-Ban, Oakley, Persol, Oliver Peoples, Vogue Eyewear et Costa), ainsi qu’un réseau qui offre aux consommateurs des soins de la vue de haute qualité et des expériences d’achat de premier ordre (tels que Sunglass Hut, LensCrafters, Salmoiraghi & Viganò et le réseau GrandVision), et des plateformes de e-commerce de premier plan. 
 Rejoignez notre communauté mondiale de plus de 190 000 employés dévoués à travers le monde pour conduire la transformation de l’industrie des lunettes et des soins de la vue. Découvrez-en plus en nous suivant sur LinkedIn ! 
 Votre #FutureInSight avec EssilorLuxottica 
 Êtes-vous prêt à explorer de nouveaux horizons, à favoriser l’inclusivité et la collaboration, l’agilité, à éveiller la passion et à avoir un impact positif sur le monde ? 
 Rejoignez-nous pour redéfinir les limites de ce qui est possible ! 
 Votre rôle : 
 Basée à Sophia Antipolis (France), Pulse Audition est une jeune start-up au sein d'EssilorLuxottica. L'équipe est composée d'experts en intelligence artificielle, en traitement du signal audio, en audiologie, en systèmes embarqués et en développement logiciel qui travaillent ensemble pour développer des technologies de pointe destinées à être intégrées dans des lunettes intelligentes, afin d'améliorer l'inclusion sociale des personnes souffrant de troubles auditifs. 
 Le déploiement de nos algorithmes de réhaussement de la parole sur des cibles embarquées à ressources limitées impose de quantizer nos modèles IA pour respecter les contraintes de mémoire et de calcul du “produit”. Comme le modèle quantizé n'est qu'une approximation du modèle en pleine précision, une partie des performances peut être perdue lors de cette étape. Aujourd'hui, nous réduisons cet écart par de la quantization post-entraînement (PTQ). 
 L'objectif de ce stage est d'explorer les méthodes de Quantization-Aware Training (QAT), que nous pensons réellement capables de réduire l'écart entre les modèles en pleine précision et leurs versions quantizées. Le stage portera sur la recherche, l'implémentation et l'évaluation de stratégies d'entraînement qui améliorent la robustesse de nos réseaux de neurones aux pertes de performance induites par la quantization. Vos contributions nous aideront à délivrer des algorithmes de rehaussement de la parole de haute qualité dans des environnements à ressources contraintes, au service des personnes malentendantes. 
 Vos missions: 
 Étudier l'état de l'art des méthodes de QAT les plus récentes et présenter à l'équipe les approches les plus prometteuses. 
 Explorer les frameworks logiciels disponibles pour la QAT et proposer une stratégie d'intégration de l'un d'entre eux dans notre codebase existante, en cohérence avec notre pipeline de quantization actuel (PTQ, export ONNX, déploiement sur cible embarquée). 
 Évaluer la dégradation de performance des modèles quantizés lorsqu'ils ne sont pas entraînés avec des techniques de QAT. 
 Évaluer le gain de performance apporté par les techniques de QAT. 
 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe IA et développer les outils logiciels facilitant la mise en œuvre de la QAT dans notre codebase. 
 Des ressources de calcul GPU seront mises à votre disposition. Vous participerez aux réunions d'équipe et serez associé aux décisions liées à votre mission. 
 Profil : 
 En formation BAC +4/+5 une spécialisation en machine learning, data science, informatique, mathématiques et/ou traitement du signal. 
 Vous avez un fort intérêt pour le déploiement de modèles IA sur cible embarquée à ressources limitées. 
 Votre formation vous a permis d'acquérir des compétences dans les domaines suivants : 
 Deep Learning avec PyTorch et ONNX (indispensable) 
 Développement logiciel en Python. (fortement apprécié) 
 Outils de TinyML : quantization, pruning, etc. (fortement apprécié) 
 Environnement Linux. (souhaité) 
 Traitement du signal, informatique, mathématiques et machine learning (un plus) 
 Systèmes embarqués et développement en C (un plus). 
 Vous êtes une personne créative et autonome. 
 Vous souhaitez comprendre et contribuer aux processus de R&D. 
 Langues : français souhaité (niveau B2) ; anglais obligatoire (niveau C1)

items.desc: About the project Depression affects many people, but antidepressant treatment does not work equally well for everyone. Predicting treatment outcomes early could help clinicians make more informed decisions and tailor treatment to individual patients. In this postdoc project, you will investigate how adaptive, AI-informed mid-field MRI, guided by questionnaire data, can provide clinically useful biomarkers for predicting antidepressant treatment outcomes. By combining artificial intelligence, brain imaging and digital mood and symptom data, you will work towards a more affordable and widely accessible approach to precision psychiatry. You will focus on three main areas: Exploring how adaptive mid-field MRI can reduce scan time and improve prediction performance compared with fixed scanning protocols, while remaining feasible in outpatient clinics and settings with limited resources. Designing an MRI-based prediction pipeline using perfusion measurements from relevant brain regions, acquired with arterial spin labelling (ASL). Developing adaptive MRI acquisition methods in which AI models, including reinforcement learning, determine what to scan next based on the information already collected. About the role You will build on data from a large randomized clinical trial on treatment outcomes in major depressive disorder. Using these data, you will adapt existing prediction models and investigate whether mid-field perfusion MRI can support the early prediction of antidepressant treatment outcomes. You will develop an end-to-end prediction pipeline and translate your methods into an adaptive MRI strategy that can run directly on the scanner. You will also design and conduct a pilot MRI study in healthy volunteers, testing a prototype model deployed on the scanner. In addition, you will share your findings with the scientific community and contribute to the further development of the PRESS platform in collaboration with consortium partners from academia and industry. Your responsibilities include: Adapting existing predictive models to explore the feasibility of mid-field perfusion MRI for predicting antidepressant treatment outcomes. Developing an AI-based prediction pipeline that combines MRI perfusion measurements with relevant clinical and digital data. Implementing and testing adaptive mid-field MRI acquisition strategies, including a prototype model deployed on the scanner. Designing and conducting a pilot MRI study in healthy volunteers. Writing scientific papers, presenting your findings at international conferences and contributing to the integration of your methods into the PRESS platform. Profile You have a PhD in artificial intelligence, computer science, (biomedical) engineering, physics, computational neuroscience, technical medicine or a closely related field. You enjoy developing new technical approaches and applying them to clinically relevant challenges. In addition, you bring: Strong programming skills, for example in Python, PyTorch or TensorFlow, and experience with modern machine learning workflows. An affinity with, and preferably experience in, one or more of the following areas: MRI or other medical imaging, reinforcement learning or sequential decision-making algorithms, and clinical prediction modelling or health data science. Experience with perfusion imaging or ASL is an advantage. A clear interest in mental health, neuroimaging and translational research at the intersection of AI and medicine. Excellent written and spoken English, good communication skills and the ability to work independently and proactively in a multidisciplinary research environment. If you travel by foot, bicycle, or car, a mileage allowance of €0.21 per km applies (up to a maximum of 40 km one way by car). Do you prefer walking or cycling? Take advantage of our good bike scheme. Pension accrual with BeFrank, a modern, comprehensible and fairly priced pension. You will collaborate with clinical experts, imaging physics scientists and AI researchers to develop innovative MRI methods and translate them into meaningful outcomes for patients with depression. items.desc: Rejoignez-nous en Stage ! CEA Tech Corporate from CEA Tech on Vimeo . Description du poste : Les équipes du LIAE sont à la tête du développement du framework Aidge [1, 2]. Aidge est une plateforme open source et complète qui prend en charge l'ensemble du cycle de vie de l'IA, de la conception du modèle à son déploiement optimisé. De plus, elle offre un ensemble complet d'outils et de méthodologies, spécifiquement conçus pour les systèmes embarqués et les dispositifs edge, afin d'analyser, d'optimiser, de valider et de déployer efficacement les modèles d'IA. Le développement de l’outil est soutenu par les projets DeepGreen [3] et NEUROKIT2E [4], étant ainsi enrichi et utilisé par plusieurs partenaires industriels et académiques. L'objectif de ce stage est de s'appuyer sur les modules Aidge existants (tels que ceux dédiés à la description matérielle, la génération de code et le déploiement) afin de développer des heuristiques pour trouver la meilleure stratégie de déploiement pour un modèle de réseau de neurones et un matériel cible donnés. Plus précisément, le travail consistera à : Explorer et projeter (map) le graphe de calcul sur les différentes ressources matérielles (unités de traitement, composants mémoire) ; Identifier et appliquer les transformations de graphe pertinentes (ex. tiling/tuilage, remplacement d'opérateurs, quantification) ; Optimiser le déploiement pour respecter les contraintes d'allocation et de budget (ex. temps d'inférence, empreinte mémoire, consommation énergétique, exactitude des prédictions). À titre d'exemple, les cibles matérielles envisagées incluent des cartes telles que l'Alif Ensemble E7 [5] et la Texas Instruments TDA4VH [6]. Côté réseaux de neurones, l'étude s'appuiera sur des modèles de référence comme ResNet-18, ResNet-50 [7, 8] ainsi que YOLOv8 [9]. Références : [1] C. Moineau, M. Naud, I. De Albuquerque Silva, A. Farrugia, and O. Bichler. Aidge: A comprehensive and traceable library for deploying standalone embedded deep neural networks. 13th European Congress of Embedded Real Time Systems (ERTS 2026) , 2026. ⟨10.82331/ERTS.2026.42⟩. ⟨hal-05513843⟩ [2] Eclipse Aidge. https://eclipse.dev/aidge/ [3] Projet DeepGreen - https://deepgreen.ai/ [4] Projet NEUROKIT2E - https://www.neurokit2e.eu/ [5] Alif Semiconductor, Ensemble E7 Series Microcontrollers and Fusion Processors, Technical Datasheet / User Manual. [6] Texas Instruments, TDA4VH-Q1 Processors for High-Performance Automotive ADAS & Autonomous Driving, Product Folder. [7] K. He, X. Zhang, S. Ren, and J. Sun, "Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition," IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2016. [8] TorchVision / PyTorch documentation, ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 Model Architectures. [9] Ultralytics, YOLOv8 Real-Time Object Detection and Image Segmentation Model, 2023. # CEA-List Moyens / Méthodes / Logiciels Framework Aidge, développement en C++ et Python Profil du candidat Profil : Vous préparez un diplôme de niveau Bac+5 en informatique, systèmes embarqués ou génie logiciel. Vous êtes passionné(e) par la recherche scientifique et technologique et êtes reconnu(e) pour votre curiosité intellectuelle, votre esprit d'analyse et votre autonomie. Vous possédez des connaissances en Deep Learning ainsi qu'une expérience confirmée en développement embarqué (C/C++, optimisation bas niveau, contraintes matérielles). Rejoignez-nous, venez développer vos compétences et en acquérir de nouvelles ! Vous avez encore un doute ? items.desc: About This Position As wind and solar shares grow, more of the value of batteries, electrolysers and other flexible assets comes from short-term markets. Yet most energy system models represent only the day-ahead market, and therefore misprice flexibility. Intraday prices, where represented, are typically derived from historical correlations with day-ahead prices. Such approaches implicitly assume that price formation is independent of system composition. Because entering storage and flexibility shift the relationship between day-ahead and intraday prices, historically calibrated models misrepresent flexibility value precisely in the high-flexibility scenarios they are intended to evaluate. This internship applies conditional generative models, GANs, diffusion models or similar, to generate intraday price scenarios that respond to a future system configuration. The results feed into stochastic and rolling-horizon energy system optimisation. You will work with a multidisciplinary team at TNO at the interface of machine learning, electricity markets and energy system modelling. What will be your role? You will design, train and evaluate a conditional generative model for intraday prices or day-ahead to intraday spreads. Typical activities include Building a dataset from historical market and system data. Deriving conditioning features that describe system state and flexibility, using an energy system model (TulipaEnergyModel.jl). Implementing and training a conditional generative model, and comparing architectures. Benchmarking against simpler baselines such as quantile regression, copulas or historical resampling. Evaluating with proper scoring rules, and testing whether the model generalises to system configurations outside the training data. Translating findings into clear technical conclusions and recommendations. You will have space to bring your own ideas to the approach. What We Expect From You For this internship we are looking for a student with a background in Computer Science / Artificial Intelligence Data Science or Applied Mathematics Electrical Engineering Econometrics or Statistics Or a related field Preferred Qualifications Solid grounding in machine learning, in particular generative or probabilistic models. Strong Python skills; experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch is an advantage. Familiarity with time series modelling and probabilistic forecasting. Interest in electricity markets and energy systems; prior knowledge is not required. Ability to work independently and communicate technical results clearly. We are looking for a curious and proactive student who enjoys open-ended technical problems. What You'll Get In Return An internship at TNO means working in an environment where substance and impact are central. You will become part of a knowledge organisation where research and practice come together, and where experts collaborate on solutions to current societal and technological challenges. Your internship is a period in which you can discover what suits you, where your strengths lie and what you would like to learn next. You are part of a professional working environment, gain insight into how things work in practice, and have the opportunity to build experience that goes beyond this internship alone. For many students, an internship is therefore also a first step in discovering whether TNO could be a potential next step after graduation. items.desc: We are seeking a postdoc for 12 months to develop an AI pipeline predicting antidepressant response from mid-field MRI perfusion and digital mood and symptom data. You will test the approach in a pilot MRI study, working towards making precision psychiatry accessible in clinical care. About The Project Depression affects many people, but antidepressant treatment does not work equally well for everyone. Predicting treatment outcomes early could help clinicians make more informed decisions and tailor treatment to individual patients. In this postdoc project, you will investigate how adaptive, AI-informed mid-field MRI, guided by questionnaire data, can provide clinically useful biomarkers for predicting antidepressant treatment outcomes. By combining artificial intelligence, brain imaging and digital mood and symptom data, you will work towards a more affordable and widely accessible approach to precision psychiatry. You Will Focus On Three Main Areas Exploring how adaptive mid-field MRI can reduce scan time and improve prediction performance compared with fixed scanning protocols, while remaining feasible in outpatient clinics and settings with limited resources. Designing an MRI-based prediction pipeline using perfusion measurements from relevant brain regions, acquired with arterial spin labelling (ASL). Developing adaptive MRI acquisition methods in which AI models, including reinforcement learning, determine what to scan next based on the information already collected. About The Role You will build on data from a large randomized clinical trial on treatment outcomes in major depressive disorder. Using these data, you will adapt existing prediction models and investigate whether mid-field perfusion MRI can support the early prediction of antidepressant treatment outcomes. You will develop an end-to-end prediction pipeline and translate your methods into an adaptive MRI strategy that can run directly on the scanner. You will also design and conduct a pilot MRI study in healthy volunteers, testing a prototype model deployed on the scanner. Responsibilities In addition, you will share your findings with the scientific community and contribute to the further development of the PRESS platform in collaboration with consortium partners from academia and industry. Your responsibilities include: Adapting existing predictive models to explore the feasibility of mid-field perfusion MRI for predicting antidepressant treatment outcomes. Developing an AI-based prediction pipeline that combines MRI perfusion measurements with relevant clinical and digital data. Implementing and testing adaptive mid-field MRI acquisition strategies, including a prototype model deployed on the scanner. Designing and conducting a pilot MRI study in healthy volunteers. Writing scientific papers, presenting your findings at international conferences and contributing to the integration of your methods into the PRESS platform. Profile You have a PhD in artificial intelligence, computer science, (biomedical) engineering, physics, computational neuroscience, technical medicine or a closely related field. You enjoy developing new technical approaches and applying them to clinically relevant challenges. In Addition, You Bring Strong programming skills, for example in Python, PyTorch or TensorFlow, and experience with modern machine learning workflows. An affinity with, and preferably experience in, one or more of the following areas: MRI or other medical imaging, reinforcement learning or sequential decision-making algorithms, and clinical prediction modelling or health data science. Experience with perfusion imaging or ASL is an advantage. A clear interest in mental health, neuroimaging and translational research at the intersection of AI and medicine. Excellent written and spoken English, good communication skills and the ability to work independently and proactively in a multidisciplinary research environment. Our offer You will be employed by Amsterdam UMC Research BV. A contract for 12 months. Classification in salary scale 10: € 3.724 to € 5.867 gross for full-time employment (depending on experience). In addition to a good basic salary, we offer 8.3% end-of-year bonus. Calculate your net salary here (https://www.vismaraet.nl/bruto-netto-salaris-berekenen/). Holiday hours: 194.4 per year for full time and a possibility to save additional hours. 100% reimbursement for public transport travel costs. If you travel by foot, bicycle, or car, a mileage allowance of €0.21 per km applies (up to a maximum of 40 km one way by car). Do you prefer walking or cycling? Take advantage of our good bike scheme. Pension accrual with BeFrank, a modern, comprehensible and fairly priced pension. items.card: The role The Ultrasonics and Non-Destructive Testing (UNDT) research group is seeking a Research Associate who will contribute to project “3D ultrasonic imaging for characterisation of critical microstructural locations in polycrystalline materials,” which aims to develop a material characterisation framework based on using ultrasonic array measurements to create a volumetric map of local microstructural properties.
items.desc: The role The Ultrasonics and Non-Destructive Testing (UNDT) research group is seeking a Research Associate who will contribute to project “3D ultrasonic imaging for characterisation of critical microstructural locations in polycrystalline materials,” which aims to develop a material characterisation framework based on using ultrasonic array measurements to create a volumetric map of local microstructural properties. This project offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research at the interface of materials science, ultrasonic imaging, and advanced signal processing with significant benefits and applications in aerospace, nuclear, renewable and conventional energy, and other industrial sectors. The UNDT group at the University of Bristol is a world leader in the application of ultrasonic arrays to NDE problems. The major initial development was the concept of Full Matrix Capture (FMC), which consists of recording signals from all transmitter-receiver array elements and then performing imaging in post-processing. This approach has completely transformed the use of ultrasonic arrays for NDE and is now available on most commercial platforms. Another significant achievement was related to the development of FMC based defect characterisation algorithms. This post is full time and has funding for up to 14 months. What will you be doing? This role focuses on the optimisation and validation of ultrasonic microstructural characterisation methods. The successful candidate will perform experimental material testing using a range of conventional material characterisation techniques, generating datasets to support numerical modelling and ultrasonic measurements. You should apply if The successful candidate will demonstrate strong expertise in materials science, ultrasonic imaging and signal processing, with a clear track record of research excellence and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary environment. Essential Qualifications And Experience A PhD (or near completion) in Materials Science, Engineering, Physics, or a closely related field Research experience in ultrasonic non-destructive testing Hands-on experience in conventional microstructure characterisation methods (e.g. Electron Back-Scattered Diffraction) Additional information To find out more about what it's like to work in the Faculty of Engineering, and how the Faculty supports people to achieve their potential, please see our staff blog: https://engineering.blogs.bristol.ac.uk/category/engineering-includes-me/ Contract type: Open ended with fixed funding until 14 months Work pattern: Full time/35 hours per week Grade: I – Pathway 2 Salary: £40,704 - £45,641 (Grade I) per annum School/Unit: School of Electrical, Electronic and Mechanical Engineering This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on 10/11/26 The interviews will take place shortly after the closing date For informal queries please contact: Alexander Velichko, Senior Lecturer +44 117 33 15920, a.velichko@bristol.ac.uk Our strategy and mission We recently launched our strategy to 2030 tying together our mission, vision and values. items.desc: Location: Remote About The Job At Alignerr, we partner with the world’s leading AI research teams and labs to build and train cutting-edge AI models. You’ll challenge advanced language models on topics like computer architecture and hardware design, embedded systems and IoT, networking and distributed systems, hardware security, and systems software and operating systems—documenting every failure mode so we can harden model reasoning. Organization : Alignerr Position : Computer Engineering Expert - AI Content Specialist Type : Hourly Contract Compensation : $35–$60 /hour Location : Remote Commitment : 10–40 hours/week What You’ll Do Develop Complex Problems: Design advanced computer engineering challenges across domains like RISC-V/ARM architecture, FPGA development, memory management, and hardware-software co-design. Author Ground-Truth Solutions: Create rigorous, step-by-step technical solutions, including assembly code, hardware description language (HDL) snippets, and architectural diagrams that serve as "golden responses" for AI training. Technical Auditing: Evaluate AI-generated code (C/C++, Verilog, VHDL), logic gate designs, and operating system kernels for technical accuracy, efficiency, and adherence to industry standards. Refine Reasoning: Identify logical fallacies in AI reasoning—such as race conditions, memory leaks, or improper timing constraints—and provide structured feedback to improve the model's "thinking" process. Requirements Advanced Degree: Masters (pursuing or completed) or PhD in Computer Engineering, Computer Science with a hardware focus, or a closely related field. Domain Expertise: Strong foundational knowledge in core areas such as Computer Architecture, Embedded Systems, Digital Logic Design, or Operating Systems. Analytical Writing: The ability to communicate highly technical hardware concepts and low-level software logic clearly and concisely in written form. Attention to Detail: High level of precision when checking bit-level operations, clock-cycle timing, and technical documentation. No AI experience required Preferred Prior experience with data annotation, data quality, or evaluation systems Proficiency in engineering software concepts (e.g., SolidWorks, MATLAB, ANSYS) to evaluate AI-generated code or workflows. Why Join Us Competitive pay and flexible remote work. Collaborate with a team working on cutting-edge AI projects. Exposure to advanced LLMs and how they’re trained. Freelance perks: autonomy, flexibility, and global collaboration. Potential for contract extension. items.desc:
mimic is an early stage deep tech robotics & AI start-up based in Zurich and supported by leading VCs. We give industry workers a helping hand for tedious manual labour tasks and mitigate labour shortages with a versatile automation platform. Our automation solutions, driven by dexterous robotic hands and cutting edge AI trained on human observations, bring a new level of AI embodiment to the real world. 
 As a Robotics Engineer, Model Deployment , you will bring mimic's AI capabilities to new robotic platforms and customer environments. You will work directly with robotics customers to integrate our models, optimize their software and robotics stack, and drive the technical changes required for successful deployment. 
 Working across AI, robotics, and software, you will own technical integrations from initial planning through deployment. You will also help build scalable tooling and workflows that make our AI capabilities easier to deploy, monitor, and improve across different robotic platforms 
 Responsibilities 
 Integrate and deploy mimic's AI models on different robotic platforms and hardware stacks
 Adapt our software, training, and deployment stack to new robots, sensors, and environments
 Work directly with customer engineering teams to integrate and optimize their robotics stack
 Diagnose AI, software, and robotics integration issues and drive them to resolution
 Build scalable tooling and workflows for deploying, monitoring, and improving our models
 Define technical requirements and implement features that improve model productization
 Own deployment planning and execution, coordinating across customers and internal teams
 Translate deployment learnings into improvements for our AI, robotics, and product stack
 Track deployment performance and communicate progress and technical risks to stakeholders
 Requirements 
 Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Robotics, AI, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field
 Strong robotics background and a very good understanding of physical AI and robotics systems
 Excellent software engineering skills, with the ability to design, implement, and test robust solutions
 Strong Python skills and experience with modern machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch
 Experience deploying AI/ML systems on real robotic hardware
 Good understanding of AI training methods, data pipelines, and model evaluation
 Ability to build repeatable and scalable solutions rather than one-off integrations
 Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work across AI, software, and robotics
 Strong ownership and ability to independently plan and execute technical deployments
 Excellent communication skills and confidence working directly with technical customers
 Fluent English
 Willingness to travel for customer deployments and technical workshops
 Driving Licence (B)
 Nice to have 
 Familiarity with modern robot learning approaches (imitation learning, reinforcement learning, diffusion policies, foundation models)
 Experience with robotic manipulation, ROS/ROS2, robot control systems, or simulation environments
 Experience integrating AI models with robotic hardware platforms
 Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, containerization, and deployment tooling (Docker, Kubernetes, etc.)
 Compensation & Benefits 
 We offer a total compensation package including a competitive yearly base salary and a strong stock option package to make you part of our shared success. 
 You will have the opportunity to shape a robotics & AI company from the ground up . In flat hierarchies you will work directly with the founders and some of the best talents in the robotics space. At mimic, you are accepted for who you are. As part of our ongoing journey towards creating a diverse and inclusive environment we encourage everyone to apply and we are looking forward to you bringing along your knowledge, personal experiences, and fresh perspectives. Together we can solve some of the greatest challenges in robotics.
