items.desc: Fixed term contract | Belvaux | 36 Months Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/ How will you contribute? Within LIST’s Sustainable Urban and Built Environment (SUBE) group, this position focuses on geospatial technologies for sustainable, climate-neutral and resilient built and natural environments . You will design and develop reusable geospatial software and analytics for a digital twin platform supporting European research and innovation projects . You will combine spatial data engineering, analytics, 2D/3D visualisation and GeoAI to turn heterogeneous data and models into interoperable services and decision-support applications for cities, regions and environmental systems. Working with researchers, software engineers and domain experts across LIST and European partners, you will explore pragmatic AI-assisted and agentic workflows for discovering, combining and interpreting trusted geospatial data, models and services, with appropriate human oversight, validation, provenance and explainability. You will translate research concepts into robust prototypes and reusable solutions demonstrated with European cities and regions. Describe the main responsibilities of the position. · Designing, developing, testing and documenting reusable components for geospatial digital twins and decision-support applications. · Building reproducible pipelines for large, heterogeneous and spatio-temporal datasets, integrating data, models and services through OGC APIs, SensorThings API, STAC, 3D Tiles, CityGML/CityJSON and related standards. · Developing APIs, microservices and interactive 2D/3D geospatial applications. · Implementing spatial analytics, simulation and GeoAI for urban, mobility, energy, climate and environmental applications. · Prototyping AI-assisted interfaces and workflow orchestration for accessing and combining geospatial data, models and services. · Applying sound software-engineering practices, including testing, version control, containerisation, continuous integration and documentation, while translating user and partner needs into reusable technical solutions. Candidates at an earlier career stage with a strong technical portfolio are encouraged to apply. · Strong practical programming skills in Python. · Experience with geospatial data processing and spatial databases, for example GDAL, GeoPandas, PostGIS, QGIS or GRASS GIS. · Experience developing APIs or web-based software and working with Git. · Understanding of good software-engineering practices, including testing, documentation and maintainable code. · Ability to communicate effectively in English and work in multidisciplinary teams. items.desc: Chromatography and mass spectrometry with a focus on NTA and data Would you like to solve complex chemical questions using chromatography and mass spectrometry, and get more value from the data you generate? At VITO, we are looking for a researcher with demonstrated experience in organic analysis and non-target analysis (NTA), preferably using both liquid chromatography (LC) and gas chromatography (GC). If you combine experimental expertise with a strong interest in data management, data processing, and artificial intelligence (AI), this opportunity is made for you. Your team and our research ambition VITO supports companies, governments and society in the transition towards sustainability. Within the Materials & Chemistry (MatCh) unit, you contribute to research on circular feedstocks, sustainable chemistry, materials and more efficient industrial processes. As the Flemish Reference Laboratory for the Environment, VITO translates analytical innovation into reliable measurement methods for water, soil and air. You contribute to the development of methods that can be applied in research, environmental monitoring and regulatory contexts. You will join the chromatography team within GOAL, our specialised laboratory for organic and inorganic analysis. With more than 150 projects each year, we address diverse questions for industry and government, conduct strategic basic research and undertake reference laboratory activities. Our clients often bring a problem for which you develop the analytical approach together with the team. Tailored solutions, method developments and scientific interpretation are central to our work. Today our team is expanding its NTA portfolio by integrating AI into its workflow to better characterize known and unknown substances. As such, you will support the development of robust NTA measurement methods and turn analytical data into reusable knowledge for innovation, chemical safety and policy. Organic analysis and method developments You develop, optimise and validate methods for small organic molecules, including but not limited to active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), xenobiotics, PFAS, and micropollutants. You select appropriate sample preparation protocols, separation and detection methods according to the matrix and research question. You work with LC and GC coupled to mass spectrometry, including tandem mass spectrometry and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). You combine targeted analysis, suspect screening and NTA where they add scientific value. You take responsibility for the entire analytical workflow, from experimental design and measurement protocols to quality assurance, interpretation and reporting. You work in the laboratory, support troubleshooting and guide analysts during implementation. You build reproducible NTA workflows for different matrices. You pay particular attention to blanks, reference materials, quality controls, structural elucidation and annotation confidence.  Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts, influence technical decisions and collaborate in global interdisciplinary R&D environments.

The research carried out at the department is performed in close connection with the clinical activities at the Uppsala University Hospital, which includes both basic studies on the causes of a variety of illnesses and the development and evaluation of improved diagnostics and new treatment methods. More information about the Department of Medical Sciences can be found at https://www.uu.se/en/department/medical-sciences. The neurotrauma research group at Uppsala University and Uppsala University Hospital conducts clinical and translational research focusing on individual differences in recovery following traumatic brain injury. Our research combines clinical patient data, continuous physiological monitoring from neurocritical care, neuroimaging and advanced data analytics. This project aims to develop and validate AI-based models for dynamic outcome prediction and improved understanding of secondary brain injury, with the long-term goal of supporting personalised care. Duties The position involves developing, implementing and evaluating machine learning and artificial intelligence methods for research data from patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI). Main duties include: Processing and integrating longitudinal clinical data, physiological time series (e.g. ICP, CPP and blood pressure), laboratory data and imaging-derived variables. Developing and externally validating predictive models of clinical outcomes and physiological changes during intensive care. Developing reproducible analytical pipelines, quality assurance, documentation and secure data workflows. Conducting scientific analyses, preparing manuscripts and presenting findings in interdisciplinary collaboration with clinicians and researchers. Requirements PhD in computer science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, bioinformatics or another field relevant to the position. Documented experience developing and evaluating machine learning or deep learning models. Strong Python programming skills and experience with relevant machine learning frameworks, such as PyTorch. Experience in quantitative data analysis and scientific research, including the ability to document and communicate results. Ability to work independently and in interdisciplinary teams, and excellent English communication skills. Additional qualifications Experience in generative artificial intelligence, including diffusion models, synthetic data generation and data augmentation techniques. ⁠Experience in high-performance computing (HPC), GPU acceleration, and the development and optimization of scalable machine learning and deep learning workflows. Experience in computer vision, medical or scientific image analysis, and multimodal machine learning involving heterogeneous data sources. About the employment The employment is 12 months . Für den klinischen Einsatz optimieren: Modellarchitekturen auf Latenz, Skalierbarkeit und Ressourceneffizienz im Echtzeit-Klinikbetrieb zuschneiden. Your work will contribute directly to creating tools and capabilities used by our customers and employees. Analyzing extensive biological and operational datasets and developing statistical models to identify and evaluate meaningful patterns, relationships, and opportunities for improvement. Defining data requirements and independently retrieving, combining, and quality-assuring large and heterogenous data sets to build reproducible analytical workflows and reusable data pipelines, ensuring traceability and appropriate documentation throughout the process. Interpreting and communicating findings to internal and external audiences, translating complex results into practical insights that support fact-based decision-making and further development. You combine scientific judgement with technical discipline and are comfortable moving between exploratory research questions and the development of hands-on solutions. Most importantly, we are looking for someone who enjoys working across disciplines. You can discuss biological hypotheses with scientists, independently investigate the underlying data, and work with software engineers and customer contacts to determine how a promising research method can become a reliable functional capability. As An Ideal Candidate, You Have A PhD in aquaculture, biology, environmental science, or another relevant life or quantitative natural science, and preferably 3-5 years of additional relevant research and/or applied analytical experience. A solid understanding of applied research methodology, experimental design, statistical modeling and result validation. items.desc: We're looking for a hands-on engineer to build two foundations of the Tricorder product: the evaluation harness and training data pipeline behind our AI models, and a clinical knowledge base grounded in tactical combat care, SNOMED CT and ICD-10. Most healthcare technology assumes a hospital: reliable power, connectivity and a clinician at a desk. Care increasingly happens somewhere else - in the field, in transit, in remote and contested environments, and in the critical minutes before a patient reaches a ward. Tricorder builds the deployable clinical infrastructure for that world: a rugged, self-contained hardware and software platform that lets clinical teams capture, monitor and act on patient data anywhere, even when the network or the grid can't be relied on. It is a dual-use venture serving defence medical and civilian pre-hospital care. Our prototype product is already in user testing. Edge AI sits at the core: multimodal language models that turn video, sensor data and clinical notes into patient records, drive predictions and inform data-driven learnings across deployments. To trust those models in the field, we need rigorous data and evaluation - that's where you come in. What you'll do You'll own two workstreams, working day to day with the founder and the FF build team. 1. Data pipeline and evaluation harness Build the data foundations that tell us whether our models are good enough for clinical use. Data labelling: design labelling schemas and guidelines, set up tooling, and run labelling with clinical input, including quality checks and inter-annotator agreement. Data processing: build reproducible pipelines to ingest, clean, de-identify and transform multimodal data (video, sensor streams, text). Video data organisation: structure, version and catalogue video datasets so clips, annotations and metadata stay searchable and traceable. Training dataset preparation: assemble balanced, well-documented train, validation and test splits, with clear lineage from raw data to model input. Eval harness: build an automated harness that benchmarks vision-language and NLP models against clinically meaningful metrics, tracks regressions and supports build-vs-buy model decisions. 2. Clinical knowledge base Build the structured clinical knowledge base that turns unstructured input into coded, interoperable records. Database design: design the schema and stand up the data store for clinical concepts and their relationships. Clinical terminologies: ingest and map TC3, SNOMED CT, ICD-10 and related NHS standards, including cross-mappings between them. Natural language processing: extract entities and relationships from clinical text and link them to coded concepts. Document handling: parse and structure clinical documents (PDFs, notes, forms) into the database. Clinical knowledge: work with clinicians to make sure the database reflects real-world clinical reasoning and pre-hospital workflows. By the end of the first 3 months, we'd expect a working eval harness in use for model decisions, a labelled and versioned core dataset, and a first version of the knowledge base linked to the product. What we're looking for We don't expect one person to be expert in everything below. Strong candidates will be deep in one workstream and credible in the other. Must-haves Strong Python and data engineering skills, with a track record of shipping production data or ML pipelines, not just research notebooks. Hands-on experience building ML evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or test harnesses, ideally for vision, video or language models. Experience running data labelling and training-data preparation, including annotation tooling and quality control. Working knowledge of databases and data modelling. Practical NLP experience: entity extraction, entity linking or document parsing. Comfort handling sensitive data under data protection and clinical safety constraints. Pragmatism and speed: you can work with ambiguity, make good build-vs-buy calls and ship in weeks, not quarters. Nice to have Experience with SNOMED CT, ICD-10, dm+d or other NHS clinical terminologies and coding. A background in health-tech, clinical informatics or another regulated domain such as defence. Experience with video data at scale (frame sampling, temporal annotation, multimodal datasets). Familiarity with FHIR or HL7 interoperability standards. Experience working with LLMs and VLMs, including edge or on-device deployment. Early-stage startup experience, especially as a founding or early engineer. Probably not the right fit if You need detailed specs and a large team around you to be effective. You prefer pure research over building tools people use every day. This is a high urgency opening, and we are flexible to consider applicants either on a more flexible consultancy agreement (rolling by mutual agreement, with a competitive day rate); or a long term permanent employment contract with shares as part of the package and scope to grow into a longer-term …

items.desc: Location: Munich Type: Full-time The Role: We’re partnering with an ambitious robotics start-up developing autonomous warehouse robots that are already operating in live customer environments. We’re looking for a Research Engineer specialising in Reinforcement Learning (RL) and robotic manipulation to develop policies that enable robots to perform precise, contact-rich tasks. You’ll work across simulation, control and real-world deployment, training policies in large-scale simulated environments before transferring them onto physical robotic systems. This is a hands-on research role where your work moves beyond experimentation. You’ll tackle genuine customer use cases, work directly with deployed hardware and iterate against real-world feedback. The objective is to turn cutting-edge research into reliable robotic capabilities that can be rolled out across an expanding fleet. Key Responsibilities Reinforcement Learning: Develop and train RL policies for precise robotic manipulation, including contact-rich tasks that require accurate force, position and motion control. Simulation & Sim-to-Real: Build and scale simulation-based training environments, transferring learned policies to physical robots and addressing the challenges of sim-to-real generalisation. Robot Control: Combine reinforcement learning with classical control methods and learned controllers to improve precision, robustness and operational safety. Policy Optimisation: Design experiments, evaluate performance and refine policies against real-world task requirements and deployment constraints. Simulation Infrastructure: Work with modern robotics simulation frameworks to support large-scale training, testing and evaluation. Real-World Deployment: Integrate successful policies into the robotics autonomy stack and validate their performance on deployed hardware. Applied Research: Translate emerging techniques in robotic learning into practical capabilities, balancing research innovation with reliability and production readiness. Skills & Experience Hands-on experience developing reinforcement learning methods for robotic control and manipulation. Experience training policies in simulation and deploying them on physical robotic hardware. Strong understanding of sim-to-real transfer, including domain randomisation, system dynamics and policy generalisation. Experience with large-scale robotics simulation environments such as NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, MuJoCo or equivalent. Strong foundations in robotics, control theory, dynamics and motion planning. Proficiency in Python and modern machine learning frameworks, with the ability to develop robust, production-quality research code. Evidence of practical research output, such as deployed robotic policies, open-source projects or relevant academic publications. Ability to work experimentally, diagnose failure modes and iterate quickly between simulation and real-world testing. Desirable Experience Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and learning-based robotic manipulation. Imitation learning, behavioural cloning or learning from demonstrations. Code-as-Policy approaches to robotic task execution. Experience with real-world robotic arms and contact-rich manipulation. A PhD in robotics, machine learning, computer science or a related field, supported by a strong research track record. Publications at leading robotics and machine learning conferences, including ICRA, CoRL, ICLR or CVPR. The Opportunity Work on physical AI systems already deployed in real customer environments. Take ownership of the full research-to-deployment lifecycle, from simulation and policy training through to real-world execution. Solve challenging manipulation problems with direct commercial relevance. Work at the intersection of reinforcement learning, robot control and autonomous systems. See research translated into operational capabilities on a short development cycle. How to Apply We’re particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate their work beyond a CV. When applying, include a link to a trained policy running on a real robot, a relevant research paper or an open-source repository showcasing your technical contributions.

Are you a MS or PhD student interested in a 2026 internship in the field of machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, large language models, speech technology, robotics, computer vision, optimization, operations research, quantum computing, automated reasoning, or formal methods? If so, we want to hear from you!
We are looking for students interested in using a variety of domain expertise to invent, design and implement state-of-the-art solutions for never-before-solved problems.
You can find more information about the Amazon Science community as well as our interview process via the links below;
https://www.amazon.science/
https://amazon.jobs/content/en/career-programs/university/science
https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/university-roles/applied-science
Key job responsibilities
As an Applied Science Intern, you will own the design and development of end-to-end systems. You’ll have the opportunity to write technical white papers, create roadmaps and drive production level projects that will support Amazon Science.
You will work closely with Amazon scientists and other science interns to develop solutions and deploy them into production. You will have the opportunity to design new algorithms, models, or other technical solutions whilst experiencing Amazon’s customer focused culture.
The ideal intern must have the ability to work with diverse groups of people and cross-functional teams to solve complex business problems.

items.desc:
We are seeking a highly motivated intern (Contract Worker) to join our research team working on self-improving agentic systems — a cutting-edge area at the intersection of reinforcement learning, LLM post-training, and autonomous AI research agents. 
We develop agentic systems that improve their own performance over time, combining reinforcement learning and LLM post-training with agents capable of writing, evaluating, and optimizing code. A central goal is building AI research agents that can autonomously propose, run, and analyze experiments, accelerating the pace of AI research itself.
Assist in the design, implementation, and evaluation of self-improving agentic systems and AI research agents. Contribute to research on reinforcement learning and LLM post-training methods, including reward design, preference optimization, and RL from execution feedback. Collaborate with senior researchers to explore new approaches for autonomous experimentation, code generation, and optimization. Help build and maintain evaluation harnesses and benchmarks for agentic capabilities. Help document findings and prepare research outputs for publication.
Currently is in the process of obtaining a Ph.D. degree in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Information or Multimedia Retrieval, Reinforcement Learning, Mathematics or relevant technical field Experience with Python, C++, C, Java or other related language Experience with deep learning frameworks such as Pytorch or Tensorflow Experience building systems based on machine learning and/or deep learning methods Eagerness to learn about advanced AI concepts such as reinforcement learning, LLM post-training, agentic scaffolding, and self-improvement Excellent problem-solving and communication skills

About Pinterest: 
 Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product.
 Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible.
 At Pinterest, AI isn't just a feature, it's a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.
 Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here .
 As a Machine Learning Intern at Pinterest, you’ll apply machine learning and AI to product and engineering challenges. You’ll work with engineering, product and data teams to prototype, evaluate and improve ML-powered features and discovery experiences. Throughout your internship, you’ll contribute to real projects, learn how large-scale ML systems are developed and build practical skills with guidance from experienced engineers.
 What you’ll do: 
 Own a scoped machine learning project from problem definition through experimentation, implementation and communication of results, with guidance from your manager and team
 Contribute to applied machine learning and AI research that informs Pinterest product experiences
 Collect, analyze and synthesize data to develop data-driven machine learning models
 Write clean, efficient and maintainable code, supported by appropriate documentation and testing
 Apply relevant machine learning techniques, including natural language processing or graph-based approaches, to modeling and ranking problems across discovery, ads and search
 Break down scoped technical problems, propose approaches and implement solutions with guidance from the team
 Deliver assigned project milestones, share progress and findings with teammates and seek guidance when needed
 Experience applying machine learning or AI concepts through research, coursework, projects or internships.
 Use AI to accelerate analysis and iteration while applying judgment and verification to ensure correctness and quality.
 What we are looking for: 
 Working towards a Master's or PhD degree in Computer Science, ML, NLP, Statistics, Information Sciences or related field
 Machine Learning (ranking, computer vision, NLP, content recommendations, embedding, information retrieval etc)
 Experience with big data technologies (e.g., Hadoop/Spark) and scalable realtime systems that process stream data
 Proficiency in at least one systems language (Java, C++, Python) or one ML framework (Tensorflow, Pytorch, MLFlow)
 Experience in research and in solving analytical problems
 Strong communicator and team player with the ability to find solutions for open-ended problems
 In-Office Requirement: 
 This onsite internship will be based in our Dublin office requiring a few days in office. Our program will run in a full-time capacity during typical business hours between Monday-Friday.
 This role will need to be in the office for in-person collaboration 2-3 weekdays per week and therefore needs to be within a commutable distance of Dublin .

We are looking for a Machine Learning Research Intern to join the Doctolib’s Artificial Intelligence teams.
 As a Machine Learning Research Intern, your mission will be to contribute to developing AI solutions that transform access to healthcare and improve the experience of healthcare professionals and patients. You will work within a research team developing ethical AI technologies to optimize care pathways for millions of patients across Europe.
 Working in the tech team at Doctolib involves building innovative products and features to improve the daily lives of care teams and patients. We work in feature teams in an agile environment, while collaborating with product, design, and business teams.
 Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:
 Develop and experiment with machine learning models to solve real-world healthcare challenges
 Collaborate with ML engineers and researchers on applied research projects
 Participate in improving medical practice efficiency through AI
 Explore new model architectures and data processing techniques
 We leverage AI ethically across our products to empower patients and health professionals. Discover our AI vision here and learn about our first AI hackathon here! 
 You can also discover the topic you might work on during your internship here .
 Who you are 
 Before you read on, if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.
 You are a Master's student with practical experience working on ML problems
 You are a strong programmer (we use Python)
 You are enthusiastic about collaborative work
 You are eager to ask questions, admit mistakes, and learn new things
 You are interested in improving healthcare through technology
 You are fluent in English and French
 What we offer 
 A flexible workplace policy offering both hybrid and office-based mode
 Lunch voucher with Swile card
 Work Council subsidy to refund part of sport club membership or creative class
 Reimbursement of public transportation

 A coding game online test
 An interview with our Talent Partner (30 minutes)

 Internship
 Duration: 6 months

 Location: Levallois-Perret
 Working mode: Hybrid - 3 days a week at the office

items.desc:
What You'll Do: 
 In a team, you will be working closely with your mentor to drive your project, design and ensure best practices are applied. You can ask questions and participate in all knowledge sharing sessions/workshops, etc. You are encouraged to actively voice your ideas whilst learning how to build and ship quality code into production which will likely affect millions of users instantly. Identify key problems, devise solutions, build prototypes, and stay current on published state-of-the-art algorithms. Gather and mine large data sets for turning them into understandable and actionable insights to ensure Criteo remains one step ahead of competitive threats. You will develop high-performance algorithms, test and implement the algorithms in scalable, product-ready code.
Projects you could work on: 
 Technical improvements in product recommendation engine and its APIs. 
 Using Machine Learning models to predict the affinity of a user with certain category of products or with a certain brand. 
 Improving the current models we have in production, which might include (amongst others) feature and model engineering, offline evaluation and online testing of the models. 
 Extracting product attributes from information provided by our advertisers. 
 Contribute to the stream of studies around the fairness of AI-driven advertisement (e.g. studying the behavior of our platform, propose and implement fixes, etc.) 
 Who You Are: 
 You are currently in your last year of Bsc/Msc degree in a quantitative field (Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science). 
 Experience with traditional and modern statistical learning techniques and you are proficient at processing data. 
 Implementation experience with high-level languages, such as Python, Scala, Java, C*. 
 Good communication skills in English. 
 We acknowledge that many candidates may not meet every single role requirement listed above. If your experience looks a little different from our requirements but you believe that you can still bring value to the role, we’d love to see your application!​
 Who We Are: 
 We’re Criteo, the Commerce Intelligence Platform. Criteo helps businesses turn shopper signals into commerce outcomes while delivering more relevant experiences for shoppers. We use proprietary commerce intelligence and AI decisioning to drive relevance for shoppers and performance for businesses.
At Criteo, our culture is as unique as it is diverse. From our offices across the globe or from the comfort of home, our 3,600 Criteos collaborate together to build an open, impactful, and forward-thinking environment.
We foster a workplace where everyone is valued, and employment decisions are based solely on skills, qualifications, and business needs—never on non-job-related factors or legally protected characteristics.
 What We Offer: 
 🏢 Ways of working – Our hybrid model blends home with in-office experiences, making space for both.   
 📈 Grow with us – Learning, mentorship & career development programs.   
 💪 Your wellbeing matters – Health benefits, wellness perks & mental health support.   
 🤝 A team that cares – Diverse, inclusive, and globally connected.   
 💸 Fair pay & perks – Attractive salary, with performance-based rewards and family-friendly policies, plus the potential for equity depending on role and level.   
 Additional benefits may vary depending on the country where you work and the nature of your employment with Criteo.

As one of the world’s largest R&D centers, we bring together more than 800 engineers and deliver over 150 inventions annually. Our site serves as the global headquarters for the Large Format Printing and 3D Printing Business Units , driving innovation across software, firmware, and hardware development.

items.desc:
Contexte 
 En robotique, en médecine ou bien dans les flottes de drones autonomes, les systèmes d'IA embarqués évoluent vers des modèles capables d'apprendre après leur déploiement grâce à l’apprentissage continue et fédéré. Le défi est de permettre cette adaptation tout en garantissant que chaque mise à jour reste dans un domaine de fonctionnement sûr (dans une enveloppe de sûreté).
 L’objectif de ce stage est de concevoir et démontrer un framework permettant à une IA d'évoluer en opération tout en garantissant le respect de critères de sûreté, de robustesse et de performance.
 Vos missions 
 Le(a) stagiaire prendra en charge/réalisera une ou plusieurs des missions suivantes :
 Définir une enveloppe de sureté pour des modèles d'IA adaptatifs.
 ·Implémenter une plateforme d’apprentissage fédéré multi-agents.
 Intégrer des mécanismes de d’apprentissage évolutif (incrémental)..
 Développer un contrôleur de sureté pour qualifier ou rejeter les mises à jour des modèles.
 Évaluer la dérive, la robustesse et les stratégies de replis.
 ​
 Votre profil 
 Niveau d’études : Bac + 5, dernière année d’école d’ingénieur électronique ou informatique avec un profil en systèmes embarqués, ou Machine Learning ou numérique,
 Compétences recherchées 
 · Python, PyTorch ou TensorFlow
 · Machine Learning / Deep Learning (étendues)
 · Programmation en C/C++
 · Programmation matlab
 · Intérêt pour l'IA de confiance, l’apprentissage fédéré ou l’apprentissage incrémental.
 · Autonomie, curiosité scientifique et esprit d'innovation
 · Un bon niveau d’anglais est exigé
 Engineer Internship: 
 Safe Adaptive AI: Safety-Bounded Federated & Continual Learning (F/M) 
 Context 
 In robotics, healthcare, and fleets of autonomous drones, embedded AI systems are evolving toward models capable of learning after deployment through continual learning and federated learning. The challenge is to enable this adaptation while ensuring that every model update remains within a safe operating domain (i.e., within a defined safety envelope).
 The objective of this internship is to design and demonstrate a framework that enables an AI system to evolve during operation while ensuring compliance with safety, robustness, and performance requirements.
 Your responsibilities 
 The intern will be responsible for one or more of the following activities:
 · Define a safety envelope for adaptive AI models.
 · Implement a multi-agent federated learning platform.
 · Integrate continual (incremental) learning mechanisms.
 · Develop a safety controller to qualify or reject model updates.
 · Evaluate model drift, robustness, and rollback/recovery strategies.
 Your profile
 Last year of Engineering school (M2) in electronics, embedded systems, digital design, and/or Machine Learning etc.
 Required Skills 
 · Python, PyTorch, or TensorFlow
 · Strong background in Machine Learning / Deep Learning
 · C/C++ programming
 · MATLAB programming
 · Interest in Trustworthy AI, Federated Learning, or Continual Learning
 · Self-motivated, scientifically curious, and innovative mindset

 Vous rejoignez une équipe de recherche dédiée à la conception de solutions de Physical AI et de robotique cognitive , capables de percevoir, raisonner, apprendre, décider et agir dans des environnements complexes. Concevoir des architectures de Physical AI combinant perception multimodale, World Models, modèles Vision-Langage-Action (VLA) et génération d’actions. Développer des solutions robotiques sous ROS 2 , de la communication entre capteurs et modèles d’IA jusqu’aux systèmes de commande et actionneurs. Développer et évaluer des approches d’apprentissage robotique pour la navigation autonome, la manipulation mobile, la locomotion et l’interaction humain-robot. Tester et fiabiliser les solutions développées , analyser leurs performances, documenter les résultats et contribuer à la valorisation des travaux de recherche.

We want this diversity to be reflected among the applicants for our positions, and we encourage all qualified candidates, regardless of background, to apply! Work Tasks SYNAPSE, funded by the Research Council of Norway, develops networks that adapt their decisions to network conditions and the clinical urgency of the information they carry. Learning is integrated into network control to support decisions about scheduling, routing and resource allocation. For example, an urgent clinical alert should reach its destination promptly even when links are congested and patients are moving. The project also develops distributed and federated learning methods that adapt to connectivity, available resources and clinical priorities. Network control and distributed learning are designed together, so that the network supports learning and learning remains effective when communication is constrained. The methods are evaluated in remote patient monitoring and hospital-at-home scenarios. This position focuses on network protocols and their control at the MAC, network, transport and cross-layer levels, combined with machine learning. It does not cover hardware, antennas, circuits or physical-layer signal processing, and is not a general data-science position. Applicants must document relevant computer-networking knowledge and experience. Research areas Learning-based network control, including scheduling, link selection, routing and resource allocation in wireless and edge networks. Reinforcement learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning for distributed network decision-making. Graph and hypergraph representation learning of network state, including temporal graph neural networks. Network- and urgency-aware distributed and federated learning, adapting the exchange of data and model updates to network conditions and clinical priorities. Evaluation through network simulation and emulation, and with real remote patient monitoring data. Responsibilities Lead research on learning-based, urgency-aware network control and distributed learning that adapts to network state and clinical priority. Collaborate with the PhD fellow and master’s students. Publish in leading networking venues and contribute to project management and new proposals. Publications on networking topics and demonstrated experience developing or applying machine-learning methods to networking problems. Experience with network simulation, emulation or testbeds. Preferred Qualifications Experience with multi-agent reinforcement learning, graph learning or federated learning. Experience supervising students or contributing to research proposals. Language Requirements Very good written and spoken English. Personal Qualities Ability to work independently and collaboratively. A structured, precise and adaptable working style. Strong communication and teamwork skills. A positive attitude and ability to manage a dynamic work environment. A high level of professionalism and work ethic. items.desc: The University of Southampton is inviting applications for a postdoctoral position (Research Fellow) in numerical relativity. The successful candidate will undertake research as part of the recently awarded STFC grant Simulating realistic neutron-star mergers. Southampton's School of Mathematical Sciences is home to a large research group in gravitational physics, currently comprising 7 staff members and a number of postdocs and PhD students. Research in the group includes black-hole and neutron-star physics, gravitational-wave source modelling and data analysis, numerical relativity and gravitational self-force modelling. Members of the group are actively involved with the LIGO Scientific Collaboration, the Einstein Telescope Collaboration and the LISA Consortium. The successful applicant will contribute to work aimed at carrying out numerical simulations of neutron star mergers with realistic physics, with particular focus of resistive magnetohydrodynamics. The ideal candidate will have a track record in numerical relativity and ideally some understanding of neutron star modelling, gravitational-wave astronomy and data analysis. Applicants will have, or be about to obtain, a relevant PhD degree in physics or mathematics. This is a fixed term post until 30th September 2027. A complete application should include (i) a CV, including a list of publications, and (ii) a statement of research interests (no more than 1 page). Informal enquiries may be made to Prof. Ian Hawke at I.Hawke@soton.ac.uk.

items.card: The Role We are excited to launch this new opportunity for a Research Associate in Land Systems Science to join us in the School of Natural and Environmental Sciences. You will join the TROPS research lab of Prof Marion Pfeifer, working with her on her new ERC project, TIF-CER, ‘From Forests to Fields to Sustainable Rural Landscapes: A Multiscale Framework for Quantifying Biodiversity and Climate Interrelationships’
items.desc: Salary: £37,369 per annum Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits . We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you. Closing Date: 11 November 2026 The Role We are excited to launch this new opportunity for a Research Associate in Land Systems Science to join us in the School of Natural and Environmental Sciences. You will join the TROPS research lab of Prof Marion Pfeifer, working with her on her new ERC project, TIF-CER, ‘From Forests to Fields to Sustainable Rural Landscapes: A Multiscale Framework for Quantifying Biodiversity and Climate Interrelationships’ , running from January 2027 to December 2031. TIF-CER seeks to understand how the structure and configuration of tree-based agricultural systems (trees in farms - TIFs) influence climate regulation, biodiversity and the delivery of ecosystem services and disservices. The project brings together ecological, environmental and social science approaches to understand these relationships from the scale of individual trees through farms and landscapes to catchments, and across contrasting agroclimatic contexts. In this position, you will work with Marion and international research partners to quantify climate and biodiversity functions and associated ecosystem services and disservices of TIFs, with a particular focus on hydrological processes, water use, flood and drought risks, and their implications at farm and catchment scales. You will contribute to the development and application of mechanistic models, integrate field and spatial data, and work with ecological and biodiversity researchers to understand how these processes change through time. TIF-CER is working with partners in the UK, Italy, Philippines, Tanzania, Chile and Tunisia to: establish an international network of field plots in TIFs and adjacent agricultural land uses and natural forests across contrasting agroclimatic zones; quantify services and disservices associated with TIFs and establish mechanisms underlying their delivery across spatial scales; analyse temporal trajectories of functions, services and disservices using co-designed scenario models of land-use and climate change; and develop tools for end-users using robust evidence for decision-making on tree planting in farms. The position is full-time (1.0 FTE) and involves substantial international travel, particularly during years 1 and 2 of the project. You will contribute to the design and implementation of field campaigns and train research assistants in standardised data collection across different local contexts. You will be expected to co-supervise two PhD students and work with a diverse range of stakeholders to identify values associated with the functions that TIFs provide at different spatial scales. Your particular focus will be on climate functions and associated services and disservices at tree, farm and catchment scales. You will work closely with another Research Associate on the project, whose focus will be on biodiversity functions and connectivity. This is a five-year project with ambitious timelines. We are looking for a candidate who can work across disciplines and spatial scales, combine modelling with field-based research, and contribute to the development of an international research network. What Happens Next Interviews will be held in early November 2026. We are looking to appoint to both Research Associate positions by Spring 2027 at the latest, with the successful candidates expected to start as soon as possible thereafter, subject to the relevant contractual arrangements. We encourage candidates who are interested in the position to contact Prof Marion Pfeifer informally before applying to discuss the role and the TIF-CER project ( marion.pfeifer@newcastle.ac.uk ). items.desc:
Research Fellow in Neuromorphic Local Sensorimotor Intelligence - IT | Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia 
 Research Fellow in Neuromorphic Local Sensorimotor Intelligence 
 Italy 
 Commitment & contract: Research Fellow, 12 months 
 Location: Centre for Robotics and Intelligent Systems, Genova, Italy 
 Step into a world of endless possibilities, together let’s leave something for the future! 
 At IIT, we are committed to advancing human-centered Science and Technology to address the most urgent societal challenges of our era. We foster excellence in both fundamental and applied research, spanning fields such as neuroscience and cognition, humanoid technologies and robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and material sciences, offering a truly interdisciplinary scientific experience. Our approach integrates cutting-edge tools and technology, empowering researchers to push the limits of knowledge and innovation. With us, your curiosity will know no bounds.
 We are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering diversity in all its forms, creating an inclusive environment. We value the unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives of our people. By embracing diversity, we believe science can achieve its fullest potential.
 THE ROLE 
 You will be working in the Event-Driven Perception for Robotics Research unit coordinated by Dr. Chiara Bartolozzi (she/her), a multicultural and multi-disciplinary group, where junior and senior scientists collaborate towards a shared research goal.
 Our research focuses on neuromorphic technologies for developing robots to act swiftly, robustly and efficiently in uncontrolled environment in a wide range of conditions and tasks. This includes real-time event-driven vision, neuromorphic touch perception, and developing end-to-end neuromorphic robots (from perception to decision making, to control) that exploit embodiment. We aim at endowing robots with the ability to continuously infer, predict and adapt to the state of the environment and of the robotic platform itself to plan and execute appropriate actions.
 Within the European funded project “SHIFT” we will endow a snake-like robot with neuromorphic tactile and proprioceptive sensors, and develop spiking neural networks to implement local reflexes and support the estimation of the robot state and action planning. The project will deliver a perfect tool to study embodied intelligence through the systematic study of the synergies between neural computation, robot morphology, sensing and actuation, and the environment.
 We are building a dedicated team with multidisciplinary competences that include neuromorphic sensory encoding, SNN computing and learning for closed-loop sensorimotor systems, and neuromorphic circuit design. The team will leverage the core competences of the EDPR group and closely collaborate with the MESH IIT facility and the projects partners.
 ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS 
 A MSc in computational neuroscience, neuromorphic computing and engineering, computer science, or similar disciplines
 Documented experience in spiking neural networks and/or spike driven learning and/or mixed-mode neuromorphic circuit design
 Good command of spoken and written English
 ADDITIONAL SKILLS 
 Knowledge of programming tools (Python) 
 Ability to work in a challenging and international environment
 Capacity to work autonomously and collaboratively in a highly interdisciplinary environment
 Possess Analytical Reasoning skills and a growth mindset
 COMPENSATION PACKAGE 
 A yearly gross salary ranging between 20k and 25k
 Candidates from abroad or Italian citizens who have carried scientific research activity permanently abroad and meet specific requirements, may be entitled to a deduction from taxable income of up to 90% from 6 to 13 years.
 This position is financed by the Horizon Europe SHIFT project (pending Grant Agreement signature) and is part of the Italian Institute of Technology Brain and Machines flagship.
 Please submit your application using the online form and including a detailed CV, cover letter, and 2 reference letters.
 Application’s deadline: 20 Nov. 2026
 To discover more about life at IIT, visit the dedicated section here: https://www.iit.it/en/work-at-iit

items.desc: About Us: At Booking.com, data drives our decisions. Technology is at our core. And innovation is everywhere. But our company is more than datasets, lines of code or A/B tests. We’re the thrill of the first night in a new place. The excitement of the next morning. The friends you encounter. The journeys you take. The sights you see. And the memories you make. Through our products, partners and people, we make it easier for everyone to experience the world. About the team: Supplier Integrity Product is part of Booking.com’s Supplier Fraud organisation. items.card: Your tasks Contribute to the scientific development of a digital detox app addressing problematic smartphone and social media use and loneliness, in close collaboration with a technical development team and project partners. Develop and adapt evidence-based intervention content, including exercises supporting mindful technology use, behavioural activation and social connection. Specify and evaluate JITAI decision
items.desc: The Central Institute of Mental Health (CIMH) stands for cutting-edge international research and ground-breaking treatment concepts in psychiatry, psychotherapy, child and adolescent psychiatry, psychosomatics and addiction medicine. The Department of Public Mental Health (led by Professor Ulrich Reininghaus) develops and evaluates new mobile Health (mHealth) interventions, with the goal of translating evidence from epidemiology into mental health service innovations. The position is based in the Research Group Precision Digital Mental Health, led by Dr. Christian Rauschenberg , within the Department of Public Mental Health. Within the SENSED-MH and EMERGE-MH projects of the German Center for Mental Health (DZPG), we investigate mental health in everyday life and develop personalized digital interventions. SENSED-MH combines Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), mobile sensing and clinical assessments to examine how everyday experiences and behaviour relate to mental health. EMERGE-MH builds on this research by translating these approaches into adaptive interventions. A particular focus of this position is the development and evaluation of a digital detox app that supports healthier smartphone and social media use and addresses loneliness. The app will use Just-in-Time Adaptive Intervention (JITAI) principles to tailor the timing and content of support to users’ individual needs, current experiences and everyday contexts. We will also explore the potential use of an LLM-based chatbot to provide personalized conversational support. The Research Group Precision Digital Mental Health is looking for a motivated research associate (m/f/d) to join our team from 1 January 2027 . This part-time position ( 37.5% FTE ) will be offered on a fixed-term contract until 31 May 2028. Your tasks Contribute to the scientific development of a digital detox app addressing problematic smartphone and social media use and loneliness, in close collaboration with a technical development team and project partners. Develop and adapt evidence-based intervention content, including exercises supporting mindful technology use, behavioural activation and social connection. Specify and evaluate JITAI decision rules that adapt intervention timing and content to users’ needs and contexts, drawing on EMA and mobile sensing data. Explore the potential integration of an LLM-based chatbot, including the design of conversational content and the evaluation of its usability, acceptability and safety. Contribute to participatory development through interviews, co-design workshops and usability tests with members of the target population and people with lived experience. Support the coordination and implementation of the feasibility study, including participant communication, study procedures and monitoring of engagement and data quality. Prepare and analyse EMA, mobile sensing and intervention data from SENSED-MH and EMERGE-MH. Present findings from research projects at scientific conferences and publish papers in international peer-reviewed journals. Our expectations An excellent Master’s degree in psychology, public health, epidemiology, mental health services research or a related field of the social or health/life sciences. A strong interest in digital mental health, behaviour change, problematic smartphone and social media use, and loneliness. Experience with quantitative research methods and statistical data analysis, ideally using Stata, R or Python. Experience with EMA, mobile sensing, digital interventions or participatory research is desirable. An interest in adaptive interventions and the ability to translate scientific concepts into practical requirements for app development. Familiarity with conversational AI or LLM-based chatbots is an advantage. Excellent communication skills and ability to work independently and as part of a team. Very good written and spoken English. German language proficiency at CEFR level B2 or above is required. We offer An exciting position at a leading research institute and clinic Collaboration in an excellent international network of experts in the field of experience sampling methodology Internal and external training and career development A workplace in the heart of Mannheim Salary in accordance with the German public sector collective agreement for the federal states (TV-L); Pay group E13. Placement in levels 1-6 depends on personal qualifications. items.desc: TXT Group is an international end-to-end IT provider of software consulting solutions and services, supporting customers in the digital transformation of their products and core business processes. Through its proprietary software portfolio and deep vertical-domain expertise, TXT Group operates across multiple markets, with a growing presence in the aerospace, aviation, defense, industrial, government, and fintech sectors. The parent company, TXT e-solutions S.p.A., has been listed on the STAR segment of Borsa Italiana (TXT.MI) since July 2000. Headquartered in Milan, Italy, TXT Group has offices across Italy, Germany, the United Kingdom, France, Switzerland, and the United States of America. AI-ready Data Products for Manufacturing Data Spaces: TXT e-Tech, a company of the TXT Group, is looking for a candidate for a curricular internship linked to a Master's thesis project. The thesis/internship will focus on the design and prototyping of AI-ready Data Products for Manufacturing Data Spaces within the AeroMES-AI project. The activity will involve the analysis and integration of open-source technologies such as Eclipse Tractus-X and Eclipse Dataspace Connector (EDC), addressing key topics including data quality, metadata management, semantic interoperability, and data provenance. The project will culminate in the development of a Proof of Concept (PoC), in which industrial data originating from systems such as Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platforms are prepared, governed, and securely shared through a Data Space, enabling their consumption by AI-powered services developed by TXT. Key Responsibilities: Analyze and design AI-ready Data Products for Manufacturing Data Spaces. Research, evaluate, and integrate Eclipse Tractus-X and Eclipse Dataspace Connector (EDC) technologies. Develop Java-based Data Space components and supporting services. Define and implement data management concepts, including metadata, semantic models, data quality, and data provenance. Design and develop a Proof of Concept (PoC) enabling the secure publication, sharing, and consumption of industrial data by AI-driven services. Integrate and validate the solution against a real-world use case within the AeroMES-AI project. Education: Master’s Degree in Computer Engineering or Computer Science, preferably with a specialization in Java Backend Development, Cloud & Distributed Systems, and Data Engineering. Soft Skills: Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities, curiosity and a willingness to learn emerging technologies, effective teamwork and communication skills, as well as a proactive, independent, and pragmatic approach to research and prototyping. Full professional proficiency in Italian and a good command of English are required. The curricular internship has a duration of 6 months and includes meal vouchers worth €7 per working day. Hybrid Working Model: 2 days per week on-site in Cologno Monzese and 3 days per week working remotely. This position is open to applicants of all genders, in accordance with Italian Legislative Decree 198/2006. The company is committed to equal opportunities and values diversity in all its forms. #Li-Hybrid

items.desc: About Refine A spreadsheet error in one of the most influential economics papers of the decade helped justify austerity across Europe and the US. Millions lived with the consequences. The error was only found years later, by sheer luck, long after the damage was done. Flawed analysis shapes policy, investment and lending every day, costs billions every year, and mostly goes unnoticed. AI makes it worse: rigorous-looking work is now cheap to produce. Refine exists to catch these errors before anyone acts on them. We're building the infrastructure that verifies high-stakes work; think CI/CD for everything beyond code. It reviews a document like a team of experts, checking the maths, data, logic and argument, in minutes. The best AI review system. Refine 5 beats frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra in over 90% of blind head-to-heads across ten fields, from economics to biology. It emulates expert human judgment, coordinating hundreds of calls to frontier models so none of their blind spots get through. We tune it on documents seeded with the errors frontier models miss. The de facto AI reviewer for economics. Econometrica and the AER run every paper they publish through Refine. It's used at 24 central banks and by researchers at Oxford, MIT, Stanford, Yale and Cambridge; Cambridge, UCLA and NYU provide it to theirs. Beyond academia. 29,000+ reviews sold at 1,000+ institutions, including litigation consultancies, hedge funds and companies bidding on public tenders. Enterprise-grade. ISO 27001 certified, SOC 2 Type 1 (Type 2 in progress). The role We build AI systems that beat frontier models at specific tasks. Refine 5 is one of them. You'll help us design and improve these systems. The job is getting as much as possible out of today's frontier models. What matters A very good mental model of what frontier models can and can't do. The kind you only get from spending a lot of time with them. You should be obsessed with AI, and with what it consistently gets wrong. Excellent intuition for using LLMs, above all inside a system. Not just one clever prompt; how many calls fit together to get the most out of them. You should know the basics (MCP, APIs, tool use), but those are learned fast. Who you are Not necessarily a conventional ML engineer. Credentials don't matter much, and you don't need a theoretical background. You've spent a lot of time experimenting with LLMs and got unusually good at it. Maybe you've built pipelines, harnesses or domain-specific tools. Maybe you've found ways of working with AI that let you do things you couldn't do yourself. You can code well enough to prototype and test your own ideas. You're experimental and inventive. Talent and output beat a conventional background. How to apply Send your CV or LinkedIn, plus something you've built with LLMs and a few lines on why it beats the obvious approach.

items.desc: Senior Research Engineer / Scientist – proteinanalys och SPR Vi söker en senior forskningsingenjör eller scientist till ett konsultuppdrag inom bioprocessutveckling i Uppsala. Uppdraget passar dig som har gedigen laboratorieerfarenhet inom proteininteraktioner och vill driva experimentell metodutveckling i en internationell forskningsmiljö. Om uppdraget Du kommer att arbeta med utveckling av analytiska metoder för att karakterisera monoklonala antikroppar, med särskilt fokus på glykosylering och nanobodies. Arbetet tar vid efter lovande inledande experiment och syftar till att utveckla ett robust analytiskt koncept inom Process Analytical Technology (PAT). Rollen kombinerar praktiskt laboratoriearbete, avancerad bindningsanalys och nära samarbete med forskare och projektintressenter. Du förväntas självständigt driva arbetet framåt, dela kunskap och förankra experiment och slutsatser i ett internationellt, tvärfunktionellt team. Arbetsuppgifter Planera och genomföra experiment inom glykosylering och nanobody-bindning. Utveckla, optimera och felsöka SPR-analyser för karakterisering av bindning, affinitet och kinetik. Utforma experimentella kontroller, koncentrationsserier samt strategier för sensorytor och infångning. Utvärdera om bindare kan särskilja relevanta glykanmönster och bidra till snabbare analys nära processen. Förbereda prover, reagenser, sensorytor och instrumentmetoder. Analysera sensorgram och experimentdata, bedöma datakvalitet och föreslå nästa steg. Dokumentera metoder, resultat, avvikelser och slutsatser på ett strukturerat och spårbart sätt. Presentera framsteg, risker och rekommendationer samt bidra till teknik- och metodval. Kompetens och erfarenhet Vi söker dig som har: Doktorsexamen inom exempelvis biokemi, bioteknik, molekylärbiologi, proteinvetenskap, analytisk kemi eller biofysik. Alternativt masterexamen med omfattande motsvarande forskningserfarenhet på senior nivå. Dokumenterad praktisk erfarenhet av SPR-system, inklusive styr- och utvärderingsprogramvara. Djup förståelse för bindningskinetik, affinitetsanalys, analysutveckling, kontroller, sensorytor och datatolkning. Erfarenhet av att utforma och genomföra utforskande laboratoriestudier där metoden inte är fördefinierad. Förmåga att felsöka bland annat proteiner, bindare, prover, buffertar, ospecifik bindning, regenerering och varierande analysdata. Erfarenhet av nanobodies, antikroppar, glykobiologi, glykosyleringsanalys, lektiner eller glykanspecifika bindare. Erfarenhet inom biofarmaceutisk processutveckling, PAT, analytisk utveckling eller reglerad forskning och utveckling inom life science. Erfarenhet av FIDA eller andra kompletterande metoder för proteinkarakterisering. Erfarenhet av produktutveckling, verifiering/validering, projektledning eller tvärfunktionellt tekniskt ledarskap. Förmåga att självständigt planera experiment, analysera resultat, dokumentera slutsatser och definiera praktiska nästa steg. God vana av samarbete över geografiska och ämnesmässiga gränser. Flytande engelska i tal och skrift samt vana av Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 och strukturerad experimentdokumentation och datalagring. Personliga egenskaper Du är vetenskapligt nyfiken, analytisk och pragmatisk. Du trivs med att testa hypoteser, lära av experiment som inte ger förväntat resultat och anpassa angreppssättet med bibehållen struktur. Rollen kräver självständighet, initiativförmåga, gott vetenskapligt omdöme och tydlig kommunikation. Praktisk information Placering: Uppsala. Omfattning: Heltid, huvudsakligen på plats eftersom arbetet omfattar praktiska laboratorieexperiment. Start: Snarast. Uppdragsperiod: Till och med 30 juni 2027, med möjlighet till förlängning. items.desc: RefinyX AB is building the world’s most efficient critical materials recovery platform for sovereign Western supply chains. We are now looking to hire a Battery Materials Engineer at the Refinyx R&D facility in Västerås, Sweden. The job. You develop battery materials on three fronts: battery-grade iron phosphate, NMC pCAM and LFP CAM, from both recycled and virgin feeds. Spray pyrolysis is at the centre of your work. You set up our lab-scale spray pyrolysis system and run it to produce battery material. With our team lead, you make material at lab and pilot scale, prepare customer samples, and learn scale-up from the team that takes our processes to commercial scale. Together with QC, every material is characterized by XRD, SEM, ICP, BET, TD and PSD. You run the experiments, analyze the results, propose the next DoE together with the team lead and execute it on time. Electrochemical performance evaluation, for example in coin cells, runs with QC and our partners: you specify the test plan for cycle life and rate capability and interpret the results. With our AI partners you build the datasets behind predictive models for battery materials, and you contribute to patents on our processes. You also meet customers. The team lead agrees specifications with clients. You support with data and stay in technical contact through validation. You work directly with three groups. The first is our battery materials team lead, a well-known expert in the field. The second is our in-house QC expert, who developed the analytical methods for this application and built QC at refinery. The third is our industrialization team, the people who built it. Your week. Most of it at Loophouse in Västerås: in the lab and on the pilot line, with QC, and on the data and the next DoE. The rest with customers and partners. Your first year. By three months, our lab scale spray pyrolysis system is set up and running under your lead, the first LFP CAM and precursor samples are produced, characterized, and evaluated with QC and our partners, and the bench scale reactors for iron phosphate and NMC pCAM are running with you as a hands on operator. By six months, spray pyrolysis produces material reproducibly against agreed targets, you take part in commissioning the battery materials pilot line, and samples of battery grade iron phosphate and NMC pCAM go to customers with QC and partner data you have interpreted. By twelve months, you have taken spray pyrolysis from the lab scale setup to a pilot scale setup together with our industrialization team and partners, it produces LFP CAM at pilot scale, and you support the larger sample batches for customers. What you must bring. Three things matter most. First, you have set up a lab scale spray pyrolysis system yourself and run it to produce battery material, and you can show us. Second, you understand the process: precursor solution chemistry, atomization (ultrasonic or nozzle), temperature profile, carrier gas and residence time, and how they control particle size, morphology and phase, including any post treatment such as annealing or carbon coating. Third, you know how the resulting battery material is evaluated: chemical and physical analysis (for example XRD, SEM, ICP, PSD and BET) and electrochemical performance in coin cells (cycle life and rate capability). The evaluation itself is carried out with our internal QC team and partners, so what matters is that you can specify the right tests, read the results critically and link them back to your process parameters. What else you bring. You hold an MSc or PhD in materials science, chemistry, chemical engineering, energy engineering, metallurgy or a related field, with at least two years of hands on battery materials research (graduate research years count). Experience with LFP or other olivine type cathodes, working knowledge of iron phosphate or NMC pCAM, and other synthesis routes such as precipitation, hydrothermal, solid state or spray drying are a strong plus. So are hands on coin cell assembly and testing, EIS, GITT or CV, process simulation, machine learning, and patents or peer reviewed publications. Industrial scale up experience is not required; you learn it here from the people who built a refinery. We expect you to be AI native in how you work, or eager to become so, because this is the company we are building. You work comfortably in English; Swedish is not required. Location. items.desc: What is Anori Tech doing? The world talks about batteries, cells and the energy transition. Almost nobody talks about the Battery Management System (BMS) that makes them work. As battery applications multiply, from robotics and mobility to data centers and grid-scale storage, BMS complexity is exploding. Legacy BMS architectures were never built for this: too rigid to keep up with new requirements, they've turned the BMS into the bottleneck of battery development. We're building something different: a novel software-defined BMS architecture combined with an AI-driven configuration process. It gets battery manufacturers the right BMS for their exact use case within days, regardless of application or cell chemistry. We're building the battery management system platform of tomorrow. Delivered in days, not years. Join us and shape one of the fastest growing markets in the energy sector: The BMS market. Our Motivation At Anori Tech, we believe everything is energy, and progress runs on it. With Anori we actively shape the energy transition: from oil to electric, from low to high efficiency. We need batteries for this transition and almost all batteries need a BMS. We strive for Shenzhen speed and German engineering quality. Our objective: put Europe back on the map in the race for the energy transition and build technical leadership out of Hamburg. About the Role A BMS is only as good as what it knows about the battery. As our Algorithm Engineer, you'll develop the algorithms that tell the Anori BMS what is happening inside the cells: state of charge, state of health and balancing. And you won't stop at the concept: you'll design algorithms, implement them in our embedded Rust firmware and validate them on real hardware. Later on, the role grows into the cloud, where data pipelines and fleet analytics will build on the models you create today. items.desc: JOB DESCRIPTION Position: Data Scientist Location: Utrecht, Netherlands Type: Full-time, Permanent Mode: Hybrid 1 day onsite per week. As Data Scientist (GenAI / Chatbot), you know the secrets of making AI assistants perform at their best. You will work at the intersection of data, engineering, and product thinking, helping to improve the quality and effectiveness of chatbot systems. Rather than building foundation models, your focus will be on understanding chatbot behaviour, identifying weaknesses, and translating insights into meaningful improvements. You help answer a fundamental question: “Why is this chatbot not doing what we expect, and what context or structure does it need?” You will assess current solutions against state-of-the-art approaches and drive innovation across retrieval, generation, reasoning loops, tool calling, and related GenAI capabilities. Your Responsibilities: • Analyse chatbot outputs and identify the improvements with the greatest impact; • Diagnose context gaps and determine what additional information agents require; • Partner with product managers and engineers to define evaluation criteria for agent performance; • Work directly with use-case teams and stakeholders to understand real-world scenarios and translate feedback into improvements; • Improve retrieval mechanisms, data structuring, and onboarding of contextual sources; • Design evaluation frameworks that enable rapid, large-scale experimentation and continuous innovation; • Translate functional requirements into actionable technical improvements.

items.card: About The Role In the Energy Optimization team, we build optimization and machine learning systems that help control when heat pumps run, when batteries charge or discharge, and when it makes sense to export energy to the grid. We are also building new flexibility capabilities by coordinating fleets of homes to support the grid when it matters most. We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join this product
items.desc: Residential heating is one of Europe’s largest sources of CO₂ emissions, while energy prices remain unpredictable for many households. At Aira, we’re on a mission to change that. Founded in 2022 and now employing more than 800 people, we develop and install clean energy solutions—including heat pumps, solar panels, and battery systems—powered by intelligent technology that helps homes operate more efficiently. Our goal is simple: to help households reduce both their carbon footprint and their energy costs. With headquarters in Stockholm, Sweden, a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Poland, and hubs across the UK, Germany, and Italy, Aira is rapidly scaling to bring clean energy technology to 5 million homes by 2034. About The Role In the Energy Optimization team, we build optimization and machine learning systems that help control when heat pumps run, when batteries charge or discharge, and when it makes sense to export energy to the grid. We are also building new flexibility capabilities by coordinating fleets of homes to support the grid when it matters most. We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join this product team. You’ll work on models and systems that turn messy real-world signals into reliable decisions for customers’ homes. This includes building and improving forecasting and optimization models, productionising them, monitoring their performance, and iterating based on real-world outcomes. You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, and other teams to ship customer-facing intelligence that is reliable, understandable, and valuable. We value clear communication, thoughtful collaboration, curiosity, and a pragmatic approach to problem-solving. If you enjoy turning ML models into production systems that create measurable customer impact, we would like to hear from you. What You’ll Be Doing Build and improve ML and optimization models that power customer-facing energy optimization features. Work on time-series forecasting, scheduling, and decision models for heat pumps, batteries, solar, tariffs, weather, and customer behaviour. Productionise and own models end-to-end, including deployment, monitoring, reliability, and iteration based on real-world outcomes. Run experiments on real customer systems, evaluate impact, and turn results into product decisions. Contribute to initiatives from discovery to production impact, helping define success metrics and align with stakeholders. Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences, explaining trade-offs, uncertainty, model behaviour, and what is good enough to ship. What You’ll Bring To The Role Experience building ML, data, or optimization systems that are used in real-world products. Good programming skills in Python and software engineering fundamentals. Experience taking models beyond notebooks, including evaluation, testing, deployment, or monitoring. Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure. Comfort working with real-world data, including ambiguity, imperfect signals, and changing requirements. A pragmatic, product-oriented mindset: you care about measurable customer impact, not model complexity for its own sake. Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate well in cross-functional teams. Bonus points if you have Experience with energy systems, electricity markets, demand response, or flexibility. Experience with constrained optimization, control systems, or physical systems modelling. What is in it for you? Gain hands-on experience in a fast-growing scale-up, with a supportive and inclusive culture, and career advancement opportunities. Collaborate with diverse teams across international markets and launch products globally. Develop and grow personally and professionally in an entrepreneurial-minded environment. Thrive in a dynamic, solution-oriented culture, tackling challenges and driving meaningful solutions that make a positive impact on the world. Influence the company's success, with a visible impact on product development and market growth. Enjoy our brand-new office at Norra Stationsgatan 93 in Stockholm. Conveniently located near public transport, with Sankt Eriksplan and Odenplan stations just a few minutes walk away. At Aira, we champion next-generation energy as well as diversity and inclusion. We firmly believe that a diverse workforce fosters innovation and creativity, enhancing our ability to serve customers and communities effectively. We welcome individuals from all backgrounds, cultures and perspectives to join our team. Our commitment is to uphold equality and inclusivity, fostering a collaborative environment where everyone can thrive and contribute to a better future for our people and the planet.
