items.desc: Introduction Thesis work is an excellent way to get closer to Scania and build relationships for the future. Many of today's employees began their Scania career with their degree project. Background Scania develops advanced powertrain and exhaust aftertreatment systems to achieve high efficiency and low emissions across a wide range of operating conditions. Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) control requires accurate dosing decisions, robust emission prediction and effective use of signals available in the vehicle control system. Objective The objective of this master thesis is to develop and evaluate a methodology for AI-based, closed-loop SCR control. The controller shall use machine learning to determine dosing and support emission control over a representative operating cycle. The work will use measured test data and additional data generated in a Software-in-the-Loop (SiL) environment. Inputs may include engine operating point, load, speed, temperatures, flow conditions and other control-system variables. The AI model will be benchmarked against an existing reference SCR model in SiL using a virtual truck powertrain named VTAB (Virtual Truck and Bus). The project will establish a traceable workflow for data preparation, model training, validation and control integration. It will assess whether a data-driven model can reduce calibration effort and enable adaptable control while maintaining robust dosing and emission performance in a real powertrain. Job Description The assignment includes the following activities: Literature study on SCR control, machine learning and AI-based control methods Collect, structure and quality-assure large volumes of test and SiL data Select relevant control-system signals and define model inputs, outputs and constraints Develop and train an AI model for SCR dosing and emission control Integrate and evaluate the model in a virtual truck powertrain SiL environment Compare performance with an existing reference SCR control model Analyse robustness, accuracy, limitations, calibration effort and implementation potential Document the methodology and present the results in a master thesis report Education/program/focus Machine learning, artificial intelligence, control engineering or applied mathematics. Understanding of mathematical models and physical functions used in control systems Experience in handling, processing and analysing large data sets. We value curiosity, structured problem solving, initiative and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. Research Scientist

 IBM Research in Zurich is expanding its quantum hardware team focused on readout and leakage reset technologies for IBM’s superconducting quantum processors.  Work on quantum processors at the core of IBM’s commercial quantum platforms, used by clients around the world

items.desc: Das AIT Austrian Institute of Technology ist Österreichs größte Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) . Unser Ziel ist es, wissenschaftliche Exzellenz in Innovation mit Wirkung zu verwandeln. Gemeinsam mit unseren Partnerinnen und Partnern entwickeln wir Technologien und Lösungen für eine nachhaltige, resiliente und digitalisierte Zukunft und stärken damit die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und technologische Souveränität Europas. Unsere internationalen Teams verbinden Spitzenforschung mit hoher Umsetzungskompetenz und schaffen messbaren Nutzen für Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft. Unsere Kolleg:innen der Competence Unit Integrated Energy Systems forschen mit Begeisterung an der Gestaltung von effizienten und nachhaltigen Energiesystemen und dem optimalen Marktdesign der Zukunft. Unser Ziel ist es Lösungen zu erarbeiten, die die Energie- und Wärmewende vorantreiben . Konkret forschen wir an Optimierungskonzepten und Szenarien für eine effektive Sektorenkopplung. Dabei ist ein großer Fokus die Integration von erneuerbaren Energien in das Energiesystem. items.desc: Italy Commitment & contract: Research Fellow, 12 months Location: Centre for Robotics and Intelligent Systems, Genova, Italy Step into a world of endless possibilities, together let’s leave something for the future! At IIT, we are committed to advancing human-centered Science and Technology to address the most urgent societal challenges of our era. We foster excellence in both fundamental and applied research, spanning fields such as neuroscience and cognition, humanoid technologies and robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and material sciences, offering a truly interdisciplinary scientific experience. Our approach integrates cutting-edge tools and technology, empowering researchers to push the limits of knowledge and innovation. With us, your curiosity will know no bounds. We are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering diversity in all its forms, creating an inclusive environment. We value the unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives of our people. By embracing diversity, we believe science can achieve its fullest potential. THE ROLE You will be working in the Event-Driven Perception for Robotics Research unit coordinated by Dr. Chiara Bartolozzi (she/her), a multicultural and multi-disciplinary group, where junior and senior scientists collaborate towards a shared research goal. Our research focuses on neuromorphic technologies for developing robots to act swiftly, robustly and efficiently in uncontrolled environment in a wide range of conditions and tasks. This includes real-time event-driven vision, neuromorphic touch perception, and developing end-to-end neuromorphic robots (from perception to decision making, to control) that exploit embodiment. We aim at endowing robots with the ability to continuously infer, predict and adapt to the state of the environment and of the robotic platform itself to plan and execute appropriate actions. Within the European funded project “SHIFT” we will endow a snake-like robot with neuromorphic tactile and proprioceptive sensors, and develop spiking neural networks to implement local reflexes and support the estimation of the robot state and action planning. The project will deliver a perfect tool to study embodied intelligence through the systematic study of the synergies between neural computation, robot morphology, sensing and actuation, and the environment. We are building a dedicated team with multidisciplinary competences that include neuromorphic sensory encoding, SNN computing and learning for closed-loop sensorimotor systems, and neuromorphic circuit design. The team will leverage the core competences of the EDPR group and closely collaborate with the MESH IIT facility and the projects partners. ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS A MSc in computational neuroscience, neuromorphic computing and engineering, computer science, or similar disciplines Documented experience in spiking neural networks and/or spike driven learning and/or mixed-mode neuromorphic circuit design Good command of spoken and written English ADDITIONAL SKILLS Knowledge of programming tools (Python) Ability to work in a challenging and international environment Capacity to work autonomously and collaboratively in a highly interdisciplinary environment Possess Analytical Reasoning skills and a growth mindset COMPENSATION PACKAGE A yearly gross salary ranging between 20k and 25k Candidates from abroad or Italian citizens who have carried scientific research activity permanently abroad and meet specific requirements, may be entitled to a deduction from taxable income of up to 90% from 6 to 13 years. This position is financed by the Horizon Europe SHIFT project (pending Grant Agreement signature) and is part of the Italian Institute of Technology Brain and Machines flagship. Please submit your application using the online form and including a detailed CV, cover letter, and 2 reference letters. Application’s deadline: 20 Nov. 2026 To discover more about life at IIT, visit the dedicated section here: https://www.iit.it/en/work-at-iit

The research group has a strong scientific and technical background in wireless communications, machine learning and artificial intelligence, as well as radio frequency engineering and electronics. It collaborates closely with physician-scientists at the Intervention Centre. The Centre is internationally recognized for its scientific excellence and unique position in the field, promoting interdisciplinary research and development. You will work in a diverse and intellectually stimulating environment that fosters creativity, innovation, and scientific excellence in the development of future ICT-based healthcare solutions. Oslo University Hospital is a workplace with great diversity. We believe this is crucial for solving our tasks in the best possible way. Key information Application deadline: 15.11.2026 Employer: Oslo universitetssykehus HF Town/city: Oslo Title: Researcher Position in AI Native Networking for Healthcare Positions: 1 Full-time/part-time: Full-time Employment type: Contract Percentage of full-time: 100 Webcruiter ID: 5200529751 Start date: 01.01.2027 End date: 31.12.2028 Social sharing : Share on x Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook Share by email About the project SYNAPSE, funded by the Research Council of Norway, develops networks that adapt their decisions to network conditions and the clinical urgency of the information they carry. Learning is integrated into network control to support decisions about scheduling, routing and resource allocation. For example, an urgent clinical alert should reach its destination promptly even when links are congested and patients are moving. The project also develops distributed and federated learning methods that adapt to connectivity, available resources and clinical priorities. Network control and distributed learning are designed together, so that the network supports learning and learning remains effective when communication is constrained. The methods are evaluated in remote patient monitoring and hospital-at-home scenarios. This position focuses on network protocols and their control at the MAC, network, transport and cross-layer levels, combined with machine learning. It does not cover hardware, antennas, circuits or physical-layer signal processing, and is not a general data-science position. Applicants must document relevant computer-networking knowledge and experience. Reinforcement learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning for distributed network decision-making. Graph and hypergraph representation learning of network state, including temporal graph neural networks. Network- and urgency-aware distributed and federated learning, adapting the exchange of data and model updates to network conditions and clinical priorities. Evaluation through network simulation and emulation, and with real remote patient monitoring data. Responsibilities Lead research on learning-based, urgency-aware network control and distributed learning that adapts to network state and clinical priority. Collaborate with the PhD fellow and master’s students. Publish in leading networking venues and contribute to project management and new proposals. Publications on networking topics and demonstrated experience developing or applying machine-learning methods to networking problems. Experience with network simulation, emulation or testbeds. What You'll
items.desc: About CommonAI CIC CommonAI CIC is a non-profit membership organisation, founded on a belief in collaborative engineering for the safe and responsible development of foundational AI technologies. A place where AI startups, enterprises large and small, public sector bodies and academia can share resources and knowledge, to codevelop and grow businesses, fast. We are led by experienced founders, investors and engineers who believe that collaborative engineering drives faster AI innovation and are backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. The Opportunity We are seeking an AI Security Researcher with the mindset of an attacker: someone who enjoys finding out how systems can be broken, misused or circumvented. Our research team works on reducing the complexity of large language models while retaining their performance. You will support our High Assurance programme, which works on the accuracy, explainability and accountability of AI systems used in regulated environments such as financial services. You will track the research that matters to the programme, challenge its technical decisions, and help test whether the simpler, more interpretable models emerging from our frontier research are easier to audit in practice. What You'll Do Track key research and developments relevant to the High Assurance programme, including attacks on AI models, defences against them, and the security of the systems that serve them. Report on what these developments mean for the programme and our Members, through written briefings and presentations. Review the programme's technical decisions and directions from an attacker's point of view, and propose stronger alternatives. Threat-model AI systems used in regulated settings, covering model weights, training data, inference serving, and the tools and agents built on them. Red-team the systems we build, within an agreed scope, and report findings through a clear disclosure process. Help develop interpretability methods for the simpler models produced by our frontier research, and test their limits, for example by trying to hide behaviour the methods should detect. Build internal expertise by sharing what you learn with colleagues and helping answer technical questions from our Members. Requirements Proven experience in security research, offensive security or adversarial machine learning (e.g. red-teaming, penetration testing, vulnerability research, or attacks on ML models). A strong understanding of how modern AI systems work, including how large language models are trained, deployed and served. Familiarity with attacks on AI systems (e.g. jailbreaks, prompt injection, data poisoning, backdoors, model extraction). Strong Python, and the ability to build your own tools and experiments. Excellent written communication: you can turn complex technical findings into clear briefings for technical and non-technical readers. The judgement and confidence to challenge technical decisions constructively. A strong enthusiasm for using LLMs, coding assistants, and agents as core tools in your own software development process. We also value: Experience with interpretability methods (e.g. probing, sparse autoencoders, circuit analysis), or a strong interest in learning them. Experience working on software systems that operate in highly regulated or high-assurance environments (e.g. financial services). An understanding of the latest AI safety research and active involvement in that community. Knowledge of hardware and side-channel security (e.g. timing attacks, risks in shared GPU and inference infrastructure). Familiarity with AI assurance standards and regulation (e.g. ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act). A public track record, such as published research, CVEs, conference talks, bug bounties or CTF results. A PhD in security, machine learning or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Benefits A collaborative and supportive work environment The opportunity to have a high impact in a growing organisation Competitive salary package and pension Professional development opportunities Networking opportunities with influential people from across the tech sector, financial services, and academia A vibrant office environment located a few minutes' walk away from Cambridge train station CommonAI CIC is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace.

items.desc: Job Advert Research Associate Division of Psychological Medicine and Clinical Neurosciences School of Medicine College of Biomedical and Life Sciences We are looking for a postdoctoral Research Associate to join the SYLFAEN-PSY project in the Centre for Neuropsychiatric Genetics and Genomics (CNGG), Cardiff University School of Medicine. Measuring the symptoms of psychosis takes time that research studies and clinics rarely have, so most people with psychotic disorders are only ever partly assessed. SYLFAEN-PSY asks whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can infer those symptoms from data that studies already hold, accurately enough to stand alongside the rating instruments we use today. You can read more in our announcement of the project. In this role, you will: Develop and validate LLM-based methods that extract and infer psychotic symptoms from multimodal research data, from clinical text to cognitive measures, neuroimaging-derived phenotypes and genomic information. Benchmark what those models infer against gold-standard symptom-rating instruments, using deeply characterised cohorts with thousands of individuals and multiple instruments. Work with our industry and healthcare partners to validate the system on external datasets, including NHS Wales records and a research network covering more than six million people. Publish in international journals, present at conferences, and develop your own applications for research funding. Supervise postgraduate research students and work with colleagues across the Schools of Medicine and Computational and Mathematical Sciences. We’d like to hear from you if you: Hold a PhD in a relevant subject (or close to submission) or have equivalent experience from industry. Have a track record in psychiatric or psychometric research. Experience with using LLMs for data analysis, or natural language processing research, will be welcome but it’s not needed for application. This project pairs our mental health research team with AI specialists in the School of Computational and Mathematical Sciences, and we expect both sides to learn from each other. The CNGG brings together clinical, genomic, statistical and bioinformatic expertise to work on psychiatric, neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders. We take career development seriously, and the Centre has a strong record of helping people build expertise in the areas that interest them, secure funding, and advance to the next stage of their professional careers. This post is based at the Hadyn Ellis Building, Cathays campus. items.desc: Das AIT Austrian Institute of Technology ist Österreichs größte Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) . Unser Ziel ist es, wissenschaftliche Exzellenz in Innovation mit Wirkung zu verwandeln. Gemeinsam mit unseren Partnerinnen und Partnern entwickeln wir Technologien und Lösungen für eine nachhaltige, resiliente und digitalisierte Zukunft und stärken damit die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und technologische Souveränität Europas. Unsere internationalen Teams verbinden Spitzenforschung mit hoher Umsetzungskompetenz und schaffen messbaren Nutzen für Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft. Unser Center for Energy sucht weitere Ingenious Partner am Standort Wien (Giefinggasse, 1210) . Im Center for Energy arbeiten wir an Lösungen für das zukünftige Energiesystem. Ein zentrales Element davon ist der Übergang zu einem integrierten Energiesystem, in dem die Energieträger Strom, Gas und Wärme gekoppelt sind damit Synergien genutzt werden können. Unsere Kolleg:innen der Competence Unit Integrated Energy Systems forschen mit Begeisterung an der Gestaltung von effizienten und nachhaltigen Energiesystemen und dem optimalen Marktdesign der Zukunft. Unser Ziel ist es Lösungen zu erarbeiten, die die Energie- und Wärmewende vorantreiben . Konkret forschen wir an Optimierungskonzepten und Szenarien für eine effektive Sektorenkopplung. Dabei ist ein großer Fokus die Integration von erneuerbaren Energien in das Energiesystem. CENTER FOR ENERGY Sie arbeiten an der Erstellung von nationalen und internationalen Szenarien und Entwicklungspfaden, verantworten und gestalten unseren „Best Estimate“ der Energiezukunft, und verbessern somit die Modellierung und Analyse des österreichischen und europäischen Energiesystems. items.desc: ML Engineer – Surrogate Modelling 📍 Location: Hybrid (UK, France, Italy, Spain, Netherlands) 💼 Employment Type: Full-time, Permanent 🎯 Level: Early Career / Mid-Level Company Overview North Sails is the global leader in sailmaking, designing and manufacturing sails for premier racing and cruising applications worldwide, including the America’s Cup, the Ocean Race, and Grand Prix racing circuits. Design and production operations are integrated across international hubs. Program Overview Sail design presents a complex coupled fluid-structural challenge. A flexible sail deforms under aerodynamic loading, causing its operational flying shape to differ significantly from its manufactured geometry. To evaluate high-dimensional design spaces at speed, machine learning surrogate models are being integrated directly into the design pipeline. The primary objective is developing surrogate models capable of rapidly predicting integrated aerodynamic forces, moments, and surface pressure distributions for user-defined flying shapes and operational conditions. Position Summary The Machine Learning Engineer – Surrogate Modelling focuses on constructing, training, and systematically evaluating machine learning models configured to emulate complex aerodynamic physics. Working closely with lead engineers and domain designers, the engineer conducts empirical model diagnostics, benchmark testing, and feature engineering to ensure surrogate accuracy meets stringent engineering design requirements. Key Responsibilities Develop, train, and benchmark machine learning surrogate models utilizing computational aerodynamics datasets. Execute structured experiment suites across model architectures, hyperparameter spaces, and feature representations with rigorous tracking. Construct evaluation frameworks, out-of-sample validation tests, and designer reference benchmarking suites. Investigate model failure modes to isolate underlying causes across data quality artifacts, architectural limits, or physical boundary edge cases. Preprocess and format raw high-dimensional simulation data into robust training data pipelines. Maintain complete documentation of experimental setups, hyperparameter sweeps, and validation results. Engage directly with sail designers to analyze surrogate predictions against domain intuition and high-fidelity baseline data. With a multidisciplinary, collaborative and inclusive approach, the group focuses on a wide array of topics such as upper atmosphere modelling - covering empirical, physics-based, and data assimilation techniques - radio propagation, satellite orbit determination, and HF engineering. Additionally, the group explores fundamental physics problems concerning small-scale ionospheric structures and non-linear radiation belt dynamics. To support a range of ionospheric projects SERENE is looking to welcome an outstanding candidate to work in the field of ionospheric data assimilation modelling. This 2-year post will provide the candidate with the opportunity to fully engage with the research group, with work spanning ionospheric data assimilation modelling, D-region remote sensing, atmosphere-ionosphere coupling, HF radio propagation model development as well as first principles modelling of the coupled ionosphere-thermosphere system. This research opportunity will also allow the successful applicant to further develop their own research ideas and pursue collaborative research both locally and internationally. You will join a group at the forefront of innovation in its field. SERENE’s upper atmosphere models are utilized by over 100 institutions in more than 25 countries around the globe. These models serve a dual purpose: advancing the state of the art in upper atmospheric science research and providing operational support for space weather products and services. Internationally and nationally, the SERENE group is actively engaged in shaping space weather policies and assessing associated risks. This group is committed not just to academic pursuits, but also to practical applications that have real-world impact. Their work informs decision-making processes at various governmental and industrial levels, thereby playing a crucial role in the broader space weather community. Assist in the training and support of other early-career members of SERENE. Main Duties The responsibilities may include some but not all of the responsibilities outlined below. Experience in ionospheric physics and numerical simulation are essential Experience in data assimilation is desirable. Strong analytical capability. Ability to communicate complex information clearly. Ability to assess resource requirements and use resources effectively. Understanding of and ability to contribute to broader management/administration processes. Collaborate on the planning and organizing of research programmes. items.desc: We are looking for an (Senior) ML Engineer to strengthen our Data & Analytics crew.🔧 If you enjoy developing machine learning models and building the pipelines and infrastructure that make them work in production, we would like to hear from you. What is the role about? As an (Senior) ML Engineer at Knowit, you will develop, train and evaluate machine learning models and build the technical foundations needed to deploy and operate them. Your work will cover the model lifecycle, from preparing data and experimenting with approaches to building production pipelines, serving predictions and monitoring performance. You will work closely with data scientists, data engineers, software developers and client teams to connect machine learning with operational systems. This could mean developing a new model or taking an existing experiment and turning it into a reliable, maintainable production service. Many of our cases involve industrial time-series, sensor and telemetry data, with use cases such as detecting anomalies, monitoring equipment condition and predicting failures to support maintenance decisions. The role also covers other domains, for example pricing and demand prediction. Preparing and processing time-series and IoT data, building features, and developing models for predictive analytics and anomaly detection. Training, evaluating and improving models, choosing validation methods and metrics that reflect their intended use. Building automated pipelines for data preparation, training, evaluation and deployment. Implementing batch inference or online serving solutions and integrating predictions with operational systems. Connecting ML workloads with cloud data services on Azure, AWS or both, and with event-driven architectures. Monitoring model performance and data quality, identifying drift, and supporting model updates and retraining. You will help define what a successful solution looks like with the client, considering both model quality and practical requirements such as reliability, latency and business value. You will also have opportunities to share your expertise, develop our ML practices and contribute to offering development and pre-sales together with your colleagues. What do we expect from you? We are looking for an engineer with practical experience in machine learning and a strong software development foundation. You enjoy working with both models and the systems around them and take ownership of how your solutions perform in production. items.desc: Handig om te weten: bewaar deze vacature gemakkelijk via de printknop bovenaan. Na sluiting verdwijnt deze vacature van onze website. Bouw mee aan een compleet vernieuwde forecastingomgeving met machine learning en warmtevoorspellingen gebouwd op smart meter data. Combineer data science en software development in één rol met veel technische diepgang. Werk direct samen met de andere afdelingen binnen de keten en zie hoe jouw forecastingmodellen strategische beslissingen ondersteunen. Waarom kiezen voor Eneco De energietransitie zorgt voor een toenemende behoefte aan nauwkeurige voorspellingen. Voor het warmtebedrijf zijn betrouwbare forecasts essentieel om vraag, aanbod en energievolumes goed op elkaar af te stemmen en risico's van schommelingen in externe factoren te mitigeren. Daarom investeert Eneco in een nieuwe generatie forecastingproducten die met behulp van data science en machine learning steeds nauwkeuriger worden. Als Forecasting & ML Data Scientist werk je niet aan de ondersteuning van day trading of real-time handelsbeslissingen. Jouw focus ligt op het ontwikkelen van forecastoplossingen die helpen bij het plannen, optimaliseren en managen van warmte- en energieportfolio's. Daarmee lever je direct een bijdrage aan een duurzaam en betaalbaar energiesysteem. Je krijgt de kans om forecasting voor een belangrijk deel opnieuw vorm te geven. Van kwartierprognoses en machine learning modellen tot datapipelines en ontwikkelstandaarden: jouw werk vormt de basis voor toekomstige beslissingen binnen de business. Dit ga je doen Als Forecasting & ML Data Scientist werk je aan de volgende fase van forecasting binnen Eneco Warmte. De focus ligt op het ontwikkelen van nieuwe forecastingproducten voor de het warmtebedrijf, waarbij bestaande methodieken worden vernieuwd en verder geautomatiseerd. Je analyseert complexe energie- en warmtedata, ontwikkelt modellen die volumes op basis van granulaire slimme meter data voorspellen en onderzoekt hoe machine learning de kwaliteit van forecasts verder kan verbeteren. Daarbij kijk je niet alleen naar het model zelf, maar ook naar de volledige keten eromheen: databronnen, datapipelines, deployment en monitoring. De nadruk ligt op bouwen. Je werkt daarom op het snijvlak van data science, software engineering en data engineering. Samen met collega's uit de business zorg je ervoor dat forecastingproducten aansluiten op de behoeften van het warmtebedrijf en daadwerkelijk worden gebruikt bij portfolio- en volumesturing. Omdat je dicht op de business werkt, zie je direct welke impact jouw oplossingen hebben. Tegelijkertijd heb je voldoende ruimte om structurele verbeteringen door te voeren en mee te denken over de technische koers van het forecastingplatform. Gaat dit over jou? Je krijgt energie van complexe vraagstukken waarin data, technologie en de praktijk samenkomen. Je hoeft niet alles al te beheersen. Belangrijker is dat je een sterke basis meebrengt en nieuwsgierig bent om je verder te ontwikkelen. Je hebt WO werk- en denkniveau en een stevige basis in data science, machine learning en statistiek. Je hebt ervaring met Python en met het ontwikkelen en verbeteren van voorspellende modellen, bijvoorbeeld voor forecasting of time series. Je kunt werken met grote en granulaire datasets en hebt affiniteit met data engineering en het bouwen van betrouwbare datapipelines. Je vindt het interessant om modellen ook echt in gebruik te brengen en hebt kennis van Git, CI/CD en DevOps. Ervaring met Azure DevOps is welkom, maar geen vereiste. Je werkt graag samen met collega's uit verschillende vakgebieden en kunt een businessvraag vertalen naar een passende data- of forecastingoplossing. Ervaring met energie, warmte of smart meter data is mooi meegenomen, maar geen vereiste. Kennis van bijvoorbeeld demand forecasting, mobiliteit, telecom of supply chain kan net zo relevant zijn. Herken je jezelf niet in ieder punt, maar denk je dat jouw kennis en ervaring goed aansluiten bij deze rol? Dan nodigen we je van harte uit om te solliciteren. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor Het ontwikkelen van forecastingmodellen voor warmte- en energievolumes; Het bouwen van machine learning oplossingen voor voorspellingen op basis van granulaire slimme meter data; Het ontwerpen en ontwikkelen van schaalbare datapipelines en datasets; Het verbeteren van forecastingmethodieken, datakwaliteit en modelprestaties; Het samenwerken met de diverse afdelingen om businessvraagstukken te vertalen naar forecastingoplossingen; Het toepassen van software engineering en DevOps-principes binnen de forecastingomgeving; Het bijdragen aan de verdere ontwikkeling van het forecastingplatform met technologieën zoals Python, Git en Azure DevOps. Dit worden je collega's Je wordt onderdeel van het team Forecasting & Delivery binnen het warmtebedrijf van Eneco. Het team richt zich op het ontwikkelen van forecastingproducten die worden ingezet voor warmte- en energieportfolio's. Waar sommige teams binnen Energy Trade zich richten op …

items.desc: At Bluefors, we’re enabling breakthroughs in quantum technology and scientific research through the world’s leading cryogenic measurement systems and dilution refrigerators. As quantum computers scale up, understanding how the cryogenic environment and control hardware affect qubits becomes ever more important. Our modelling work connects these worlds, from heat flow in a dilution refrigerator to the behaviour of a single qubit. We are looking for a Trainee for Cryogenic and Quantum Modelling to join our Quantum and Measurement Team. In this role, you’ll help develop theoretical and numerical models that link the thermal, mechanical, and quantum aspects of our systems. Your work will support customer projects, research and development, and Bluefors’ scientific publications. This is a 12-month fixed-term trainee position. We’re looking for someone with strong foundations in physics and numerical methods, real depth in at least one of our modelling areas, and the curiosity to learn the others. You’ll work alongside experienced physicists and engineers who will support your development throughout the year. We offer you an interesting, challenging, and responsible position, supported by a highly skilled and growing organization. Our working environment is multicultural and leaves room to grow, so you can use your full potential and keep developing your skills. items.card: The role This is an exciting opportunity to join an active multidisciplinary research team, focussed on optimisation, synthesis and evaluation of PROteolysis TArgeted Chimeras (PROTACs) to induce targeted protein degradation in human platelets and evaluate their functional effect on human platelet function and thrombosis. We are seeking to appoint a talented, ambitious, and self-motivating Postdoctoral Research
items.desc: The role This is an exciting opportunity to join an active multidisciplinary research team, focussed on optimisation, synthesis and evaluation of PROteolysis TArgeted Chimeras (PROTACs) to induce targeted protein degradation in human platelets and evaluate their functional effect on human platelet function and thrombosis. We are seeking to appoint a talented, ambitious, and self-motivating Postdoctoral Research Assistant (PDRA) with a background in Biomedical Sciences (Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Medical Biology, Cell Biology etc) to join the PROTAC research team of Prof Ingeborg Hers (Bristol Medical School). What will you be doing? You will work on a collaborative project within the Hers Group, funded by an external industrial partner, and will investigate the effects of BTK degradation on human platelet signalling, function, and thrombosis. You will compare the ability of a range of BTK degraders, alongside conventional BTK kinase inhibitors, and assess the resulting functional and signalling consequences. Work will involve studies on human platelets, as well as in vivo/ex vivo mouse studies to explore the effect of compounds on thrombosis and haemostasis. The project will provide comparative insight into BTK degradation versus kinase inhibition and its potential impact on platelet function and thrombosis. You should apply if You have: A Biomedical background and a recently (or imminently) awarded PhD in a relevant area. Experience with a wide range of experimental techniques, such as cell culture, western blotting, FACS analysis and confocal microscopy, and are confident to develop new techniques/approaches. Experience in platelet functional analysis and animal work is desirable. Excellent problem-solving abilities and an ability to plan and organise your own workload effectively as well as working in a team environment. Good organisational, interpersonal and communication skills and ability to write and publish scientific papers (commensurate with career stage) are essential. We look forward to receiving applications from motivated, enthusiastic, and curious people with a keen interest in cellular mechanisms, novel approaches and problem solving. Additional information Contract type: Open-ended (with fixed funding until 31/08/2028 Work pattern: Full-time Grade: I Salary: £40,704 - £45,641 per annum School/Unit: Bristol Medical School This advert will close at 23:59 UK on Tuesday 10th November 2026 For informal queries please contact: Prof Ingeborg Hers, Professor of Pharmacology and Cell Signalling via email: i.hers@bris.ac.uk Our strategy and mission We recently launched our strategy to 2030 tying together our mission, vision and values. items.desc: OneRail is a technology company innovating solutions for multi-modal delivery. We have built and continue to develop a delivery orchestration platform that connects shippers to an extensive courier ecosystem to automate, optimize, and control the entire delivery supply chain, from the demand signal to the proof of delivery. Our OmniPoint SaaS platform uses proprietary algorithms and artificial intelligence to power efficient same-day delivery programs for major companies like Lowe’s, Pepsi, American Tire Distributors, and Advance Auto Parts. We’re seeking a dedicated Integration Engineer whose primary focus will be integrating machine learning models into our flagship product. You’ll bridge the gap between data science and production software—implementing, deploying, and maintaining ML-powered features while contributing to back-end services and React-based front-end components. Your work will enable seamless, scalable AI capabilities for end users. Key Responsibilities Work with ML pipeline engineers to deploy and maintain ML models (e.g., PyTorch, scikit-learn) as robust service endpoints. Collaborate with data scientists and product to productionize prototypes, and extend the product to enable ML and AI features. Define and evolve RESTful APIs with OpenAPI/Swagger—ensuring they support low-latency, high-throughput ML inference. Version, document, and maintain API contracts for internal and external consumers. Build microservices (Python—FastAPI/Flask—or Node.js) that encapsulate ML logic, data pre/post-processing, and business rules. Optimize service performance, scalability, and reliability (caching, async processing, batching). Implement and modify React components and pages to expose ML-driven functionality Ensure seamless data flow from back end to front end, handling streaming or polling as needed. Containerize ML services (Docker) and orchestrate deployments Work closely with cross-functional teams (data science, product, QA) to translate ML requirements into production features. Champion code quality, API versioning strategies, and thorough documentation. Requirements 3+ years of professional full-stack development, with a clear track record of integrating ML into production systems. Hands-on experience serving models in production (model serialization, serving frameworks, inference optimizations). Strong TypeScript and Python proficiency Experience with microservices architecture, message brokers (Kafka wtc), and async frameworks Solid React knowledge (hooks, context, state management); Deep understanding of REST principles, OpenAPI/Swagger, and API versioning/Backward-compatibility. Docker and orchestration experience. CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI) and automated testing (unit, integration, e2e). Strong communicator, able to translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders. Excellent problem solver with an eye for scalable system design. Advanced proficiency in English, both written and spoken (B2+). Not sure if you have enough experience to meet the challenge, but still willing to learn and join our team? Send us your application and we will be happy to talk about the possibilities. Think big! Why Join OneRail Poland? Innovation at its Core: Work on industry-leading technology that is shaping the future of logistics. Career Growth: Opportunities for professional development and career advancement. Collaborative Culture: Join a team of talented engineers and industry experts. Exciting Challenges: Solve complex problems and contribute to impactful projects. Flexibility: We offer a flexible hybrid work style and flexible employment types to suit your needs, ensuring a work-life balance that works for you. Competitive Compensation: Attractive salary and benefits package. Office location: Kraków, Poland Work Style: hybrid (2-3 days from the office/week preferred). We are open to a more flexible arrangement for candidates located outside the Krakow area. Salary level: 20 000 – 27 000 PLN/month Take the next step in your career and become a part of OneRail’s exciting journey!

items.card: You will contribute to the development of advanced sonar processing algorithms, mathematical models, and software for our next-generation fiber-optic sensing systems. Working closely with experts from multiple disciplines, you will help develop technologies that operate in some of the world's most challenging environments. items.desc: We are expanding our Underwater Acoustics R&D team with a Acoustic Signal Processing Engineer who is motivated to solve challenging scientific and engineering problems at the intersection of signal processing, applied mathematics, physics, and software engineering. Optics11 is a deep-tech company developing advanced fiber-optic sensing technologies for demanding applications in underwater acoustics, offshore energy, and defense. Our novel fiber-optic technology is redefining underwater security by enabling next-generation sonar solutions to protect critical naval assets and underwater infrastructure. You will contribute to the development of advanced sonar processing algorithms, mathematical models, and software for our next-generation fiber-optic sensing systems. Working closely with experts from multiple disciplines, you will help develop technologies that operate in some of the world's most challenging environments. Previous experience in underwater acoustics, sonar, radar, geophysics or medical imaging is an advantage, but not a dealbreaker. We value strong analytical thinking, curiosity, and the willingness to learn new domains. Key responsibilities: Execute acoustic modelling and signal processing tasks: Implement and improve algorithms and mathematical models for underwater acoustic sensing systems using principles from signal processing, applied mathematics, statistics, physics, and numerical methods. Analyze and interpret experimental data: Process and evaluate fiber-optic datasets from laboratory and field trials to extract insights that support design improvements and validation. Develop and test algorithms: Contribute to the development and testing of algorithms for beamforming, event detection, filtering, and data classification under guidance from senior engineers. Document and communicate progress: Maintain clear, structured documentation of methods, results, and conclusions. Proactively communicate progress, challenges, and proposed solutions to the team. Collaborate across functions: Work closely with software, embedded, and hardware engineers to ensure smooth data flow, model integration, and system testing. Improve team workflows and tools: Identify opportunities to improve data handling, simulation scripts, and processing pipelines, contributing to better team efficiency and clarity. Share knowledge and provide feedback: Contribute to internal discussions by sharing your learnings, simplifying complex findings for others, and offering constructive feedback on shared work. Why Join Us? Join one of Europe’s most promising deep-tech scale-ups. Shape the future of a rapidly growing multidisciplinary R&D organization. Competitive salary and benefits package. Enjoy regular team activities and company events. Fresh team lunches provided3 times/ week. Required Qualifications: MSc degree (or equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Signal Processing, Statistics, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or another quantitative discipline. 1-3 years of experience in research or development, preferably with sensing systems, applied statistics, or wave-related phenomena or a PhD in a relevant discipline. A strong background in physical modelling, underwater acoustics, wave propagation, signal processing, sonar, applied mathematics, or equivalent. Good understanding of several of the following topics: digital signal processing, statistical signal processing, estimation theory, numerical methods, scientific computing Excellent programming skills (e.g. Python, Julia, C++, etc.) with readiness to deepen your programming proficiency. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. You have a can-do mentality with no fear of getting your hands dirty when needed. You have strong verbal and written communication skills in English. You can work independently as well as in a team with well-developed communication skills. Knowledge of AI, machine learning techniques is a plus. Experience with CUDA, PyTorch, TensorFlow skills is a plus. Experience with fiber optic measurement principles and/or interferometry is a plus. Applicants should be eligible for NATO/Dutch security clearance. Security & Compliance: You'll be working with clients in the defense and security sectors, obtaining a Certificate of No Objection issued by the AIVD (Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service) is mandatory. This means you will need to undergo a security screening. For more information, please refer to details on security screening.

items.title: Teamlead AI Engineering - RoboGym (Mensch)
items.card: Aufgaben in echten Umgebungen sehen, hören und erfahren. Genau das ist die Idee hinter NEURA Gym: ein globales Netzwerk physischer Trainingszentren, in denen Roboter industrielle Aufgaben und Fähigkeiten direkt von den Menschen lernen, die diese Prozesse aus dem Effeff kennen. Als Team Lead AI Engineering – RoboGym leitest Du das Team, das dieses Fachwissen in einsatzbereite Roboterfähigkeiten verwandelt. In enger
items.desc: Physical AI kann nicht allein anhand von Internetdaten trainiert werden. Roboter müssen in der realen Welt lernen – indem sie echte Aufgaben in echten Umgebungen sehen, hören und erfahren. Genau das ist die Idee hinter NEURA Gym: ein globales Netzwerk physischer Trainingszentren, in denen Roboter industrielle Aufgaben und Fähigkeiten direkt von den Menschen lernen, die diese Prozesse aus dem Effeff kennen. Als Team Lead AI Engineering – RoboGym leitest Du das Team, das dieses Fachwissen in einsatzbereite Roboterfähigkeiten verwandelt. In enger Zusammenarbeit mit Kunden hilfst Du dabei, Domänenwissen zu erfassen, Datenerfassung und Teleoperation zu steuern und den gesamten Prozess vom Training bis zum Einsatz zu begleiten. Du führst ein Team von AI Engineers und bist die technische Ansprechperson für Partner, die neue Roboteranwendungen zum Leben erwecken. Erfolg in dieser Rolle bedeutet, hands-on technische Führung mit operativer Umsetzung in Einklang zu bringen und sicherzustellen, dass Teleoperation, Datenpipelines, Modelltraining und Deployment als zuverlässiges, skalierbares System zusammenspielen. Diese Rolle passt gut zu jemandem, der gerne reale KI-Systeme baut, eng mit Kunden zusammenarbeitet und seine Arbeit lieber auf physischen Robotern im Einsatz sieht, statt in Forschungsprototypen oder Demos stecken zu bleiben. Deine Mission & Herausforderungen Baue das Team auf, dass das NEURA Gym möglich macht. Stelle ein Team von AI Engineers ein, coache es und führe es – verantwortlich dafür, Partner-Expertise in einsatzbereite Roboterfähigkeiten zu verwandeln. Übernimm die technische Verantwortung für die Beziehung zu NEURA Gym-Partnern. Bewerte neue Use Cases, prüfe die technische Machbarkeit, wähle die passenden Algorithmen aus und definiere effektive Strategien zur Datenerfassung. Sorge dafür, dass die Trainingspipeline durchgängig reibungslos läuft. Überwache den gesamten Prozess von Teleoperation und Training über Simulation bis hin zu Deployment und Validierung und stelle eine nahtlose Ausführung in jeder Phase sicher. Sei da, wenn es darauf ankommt. Arbeite eng mit den Robotics Engineers vor Ort während der Live-Datenerfassung und bei Experimenten zusammen, um sicherzustellen, dass Zielverhalten erfolgreich erfasst wird – bei gleichzeitig hohen Sicherheitsstandards in realen Umgebungen. Biete hands-on technische Unterstützung. Greife ein, wenn das Team auf komplexe Herausforderungen stößt – sei es bei der Überprüfung von Trainingspipelines, der Untersuchung von Datenqualitätsproblemen oder der Reproduktion und Behebung modellbezogener Bugs. Verbinde Teams innerhalb von NEURA. Fungiere als Brücke zwischen NEURA Gym, Cloud und den Core-AI-Teams und stelle sicher, dass Erkenntnisse aus einem Partner-Engagement der gesamten Organisation zugutekommen. Gestalte die Produkt-Roadmap mit. Übersetze Learnings aus realen Deployments in Verbesserungen sowohl für die NEURA Gym-Plattform als auch für NEURAs Kern-KI-Fähigkeiten. Miss, was zählt. Definiere und verantworte zentrale Kennzahlen wie Skill Success Rate, Time-to-Validated-Skill und Dateneffizienz, und nutze sie, um kontinuierliche Verbesserung und Teamleistung voranzutreiben. Worauf wir uns freuen Ein Abschluss in Informatik, Robotik, Elektrotechnik oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet, oder gleichwertige praktische Erfahrung. Fundierte praktische Erfahrung in der Entwicklung von Machine-Learning-Lösungen für Robotik, mit Expertise in mindestens zwei der folgenden Bereiche: Vision-basierte Manipulation Reinforcement- und/oder Imitation Learning Vision-Language-Action (VLA)-Modelle, multimodale Foundation-Modelle oder verwandte Embodied-AI-Ansätze Erfahrung in der Führung von Engineers, Projekten oder technischen Initiativen – sei es durch Personalführung oder formale technische Leitungsverantwortung. Praktische Erfahrung mit Machine-Learning-Frameworks wie PyTorch oder TensorFlow sowie solide Python-Kenntnisse. Erfahrung mit C++ ist von Vorteil. Sicherer Umgang mit physischen Robotersystemen sowie den relevanten Robotik-Software-Stacks und der Middleware. Vertrautheit mit Cloud-Plattformen (AWS, Azure oder GCP) und/oder robotischen Simulationsumgebungen wie Isaac Sim oder MuJoCo ist von Vorteil. Nachweisliche Erfolge bei der Umsetzung komplexer Robotik- oder KI-Projekte von der Konzeption bis zum Einsatz, mit messbarem geschäftlichem oder technischem Impact. Starke Kommunikationsfähigkeiten und die Fähigkeit, zwischen Forschenden, Engineers, Endnutzer:innen/Kunden und weiteren Stakeholdern zu vermitteln. Verhandlungssicheres Englisch; Deutschkenntnisse sind von Vorteil.

items.card: Responsibilities: Analyze and design AI-ready Data Products for Manufacturing Data Spaces. Research, evaluate, and integrate Eclipse Tractus-X and Eclipse Dataspace Connector (EDC) technologies. Develop Java-based Data Space components and supporting services. Define and implement data management concepts, including metadata, semantic models, data quality, and data provenance. Design and develop a Proof of Concept
items.desc: TXT e-Tech , a company of the TXT Group , is looking for a candidate for a curricular internship linked to a Master's thesis project. The thesis/internship will focus on the design and prototyping of AI-ready Data Products for Manufacturing Data Spaces within the AeroMES-AI project. The activity will involve the analysis and integration of open-source technologies such as Eclipse Tractus-X and Eclipse Dataspace Connector (EDC), addressing key topics including data quality, metadata management, semantic interoperability, and data provenance. The project will culminate in the development of a Proof of Concept (PoC), in which industrial data originating from systems such as Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platforms are prepared, governed, and securely shared through a Data Space, enabling their consumption by AI-powered services developed by TXT. Key Responsibilities: Analyze and design AI-ready Data Products for Manufacturing Data Spaces. Research, evaluate, and integrate Eclipse Tractus-X and Eclipse Dataspace Connector (EDC) technologies. Develop Java-based Data Space components and supporting services. Define and implement data management concepts, including metadata, semantic models, data quality, and data provenance. Design and develop a Proof of Concept (PoC) enabling the secure publication, sharing, and consumption of industrial data by AI-driven services. Integrate and validate the solution against a real-world use case within the AeroMES-AI project. Education: Master’s Degree in Computer Engineering or Computer Science, preferably with a specialization in Java Backend Development, Cloud & Distributed Systems, and Data Engineering. Soft Skills: Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities, curiosity and a willingness to learn emerging technologies, effective teamwork and communication skills, as well as a proactive, independent, and pragmatic approach to research and prototyping. Full professional proficiency in Italian and a good command of English are required. The curricular internship has a duration of 6 months and includes meal vouchers worth €7 per working day. Hybrid Working Model : 2 days per week on-site in Cologno Monzese and 3 days per week working remotely. This position is open to applicants of all genders, in accordance with Italian Legislative Decree 198/2006. The company is committed to equal opportunities and values diversity in all its forms.

items.card: You will design and ship the Swift frameworks that turn high-level inference requests into a compact wire protocol, manage long-lived connections, stream multimodal output back to client apps - all under strict process isolation and privacy guarantees. Your code will run on every device that uses Apple Intelligence — and the bar for correctness, performance, and privacy is set accordingly. You will be a key
items.desc:
The Private Cloud Compute (PCC) team builds Apple's privacy-preserving cloud inference platform — the system that lets generative-AI features on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Vision Pro reach into the cloud without compromising user privacy. We are looking for a Software Engineer to join the team that builds the on-device client side of that pipeline: the system frameworks and sandboxed services that every Apple Intelligence and Foundation Models request flows through before it ever leaves the device.
This is system-level Apple platform work. You will design and ship the Swift frameworks that turn high-level inference requests into a compact wire protocol, manage long-lived connections, stream multimodal output back to client apps - all under strict process isolation and privacy guarantees. Your code will run on every device that uses Apple Intelligence — and the bar for correctness, performance, and privacy is set accordingly.
You will be a key contributor to the Swift frameworks and XPC services that connect on-device apps and system daemons to PCC. Day-to-day responsibilities include:
Designing and evolving the on-device client SDKs and the XPC services they sit behind, balancing API ergonomics for client teams with the strict process-isolation and attestation guarantees required by PCC.
Implementing high-throughput, low-latency request paths: protobuf serialization of inference payloads, payload compression, multi-turn session state and lifecycle, retry/cancellation semantics, and streaming of incremental model output back to clients.
Owning concurrency and resource management across async/await, AsyncStream, and GCD — including correct cancellation, back-pressure, and lifetime management of long-lived XPC connections.
Building the telemetry, signposts, and privacy-audited logging that let on-call engineers diagnose request failures across device, cloud, and inference layers without exposing user data.
Collaborating closely with the PCC server-side, Foundation Models, attestation, and platform-frameworks teams; writing design documents, leading reviews, and mentoring engineers on Apple platform fundamentals.
Profiling on real hardware with Instruments and driving down memory, latency, and energy costs in the request path — these libraries run on every device, on every inference, so every microsecond matters.
Experience developing complex, system-level frameworks, daemons, or background services for iOS and macOS (beyond standard UI-focused app development).
Strong programming proficiency in Swift, alongside experience with Objective-C or C/C++ for lower-level system integration.
Deep understanding of concurrency (Swift Concurrency, GCD), memory management, and asynchronous network programming.
Experience designing or evolving wire protocols (e.g., Protocol Buffers), data-streaming pipelines, or connection management.
Hands-on experience with Apple's Inter-Process Communication (XPC) to bridge sandboxed applications and system services.
Familiarity with secure communication protocols, cryptography, or privacy-preserving architectures.
Working knowledge of ML concepts and frameworks and proficiency in performance profiling with Instruments, and experience implementing robust client-side telemetry and logging using native Apple APIs.
Familiarity with end-to-end systems that span device, network, and server tiers, and comfort reasoning about failure modes across that boundary.

items.card: ABOUT THE ROLE - Embed directly within a product team. Work closely with the SMB, Scaler or Enterprise team on focused ML problems tied to clear customer and business outcomes. - Own ML projects end to end. Frame the problem, choose the approach, execute the plan, ship the feature and monitor its performance in production. - Make the build vs. buy decision. Determine when to fine-tune or build a model yourself
items.desc:
ABOUT US

Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom https://www.photoroom.com is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.

We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.

We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.




ROLE SUMMARY

We're looking for a Product ML Engineer to join one of our product experience teams — SMB, Scaler or Enterprise — and own the ML side of short, high-impact projects.

You'll work on focused ML problems with a clear product outcome, sometimes fine-tuning one of our models, sometimes integrating the best externally available model, but always choosing the fastest and most effective path to customer value.

You'll bring the technical depth of an Applied Scientist while operating with the pace and pragmatism of a product engineer. You'll own the journey from framing the problem through to shipping, measuring and iterating on the feature in production.

This is not a research role. Your time horizon is weeks rather than quarters, and success is measured by what reaches users and the impact it creates.



ABOUT THE ROLE

 - Embed directly within a product team. Work closely with the SMB, Scaler or Enterprise team on focused ML problems tied to clear customer and business outcomes.

 - Own ML projects end to end. Frame the problem, choose the approach, execute the plan, ship the feature and monitor its performance in production.

 - Make the build vs. buy decision. Determine when to fine-tune or build a model yourself versus integrating an external model, API or existing library.

 - Move from idea to production quickly. Work on projects scoped in weeks rather than quarters, prioritising rapid iteration and customer impact.

 - Work closely with the ML team. Leverage shared infrastructure, evaluation tooling and expertise while remaining embedded in the product team's priorities and cadence.

 - Stay close to users. Get rapid feedback from customers, monitor how people use what you've shipped and use those insights to drive the next iteration.

 - Balance technical depth with pragmatism. Know when deeper modelling work is necessary and when an existing solution is already good enough to ship.

 - Write production code. Work directly in the product team's codebase rather than operating primarily through research notebooks and experiments.

 - Own quality in production. Build sound evaluations, monitor performance and investigate failures once the feature is live.
   


ABOUT YOU

 - You've shipped ML into production. You have 2+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping ML-powered products, with strong experience in PyTorch or equivalent frameworks such as TensorFlow or JAX.

 - You have applied-science depth. You can fine-tune vision or diffusion models, design meaningful evaluations and debug training runs when necessary.

 - You're a pragmatic builder. You care about solving the customer's problem rather than proving that your own model is the best approach. You'll happily use an external model, API or existing library when that's the fastest route to value.

 - You're product-minded. You measure success through shipped features, user behaviour and business outcomes rather than papers or benchmarks alone.

 - You're comfortable in production codebases. You can move between experimentation and production engineering, writing maintainable code that lives inside a real product.

 - You have strong ownership. You're comfortable taking an ambiguous ML problem, deciding what matters, choosing an approach and driving it through to production.

 - You iterate quickly. You enjoy short feedback loops and would rather ship something useful, learn from users and improve it than spend months optimising something that hasn't reached production.

 - You're curious and collaborative. You can both explain your expertise and learn from the deep technical expertise around you. You value knowledge sharing and humility.

 - You're fluent in English. French isn't required.

Nice to have: experience shipping generative image models or diffusion models into production; experience evaluating third-party AI APIs against internal alternatives; experience working in a fast-growing startup or directly within a product team.



BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary + meaningful equity

 - Hybrid working from our Paris headquarters

 - Visa sponsorship and relocation support up to €10,000

 - MacBook Pro and full home office setup

 - 30 days annual leave

 - Private healthcare

 - Regular company off-sites and team retreats

 Step into a world of endless possibilities, together let’s leave something for the future! 
 At IIT, we are committed to advancing human-centered Science and Technology to address the most urgent societal challenges of our era. We foster excellence in both fundamental and applied research, spanning fields such as neuroscience and cognition, humanoid technologies and robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and material sciences, offering a truly interdisciplinary scientific experience. Our approach integrates cutting-edge tools and technology, empowering researchers to push the limits of knowledge and innovation. With us, your curiosity will know no bounds.
 We are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering diversity in all its forms, creating an inclusive environment. We value the unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives of our people. By embracing diversity, we believe science can achieve its fullest potential.
 THE ROLE 
 The Neurodevelopmental Disorders Research Unit at Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia - IIT (https://www.iit.it/research/lines/neurodevelopmental-disorders), led by Dr. Michael Lombardo, is looking for 2 talented Research Assistants as part of ongoing research understanding multilevel heterogeneity in the autisms.
 The research program aims to identify stratification markers that delineate important distinctions within the population of individuals with autism. The work will require successful candidate to aid other lab personnel (PhD students, Post-docs, PI) in actions relevant to the research program’s aims. The laboratory uses multidisciplinary methods such as observation behavioral methods, neuropsychological testing, eye tracking, EEG, MRI, and fMRI.
 Successful candidates will work with the PI, other lab members, and international collaborators on a variety of research-focused actions focused on identifying important subtypes of patients with ASD. The main tasks are, but not limited to, recruitment of participants for new scientific studies, collection of research data in experiments that include eye tracking, EEG and fMRI methodologies.

 Possession of a Bachelors or Masters in a discipline related to the work we do in the lab (e.g., psychology, psychiatry, neuroscience, cognitive science)
 Good command of both Italian and English languages and good organizational skills
 Prior research experience working with children and/or adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
 ADDITIONAL SKILLS 
 Training or experience on existing neuropsychological and/or clinical assessments such as IQ assessments and/or the ADOS.
 Computational skills (e.g. statistics, coding skills in MATLAB, R, Python)
 High motivation and ability to work both independently and as part of a team
 Knowledge of the field of autism and neurodevelopmental disorders
 Motivation to pursue a career in academic research

items.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Thèse ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel Contexte et atouts du poste This research engineer position is part of the PILOT (Practices and Infrastructure for Long-Term Collaboration) project within the French national research programme PEPR eNSEMBLE (Future of Digital Collaboration). Running from 2023 to 2030, PILOT is coordinated by Claudia-Lavinia Ignat (Inria), Myriam Lewkowicz (Université de Technologie de Troyes), and François Charoy (Université de Lorraine). The project brings together 15 partner institutions and approximately 25 research teams. PILOT aims to design and develop the next generation of collaborative technologies that support sustainable, secure, and interoperable collaboration across organizational boundaries. By combining research in distributed systems, Computer-Supported Cooperative Work (CSCW), Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), and social sciences, the project seeks to develop collaborative infrastructures grounded in actual work practices and organizational needs. A central objective of PILOT is to overcome the limitations of existing collaborative platforms, particularly their dependence on centralized services, limited interoperability, and restricted user control over shared data. The project investigates alternative approaches that enable organizations and individuals to collaborate while preserving their autonomy, privacy, and control over their data and tools. The successful candidate will join the LORELEY research team at the Inria Centre at the University of Lorraine in Nancy. They will work at the intersection of academic research and software engineering, collaborating closely with researchers, PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and engineers from the PILOT consortium. The position offers the opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research on distributed collaborative systems and to transform scientific results into open-source software components, integrated prototypes, and demonstrators. Mission confiée The Research Engineer will contribute primarily to two complementary research axes of PILOT: Axis 2 – Open Technical Frameworks and Protocols for Long-Term Collaboration, which develops new algorithms, protocols, and software components for secure, distributed, and interoperable collaborative systems. Axis 4 – Actionable Guidelines and Demonstrators for Long-Term Collaboration, which aims to translate research outcomes into practical solutions, demonstrators, technical guidelines, and reusable software artifacts supporting future forms of collaboration. The main mission will be to design, implement, integrate, and evaluate research prototypes of distributed and secure collaborative applications, working closely with the PhD students and postdoctoral researchers developing the underlying algorithms and protocols. The Research Engineer will also contribute to transforming these individual research prototypes into more comprehensive demonstrators illustrating how different technologies can be combined to support real-world collaborative scenarios. An important part of the position will involve the development and maintenance of an open-source repository of PILOT software components, prototypes, and demonstrators, together with their technical documentation, deployment instructions, and associated use cases. This repository will contribute to the broader PILOT platform, which brings together research findings, collaborative practices, technical components, and guidelines for long-term collaboration. The position therefore combines hands-on software development, research prototyping, system integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Principales activités The Research Engineer will contribute to the development, integration, and dissemination of technologies supporting secure, interoperable, and long-term collaboration, with a particular focus on Axes 2 and 4 of PILOT. The main responsibilities will include: Development of research prototypes (Axis 2): Work closely with PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and other consortium members to implement and evaluate novel technologies for distributed collaborative systems, including collaborative editing, data synchronization, decentralized architectures, interoperability, and security. Integration and development of demonstrators (Axis 4): Combine research prototypes into functional demonstrators illustrating new forms of long-term collaboration, particularly across organizational boundaries and in application domains studied within PILOT. Development and maintenance of the PILOT technical repository: Organize, document, and maintain open-source software components, prototypes, and demonstrators, ensuring their accessibility, reusability, and sustainability. items.desc: A propos de nous Le Shom, service national d’hydrographie et d’océanographie, fournit la connaissance physique de l’océan. Il mesure et décrit les niveaux de la mer, les courants, les sédiments marins, la houle, la température de la mer, la salinité, les bruits sous-marins, les reliefs, les champs magnétiques… et en prévoit l’évolution. Son expertise, reconnue internationalement, éclaire les décisions des usagers de la mer et des acteurs du monde maritime. Ses produits et services répondent aux besoins des forces armées, garantissent la sécurité des navigateurs, guident les politiques publiques de la mer et du littoral, accompagnent le développement de l’économie bleue et contribuent à la préservation de l’environnement marin. Dans un environnement en constante mutation, le Shom innove et se transforme. Drones maritimes, intelligence artificielle et jumeaux numériques sont appelés à renforcer ses moyens d’acquisition et ses capacités de traitement et de modélisation des données collectées. Établissement public à caractère administratif de premier rang au niveau mondial, le Shom est implanté à Brest (siège social), Saint-Mandé, Toulouse, Papeete et Nouméa. Ses 550 collaborateurs, civils et militaires, allient excellence, rigueur, capacités d’adaptation et esprit d’équipe pour relever, aux côtés de nombreux partenaires, les défis de la connaissance de l’océan. Contexte et description du poste : Le poste est rattaché au laboratoire intelligence artificielle du Shom (Brest), au sein de la Direction de la Recherche, de l’Innovation et des Programmes (DRIP/LAB). Ce laboratoire a pour objectif de bénéficier des ruptures technologiques (comme l’apprentissage machine et profond) pour moderniser / prototyper de nouveaux produits et services. Ce poste est également en interaction forte avec le département Océanographie Régionale, Côtière et Littorale (ORCL) du Shom. Le poste vise à intégrer et évaluer des outils d’élaboration de l’information numérique de l’environnement marin, en particulier pour la lutte sous la mer. Ces outils logiciels ont été développés dans le cadre d’un Projet de Technologie de Défense (PTD FASCINATION) en collaboration de recherche avec l’IMT Atlantique. Conçus pour répondre au concept d’Océanographie Nomade, ils sont basés sur des méthodes d’IA (intelligence artificielle) et ont des degrés de maturité différents : un outil de mapping 2D (4DVARNET) qui permet de faire à partir de données éparses et d’un apprentissage sur une base de connaissances, la reconstruction d’un champ complet ; un outil de compression-décompression de champs scalaires 3D (MLIC++) basé sur une minimisation de la perte d’information métiers (mesurée à l’aune de métriques dédiées) ; un outil d’identification des incertitudes dans un champ donné permettant d’optimiser les actions d’acquisition de nouvelles observations en les concentrant aux endroits les moins bien connus. Mission proposée Les missions du poste sont les suivantes : exploiter les conclusions de précédentes évaluations menées sur 4DVARNET et MLIC++ pour en tirer des axes d’optimisation et d’implémentation logicielle ; poursuivre l’évaluation de ces outils sur des situations métiers proches de ceux ayant servi à leur mise au point mais aussi dans de nouveaux contextes (transfert géographique, données de simulations numériques différentes, champs scalaires différents) pouvant requérir de nouveaux apprentissages / des modifications logicielles ; réaliser des développements compatibles avec les capacités d’expérimentation à des fins opérationnelles, en particulier dans le cadre des systèmes SOAP4 et le DataHub embarqué sur les unités de la Marine. Au sein du service DRIP/LAB, vous serez en charge de : Activités principales : Structurer le pipeline et concevoir l’architecture du banc d’essais logiciels Intégrer les outils logiciels en : Analysant les résultats des travaux (CDD, thèse) précédemment menés au sein du PTD FASCINATION ; Reprenant et optimisant l’existant des méthodes et composants logiciels ; Poursuivre les développements en facilitant si possible une intégration future dans les systèmes opérationnels. Évaluer et garder un regard critique sur les résultats, afin d’identifier des améliorations et évolutions (voire corrections) compte-tenu des exigences des besoins opérationnels ; Participer aux expérimentations en relation avec les équipes de production et les opérationnels, Assurer la veille scientifique du domaine et valoriser scientifiquement les travaux (rédaction de publications, participation à des colloques). Poste à pourvoir à partir du 4 janvier 2027, contrat de projet d'une durée estimée à 24 mois (convention PDT Fascination) Salaire : à partir de 35 800 € brut annuel. Dans le secteur des télécommunications, anticiper les résiliations et comprendre les facteurs associés aux départs des clients constituent des enjeux majeurs pour améliorer la connaissance client et accompagner les stratégies de fidélisation. Au-delà de la performance prédictive des modèles, l’objectif est de mieux comprendre les comportements de résiliation et d'identifier les facteurs qui contribuent aux prédictions des algorithmes. Vous travaillerez sur une problématique concrète de churn, notamment sur une typologie de clients spécifique, en combinant analyse de données, modélisation prédictive et méthodes d’explicabilité. Dans cette optique, vos principales missions seront : Comprendre les problématiques métier et les comportements clients : vous familiariser avec les activités télécoms, les offres, les usages et les parcours clients afin d'appréhender les enjeux et les mécanismes de résiliation étudiés. Explorer et analyser les données : extraire, manipuler et analyser les données clients à l'aide de SQL et d'outils tels que BigQuery, puis réaliser des analyses exploratoires en Python (Pandas, NumPy, etc.) afin d'identifier les tendances et les spécificités des populations étudiées. Développer des modèles de prédiction du churn : mettre en œuvre et comparer différentes approches de Machine Learning, notamment des algorithmes de classification, afin de prédire les risques de résiliation. Étudier l’explicabilité des modèles : explorer et appliquer des méthodes d’interprétabilité telles que la feature importance, SHAP ou d’autres approches d’explicabilité afin de comprendre les contributions des différentes variables aux prédictions. Identifier et analyser les facteurs associés au churn : approfondir l’analyse des résultats des modèles, étudier les interactions entre variables et caractériser les comportements spécifiques de certaines typologies de clients churners. Évaluer et valoriser les résultats : confronter les analyses aux réalités métier, étudier leur robustesse, synthétiser les enseignements et présenter les conclusions aux équipes Data Science et aux interlocuteurs métier. Vous disposez d'une bonne maîtrise de SQL pour l'extraction et la manipulation de données, idéalement dans un environnement BigQuery. Vous possédez de solides connaissances en statistiques et en Machine Learning, notamment sur les principaux algorithmes de classification (régression logistique, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, etc.). Vous comprenez les principes de fonctionnement des algorithmes de Machine Learning, leurs hypothèses, leurs limites et les principales méthodologies d'évaluation des performances. Vous êtes à l'aise avec l'analyse exploratoire de données, la visualisation et l'interprétation de résultats statistiques. Des connaissances en méthodes d'explicabilité des modèles (SHAP, feature importance, etc.) constituent un plus. Vous faites preuve de curiosité scientifique, de rigueur, d'autonomie et d'un esprit analytique. Vous appréciez le travail en équipe et savez faire preuve d'initiative. Travailler sur des problématiques concrètes de Data Science au cœur des activités d'un grand opérateur télécom, avec des enjeux forts autour de la connaissance client et de la fidélisation. Approfondir votre expertise en Machine Learning et en intelligence artificielle explicable, en expérimentant différentes approches de modélisation et d'interprétabilité. Développer une double compréhension technique et métier, en reliant les résultats des algorithmes aux comportements clients et aux enjeux opérationnels.
