items.card: Your role We are looking for a highly motivated Machine Learning Scientist to help develop world-leading machine learning models for weather and climate and ensure these are built on an efficient, scalable and sustainable software infrastructure. The work requires technical expertise to create state-of-the-art and sustainable machine learning models but also to develop the required underlying software
items.desc: Your role We are looking for a highly motivated Machine Learning Scientist to help develop world-leading machine learning models for weather and climate and ensure these are built on an efficient, scalable and sustainable software infrastructure. The work requires technical expertise to create state-of-the-art and sustainable machine learning models but also to develop the required underlying software infrastructure. It necessitates excellent soft skills to work seamlessly in an international, interdisciplinary, and highly diverse working environment. The role will, in particular, support the scientific and technical development of a machine-learned Earth system model and contribute to Anemoi, the software library for machine learning-based weather forecasting and Earth system modelling developed by ECMWF and its member states. It will also contribute the maintenance of the WeatherGenerator code base that is used in the EarthGenerator project and help increase the HPC efficiency of the model. The position will also support the CLAIMA project, which develops infrastructure for machine learning climate models, and wider developments around the WeatherGenerator. About the Team The position will be located in the Machine Learning Modelling Team in the Earth System Modelling Section of the Research Department. The Machine Learning Modelling Team focuses on the development and application of machine learning for Earth system modelling. This includes developments for ECMWF’s operational Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS), machine learning models to represent Earth system components such as ocean, sea ice and land, and methodological developments such as foundation modelling and generative machine learning. The advertised position will work in very close collaboration with physical modellers and several other teams and sections within ECMWF. It will also have a direct impact on operational weather prediction at ECMWF and the creation of Digital Twins as part of Destination Earth. At ECMWF, you will find a passionate community, collectively aiming to build world-leading global Earth system models for numerical weather prediction. This effort supports ECMWF’s strategy of producing cuttingedge science and world-leading weather predictions and monitoring of the Earth system. About the Project This role is funded through two major European initiatives: Destination Earth (DestinE) and EarthGenerator. Destination Earth, an initiative of the European Commission, is developing Digital Twins of the Earth and a machine-learned Earth system model for weather and climate applications. This includes learned ocean, wave, sea-ice, land surface and hydrology models developed using Europe's largest EuroHPC supercomputers. The WeatherGenerator Horizon Europe project builds a European foundation model for weather and climate. The EarthGenerator Horizon Europe project extends the concept of the WeatherGenerator and explores foundation models for Earth sciences that can be applied to long prediction timescales from multiple years to decades. The CLAIMA Horizon Europe project will compare different machine learning models for use cases in the area of climate modelling. Your responsibilities You will: Contribute to an efficient and sustainable software infrastructure for world-leading machine learning models at ECMWF and the ECMWF Member and Co-operating States Support the evolution of Anemoi while ensuring that the code meets the highest standards and is long-term sustainable Support maintenance and improvements to the WeatherGenerator code base, ensuring its long-term viability Explore new machine learning architectures and capabilities for Earth system modelling for operational weather predictions and Earth system modelling more generally Implement and evaluate new models and training protocols for weather forecasting and Earth system modelling in the context of both AIFS and the WeatherGenerator What we are looking for You will bring: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across interdisciplinary teams (machine learning engineers and scientists, domain scientists, operations) and external partners Ability to work on and contribute effectively to large software projects following modern coding practices, including writing tests and reviewing code Experience with the development and evaluation of machine learning models, including model design, implementation, training, and scaling Experience with the application of machine learning in the wider context of Earth system modelling would be an advantage Experience in designing for and optimizing performance of machine learning tools for training and inference on single GPUs and large HPCs would be an advantage Your profile - Education, experience, knowledge and skills (including language) Advanced university degree (EQ7 level or above) in a physical, mathematical, data/machine learning or environmental science, or …

items.desc: 26.10.2026 Research Associate – Neurosurgery Stream (m/f/d, E 13 TV-L, 80%) Cluster of Excellence “Machine Learning: New Perspectives for Science” Bewerbungsfrist : 11.11.2026 The Cluster of Excellence “Machine Learning: New Perspectives for Science” (EXC 2064) at the University of Tübingen invites applications for a Research Associate – Neurosurgery Stream (m/f/d, E 13 TV-L, 80 %, 32 hours/week, fixed term until 31 October 2031) in the ERC-funded project APORIA, starting on 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The project APORIA (“Augmenting Poiesis: Relational Inquiries in the Age of AI”), led by Dr Maxime Le Calvé and funded by the European Research Council (ERC Starting Grant), studies everyday AI practices in three epistemic communities where making and knowing are deeply embodied yet increasingly digital: neurosurgery, design and anthropology. The project develops a theory of Aporetic Intelligence: how practitioners sustain, lose or cultivate productive puzzlement when AI tools promise to resolve it. It combines multimodal ethnography, microphenomenological interviewing, workshop based research and exhibition-as-research, and co-creates “aporetic field devices”, speculative prototypes and workshop formats that invite practitioners to reflect on their relations to AI. The team works between Tübingen and Berlin, with field sites in both cities. items.desc: The role The successful applicant will join the School of Geographical Sciences, but will work across the University and with cross-disciplinary research institutes such as the Cabot Institute for the Environment, the Elizabeth Blackwell Institute for Health, and Jean Golding Institute for Data Science. We are open to applicants in all areas of climate change and health, but evidence of strong connections and understanding of both the ‘climate change’ and ‘health’ sectors is important. We would welcome applications from candidates with interests in the primary application of data science and AI to research questions in climate change and health. Research interests might include: human health for different climate and adaption scenarios; fine-scale weather/climate hazard modelling relevant for health; different health, data, and AI models that complement and add to our existing ones, for instance related to lifetime exposures or impacts on chronic health outcomes; linked data and digital health; lived experience; different types of methods of assessment for climate and health impacts. What will you be doing? Develop and sustain funding support for their own areas of research. Independently identify relevant research objectives for a research team to pursue and, where appropriate, contribute effectively to faculty research programmes, ensuring that outputs meet the quality and quantity expectations for the School and/or Faculty. Lead research funding bids and research teams. Take a leading role in the successful dissemination, nationally and internationally, of research findings. Develop knowledge of, and contacts with, appropriate funding bodies external to the University. Provide expert advice on research issues to research fellows and other colleagues. Play a leading role in, and/or help to create, networks of researchers active in their area of scholarship and help create opportunities for collaborative work with other research centres. Peer review manuscripts for publication and/or research bids. Participate actively in the development of the School’s research strategy. Make a significant contribution to the School’s research reputation and income. Develop effective activities to achieve engagement with research, and/or impact beyond academia. Where appropriate, develop relations with communities relevant to the research, and public and private enterprises in order to capitalise on intellectual property and collaboration. You should apply if You have extensive academic experience, which includes contributions in research, related leadership and administration. Role holders will be expected to be leading collaborative research bids, research teams or scholastic projects (e.g. editing journals or academic books). You will have an established reputation within your academic discipline and will be producing research of national, if not international, quality. You will be making a significant leadership and/or management contribution within your school or the wider University. You will have completed your PhD and will have demonstrated excellence in scholarship, research, teaching, and administration appropriate to your career stage. The role of Research Fellow in Climate Change and Health is a fixed 3-year Pathway 2 position. We expect the role holder will develop their research including actively seeking opportunities to fund their research beyond the 3 years and publish their research findings, contribute to doctoral supervision, and support the activities of the School in an administrative role. items.desc: Research Associate in Imaging in NMDs Requisition ID: 29880 Location: Newcastle, GB Contract Type: Fixed Term Working Pattern: Full Time Posted Date: 26 Oct 2026 Salary: £37,369 per annum Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you. Closing Date: 09 November 2026 The Role We are delighted to offer an exciting opportunity for a Post Doctoral Research Associate (Evaluator) to our team at the John Walton Muscular Dystrophy Research Centre, Newcastle University, working on a Myositis UK funded project to validate MRI-based diagnostic biomarkers for inclusion body myositis (IBM). You will join an internationally recognised neuromuscular research environment in Newcastle and work closely with Professor Giorgio Tasca, Professor Jordi Diaz-Manera, and collaborating international referral centres contributing anonymised muscle MRI datasets to the study. IBM is the most common acquired myopathy in people over 40 years of age, but diagnosis is often delayed or incorrect because robust diagnostic biomarkers are lacking. This project, “Validation and AI implementation of MRI Diagnostic Criteria for Inclusion Body Myositis: establishing imaging biomarkers to improve diagnostics and trial recruitment”, will provide the first large-scale external multicentre validation of refined MRI diagnostic criteria and compare expert visual assessment with AI-assisted MRI analysis. The postholder will have a central role in the blinded MRI reading phase of the study and will provide expert evaluation of muscle MRI scans collected from international neuromuscular centres. You will apply refined IBM MRI diagnostic criteria, undertake semiquantitative scoring across approximately 40 muscles per scan, and contribute repeat assessments for intra-rater reproducibility analyses, helping to establish structured muscle MRI as a reliable diagnostic biomarker for IBM. We are particularly keen to hear from candidates with expertise in muscle MRI assessment, strong analytical skills, and experience working with complex clinical research datasets in neuromuscular or closely related disorders. The successful candidate will be comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative translational research team, with the ability to interpret imaging data rigorously and communicate findings clearly to academic and clinical audiences. The role will also involve active engagement with national and international collaborators and may support dissemination of findings at scientific meetings. As part of our commitment to career development for research colleagues, the University has developed 3 levels of Research Innovation Role Profiles.pdf. These profiles set out firstly the generic competencies and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and, secondly, the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level. The successful candidate will report to Giorgio Tasca, Clinical Professor of Neuromuscular Sciences. For an informal discussion about the role, please contact him at Giorgio.tasca@newcastle.ac.uk Please submit a CV and covering letter, highlighting your relevant experience in sample preparation and analysis, omics research, experimental workflow development and collaborative, multi-site research. Find out more about the Faculty of Medical Sciences here: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/medical-sciences/ Find out more about our Research Institutes: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/medical-sciences/research/institutes/ This is a fixed term post for 8 months. items.desc: About AMI We are building a new breed of AI systems that (1) understand the real world, (2) have persistent memory, (3) can reason and plan, and (4) are controllable and safe. We are a team of scientists and engineers building frontier world model-based AI. We combine the scientific rigor of a top-tier research institute with focus on engineering excellence and execution. We are a global company, with offices in Paris, Montreal, New York, and Singapore. Come build the future of AI with us! AMI believes AI agents should predict and plan using an internal model of the world — their world model. We’re looking for new team members to advance the state-of-the-art in world modeling. We believe that video is a rich and abundant source of data reflecting how the world works, and that in general models need to be able to process continuous, high-dimensional data from a variety of sensors to: (a) understand context about the current state of the physical world, (b) make predictions about how the world will evolve, possibly as a result of actions taken, and (c) plan and adapt sequences of actions to complete complex tasks, possibly in dynamic, complex environments. You will work with a team on world model research efforts, including: Self-supervised learning methods to efficiently learn from video and other continuous, high-dimensional signals New architectures that efficiently learn to predict world dynamics from video and other high-dimensional signals Scalable algorithms for pre-processing and curating video data Evaluations for benchmarking world model understanding, prediction, and planning Efficient algorithms for model-based planning and reasoning Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science or a related field Proficiency in Python Ability to design, run, and analyze experiments independently Understanding of machine learning fundamentals, large-scale training, and accelerator-based (GPU or TPU) compute environments Preferred Qualifications: Deep expertise in at least one of the following: self-supervised learning, video and multimodal model architectures, planning algorithms Demonstrated record of contributing to advanced research projects via publications and/or major model releases Experience developing evaluation frameworks for world models Experience releasing and maintaining open-source projects Proficiency in a deep learning framework (PyTorch or JAX)

The work requires technical expertise to create state-of-the-art and sustainable machine learning models but also to develop the required underlying software
items.desc: Your role We are looking for a highly motivated Machine Learning Scientist to help develop world-leading machine learning models for weather and climate and ensure these are built on an efficient, scalable and sustainable software infrastructure. The work requires technical expertise to create state-of-the-art and sustainable machine learning models but also to develop the required underlying software infrastructure. It necessitates excellent soft skills to work seamlessly in an international, interdisciplinary, and highly diverse working environment. The role will, in particular, support the scientific and technical development of a machine-learned Earth system model and contribute to Anemoi, the software library for machine learning-based weather forecasting and Earth system modelling developed by ECMWF and its member states. It will also contribute the maintenance of the WeatherGenerator code base that is used in the EarthGenerator project and help increase the HPC efficiency of the model. The position will also support the CLAIMA project, which develops infrastructure for machine learning climate models, and wider developments around the WeatherGenerator. About The Team The position will be located in the Machine Learning Modelling Team in the Earth System Modelling Section of the Research Department. The Machine Learning Modelling Team focuses on the development and application of machine learning for Earth system modelling. This includes developments for ECMWF’s operational Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS), machine learning models to represent Earth system components such as ocean, sea ice and land, and methodological developments such as foundation modelling and generative machine learning. The advertised position will work in very close collaboration with physical modellers and several other teams and sections within ECMWF. It will also have a direct impact on operational weather prediction at ECMWF and the creation of Digital Twins as part of Destination Earth. At ECMWF, you will find a passionate community, collectively aiming to build world-leading global Earth system models for numerical weather prediction. This effort supports ECMWF’s strategy of producing cutting‐edge science and world-leading weather predictions and monitoring of the Earth system. About The Project This role is funded through two major European initiatives: Destination Earth (DestinE) and EarthGenerator. Destination Earth, an initiative of the European Commission, is developing Digital Twins of the Earth and a machine-learned Earth system model for weather and climate applications. This includes learned ocean, wave, sea-ice, land surface and hydrology models developed using Europe's largest EuroHPC supercomputers. The WeatherGenerator Horizon Europe project builds a European foundation model for weather and climate. The EarthGenerator Horizon Europe project extends the concept of the WeatherGenerator and explores foundation models for Earth sciences that can be applied to long prediction timescales from multiple years to decades. The CLAIMA Horizon Europe project will compare different machine learning models for use cases in the area of climate modelling. Your Responsibilities You will: Contribute to an efficient and sustainable software infrastructure for world-leading machine learning models at ECMWF and the ECMWF Member and Co-operating States Support the evolution of Anemoi while ensuring that the code meets the highest standards and is long-term sustainable Support maintenance and improvements to the WeatherGenerator code base, ensuring its long-term viability Explore new machine learning architectures and capabilities for Earth system modelling for operational weather predictions and Earth system modelling more generally Implement and evaluate new models and training protocols for weather forecasting and Earth system modelling in the context of both AIFS and the WeatherGenerator What We Are Looking For You will bring: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across interdisciplinary teams (machine learning engineers and scientists, domain scientists, operations) and external partners Ability to work on and contribute effectively to large software projects following modern coding practices, including writing tests and reviewing code Experience with the development and evaluation of machine learning models, including model design, implementation, training, and scaling Experience with the application of machine learning in the wider context of Earth system modelling would be an advantage Experience in designing for and optimizing performance of machine learning tools for training and inference on single GPUs and large HPCs would be an advantage Your profile - Education, experience, knowledge and skills (including language) Advanced university degree (EQ7 level or above) in a physical, mathematical, data/machine learning or environmental science, or …

items.desc: Fetcherr builds responsible AI that transforms market complexity into measurable profit growth. At the core of the company is the Market Model - a proprietary AI-powered model delivering accurate, granular demand predictions with 96% forecast accuracy and real-time decision intelligence for commercial teams. Built on a glass-box architecture, it uses market data - not personal data - with full transparency into logic and outcomes. First deployed in global aviation, the technology is industry-agnostic and scales across volatile markets. Fetcherr delivers a consistent average profit uplift of 7%, with corporate partners including Delta, Virgin Atlantic, WestJet, Viva, and Azul. The Large Market Modeling (LMM) team is the engine underneath Fetcherr's pricing intelligence. We're the ones who actually build and train the models — taking a chaotic world of market signals, customer behavior, and competitive dynamics and turning them into reliable, production-ready demand models. Other teams at Fetcherr work with the models; we're the ones who bring them to life. Think of us as the team that teaches Fetcherr's AI how people buy — so it can always recommend the right price at the right moment. We are seeking a talented and self-driven experienced Data Scientist to help advance our machine learning capabilities.This is a key role for someone passionate about leveraging machine learning to solve complex, real-world problems and deliver measurable business impact. Responsibilities: Develop and implement state-of-the-art econometric and machine learning models for demand forecasting. Conduct research and experimentation to evaluate novel approaches for improving accuracy, robustness, and scalability. Collaborate with cross-functional teams (including product, data engineering, MLOPS and Platform) to deploy ML systems in production. Clearly communicate complex technical findings to non-technical stakeholders, including product leaders and executives. Requirements: 5+ years of hands-on experience in data science and machine learning with a proven record of leveraging modeling into business outcomes. Proficiency in Python and its ML/data stack (e.g., PyTorch or TensorFlow, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn). Expertise in time-series forecasting, ideally Deep Learning based, preferably in demand prediction or related areas. Feature engineering, feature importance testing, explainability based experience. Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Engineering or a relevant field. Solid understanding of ML production workflows (versioning, testing, reproducibility, and deployment). Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Nice to have: Publications in top-tier, peer-reviewed ML/AI venues (e.g. ICLR, ICML, NIPS, etc.) Experience applying ML in domains like finance, trading, revenue management etc. Familiarity with cloud based solutions on GCP platform (e.g., Vertex AI, PubSub, Cloud Run Functions). Strong data visualization and exploratory data analysis skills. Familiarity with code optimization, containerization (e.g., Docker), CI/CD, or cloud-native architectures. Participation in competitive programming or data science challenges (e.g., Kaggle). If you're excited about building impactful AI systems in a high-growth startup environment, and want to help redefine how industries price, forecast, and optimize, we’d love to hear from you.

items.desc: Join the Growth Story at Envitia Envitia operates at the heart of the UK’s most sensitive and high-profile operations. Our approach is entirely mission-focused, enabling customers to see more, decide faster, and act with confidence across complex domains. We deliver situational awareness and information advantage across C5ISR, fusing cyber, geospatial, and kinetic data into an operational picture. This transforms fragmented data into a shared understanding of the battlespace, delivering actionable insight when it matters most. Our solutions are secure-by-design, built from the ground up to protect sensitive information and ensure resilience in contested environments. We simplify complex heterogeneous data sources into a rich picture of fused intelligence, providing a digital backbone that underpins success. We operate as small teams delivering fast value, blending deep technical expertise with agile methods to deliver measurable outcomes. Every engagement focuses on capability, clarity, and confidence for those who protect the nation. A career with Envitia enables you to work with mission driven innovation. The Role Envitia is recruiting for a Data Scientist to join our Security and Intelligence consulting team and will be responsible for designing, developing and delivering advanced analytics and machine learning capabilities within secure government environments. The role focuses on applying data science and AI techniques to operational intelligence challenges, including large-scale data analysis, predictive modelling, pattern recognition, and automated decision support. The successful candidate will work within multi-disciplinary agile teams, collaborating with data engineers, software engineers, mission analysts and operational users to develop and deploy analytics solutions that enable insight and mission advantage. Typical engagements include: Intelligence data exploitation and advanced analytics ML model development and optimisation Natural Language Processing (NLP), data matching and pattern detection Data triage and automated analysis of large datasets Operational decision-support systems Due to the nature of our work, the successful candidate will be required to obtain a high level of security clearance. Once cleared, you will be expected to work on-site at client locations in either London, Cheltenham, or Manchester for approximately 3-4 days per week. Whilst you clearance is going through, you will work on programmes across our wider defence and central government portfolio. Build and maintain scalable data and AI/ML pipelines to support advanced analytics and automated insight generation. Apply a range of data science techniques including machine learning, statistical modelling, deep learning, NLP, graph analytics and time‑series analysis. Prepare, transform and integrate large, multi‑source datasets (e.g. sensor, geospatial and communications data) for analytics and model development. Collaborate closely with data engineers, software engineers and platform teams to deploy solutions into operational systems. Strong knowledge of modern data science and machine learning techniques, including supervised and unsupervised learning. Data visualisation skills and experience communicating insights through analytical tools and dashboards. items.desc: Research Software Engineer – Environment & Sustainability for the Research Software Sustainability programme (2-year contract) The Netherlands eScience Center is looking for a Research Software Engineer (RSE) to join our dynamic team and collaborate on exciting research projects within the context of the Research Software Sustainability Programme. Join us in harnessing the power of technology to drive innovative research forward. Supported by the Open Science NL Infrastructure programme, which strengthens open science infrastructure in the Netherlands, we are offering a temporary two-year position. The fixed-term contract reflects the project-based nature of the role and its associated funding. The preferred start date is 1 March 2027 or 1 April 2027. If you are driven to continuously improve software and contribute to scientific progress, are creative and communicative, and enjoy tackling complex challenges, this could be the perfect opportunity for you. Who are we? The Netherlands eScience Center is the national center for innovative software solutions in academic research. We aim to bridge the gap in knowledge and expertise between digital technologies on the one hand and scientific and scholarly inquiry on the other. We create tools and digital methodologies that enable researchers across all disciplines to answer research questions, harnessing our unique blend of academic expertise and software development skills. We attach great importance to software quality and sustainability, and academic recognition of research software. We stand for a research-focused, professional, collaborative, open and resourceful approach to everything we do, and we require that our staff can identify with these eScience Center values. Our people have a diverse background in education, gender, nationality, and ethnicity. Together, we form an inclusive group with a common drive. Our Research Software Engineers are distributed into four different sections, Natural Sciences & Engineering, Social Sciences & Humanities, Life Sciences, and Environment & Sustainability, with opportunities to exchange knowledge between the different sections. We always work at the crossroads of digital technologies and academic research with projects ranging from machine learning for climate science to GPU for high-energy physics or linked data for digital humanities. What will you do? This position sits within the Research Software Sustainability Programme (RSSP), which the eScience Center runs on behalf of Open Science NL to improve the sustainability of existing research software. You will be assigned to 2 or 3 projects funded under this programme's 2026 call. The exact tasks vary by project but typically fall into a few categories: software engineering work such as refactoring, modularisation, and improving test coverage and packaging; documentation and training, including writing tutorials and onboarding materials; and community-building activities, such as boosting adoption, extending contributor base, or helping set up governance structures for the project. A typical day may include discussing project progress with researchers and developers, developing and testing software, exploring new computational approaches, improving existing workflows, or contributing to research outputs such as publications, documentation, and open-source software. You will participate in local, national and international events, acting as ambassador of your projects and the tools you contribute to. Who are you? You are motivated to tackle complex research challenges using digital approaches. You enjoy working at the intersection of research and technology and take pride in enabling researchers to answer cutting-edge questions through robust and innovative software solutions. You are curious, proactive, and collaborative, and you communicate effectively with both academic researchers and technical experts. You bring a strong sense of ownership to your work, while remaining flexible and open to learning new tools, domains, and methodologies. You value software quality, sustainability, and reproducibility, and are eager to contribute to an open and inclusive research environment. Furthermore: You hold a master's degree or higher in Earth and Environmental Sciences. You have demonstrated experience in academic research and in development of research software, methodologies, or open-source frameworks for research purposes. You have proven experience in developing research software, including testing, documenting, and applying FAIR principles to research software, and you have an interest in building sustainable software which is adopted by others. You have experience with computational environmental research, including geospatial data, environmental modelling, scientific workflows, and data-intensive analysis. Familiarity with GIS, hydrology, climate and sustainability applications, ecological or agricultural modelling, and the broader Earth-system science ecosystem is …

items.desc: The role The successful applicant will join the School of Geographical Sciences, but will work across the University and with cross-disciplinary research institutes such as the Cabot Institute for the Environment, the Elizabeth Blackwell Institute for Health, and Jean Golding Institute for Data Science. We are open to applicants in all areas of climate change and health, but evidence of strong connections and understanding of both the ‘climate change’ and ‘health’ sectors is important. We would welcome applications from candidates with interests in the primary application of data science and AI to research questions in climate change and health. Research interests might include: human health for different climate and adaption scenarios; fine-scale weather/climate hazard modelling relevant for health; different health, data, and AI models that complement and add to our existing ones, for instance related to lifetime exposures or impacts on chronic health outcomes; linked data and digital health; lived experience; different types of methods of assessment for climate and health impacts. What will you be doing? Develop and sustain funding support for their own areas of research. Independently identify relevant research objectives for a research team to pursue and, where appropriate, contribute effectively to faculty research programmes, ensuring that outputs meet the quality and quantity expectations for the School and/or Faculty. Lead research funding bids and research teams. Take a leading role in the successful dissemination, nationally and internationally, of research findings. Develop knowledge of, and contacts with, appropriate funding bodies external to the University. Provide expert advice on research issues to research fellows and other colleagues. Play a leading role in, and/or help to create, networks of researchers active in their area of scholarship and help create opportunities for collaborative work with other research centres. Peer review manuscripts for publication and/or research bids. Participate actively in the development of the School’s research strategy. Make a significant contribution to the School’s research reputation and income. Develop effective activities to achieve engagement with research, and/or impact beyond academia. Where appropriate, develop relations with communities relevant to the research, and public and private enterprises in order to capitalise on intellectual property and collaboration. You should apply if You have extensive academic experience, which includes contributions in research, related leadership and administration. Role holders will be expected to be leading collaborative research bids, research teams or scholastic projects (e.g. editing journals or academic books). You will have an established reputation within your academic discipline and will be producing research of national, if not international, quality. You will be making a significant leadership and/or management contribution within your school or the wider University. You will have completed your PhD and will have demonstrated excellence in scholarship, research, teaching, and administration appropriate to your career stage. The role of Research Fellow in Climate Change and Health is a fixed 3-year Pathway 2 position. We expect the role holder will develop their research including actively seeking opportunities to fund their research beyond the 3 years and publish their research findings, contribute to doctoral supervision, and support the activities of the School in an administrative role. Additional information Contract type: Fixed term for three years Work pattern: 1 FTE Grade: K Salary: £52,788 - £59,390 per annum School/Unit: School of Geographical Sciences Shift pattern: Monday - Friday This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on 23/11/2026 For informal queries please contact: Name: Professor Dann Mitchell, Professor of Climate Science Address: School of Geographical Sciences, University Road E-mail: d.m.mitchell@bristol.ac.uk Name: Dr Eunice Lo, Senior Research Fellow in Climate and Health Address: School of Geographical Sciences, 12 Berkeley Square E-mail: eunice.lo@bristol.ac.uk Our strategy and mission We recently launched our strategy to 2030 tying together our mission, vision and values. items.desc: Reference: ICCF26II Start date: 17/09/2026 0:00:00 Expiration Date: 05/11/2026 23:59:00 The Flow Cytometry Core Unit at the Spanish National Cancer Research Centre (CNIO) is seeking an outstanding and highly motivated scientist to join our dynamic and innovative Core Facility as Staff Scientist. Working closely with the Head of the Unit, the successful candidate will contribute to the scientific, technical, and strategic development of the facility, ensuring the delivery of high-quality services and expert support to a diverse portfolio of research programmes. The role will involve supporting researchers in the design, execution, and analysis of advanced cytometry experiments, while contributing to the adoption of emerging technologies, development of best practices, and continuous enhancement of the Unit’s capabilities. The successful candidate will also be expected to provide leadership for the Unit in the absence of the Head, ensuring continuity of its scientific and operational activities and contributing to its strategic development CNIO is one of Europe's leading cancer research institutions, dedicated to advancing cancer research through excellence in basic, translational, and clinical science. The Flow Cytometry Core Unit provides expert technical support, scientific consultation, and access to state-of-the-art cytometry technologies for CNIO researchers. The facility is equipped with three high-speed cell sorters, including the latest BD FACSDiscover™ S8, with full spectral and imaging capabilities, as well as four analytical cytometers encompassing both high-parameter conventional and full-spectrum technologies. This advanced platform supports a broad range of applications, including multiparametric phenotyping, high-dimensional analysis, imaging, and sophisticated cell. Selection Criteria A PhD in Immunology, Cancer Biology, Biomedical Sciences, or a related discipline, together with at least four years of relevant postdoctoral research experience, is required. A minimum of five years of hands-on experience in flow cytometry, with extensive expertise in cell sorting and advanced analytical cytometry, including full-spectrum and imaging flow cytometry, is required. Experience in core facility operations, user support and training, method development, and implementation of new cytometry technologies will be highly valued. Demonstrated expertise in high-speed cell sorting and advanced analytical flow cytometry. Experience with instrumentation available in the Unit (Influx, FACSAria, FACSDiscover S8, FACSCanto, LSRFortessa, and Cytek Aurora) is highly desirable. Strong hands-on experience with conventional multiparametric, full-spectrum, imaging, and next-generation cytometry platforms. Proven ability to design and optimize complex flow cytometry panels and advanced cytometry workflows. Expertise in immune monitoring applications, with experience in cancer research environments highly desirable. Advanced knowledge of flow cytometry acquisition and analysis software, including OMIQ, FlowJo, FCS Express, FACSDiva, FACSChorus, and SpectroFlo. Tissue culture and hands-on experience in sample preparation for flow cytometry. Familiarity with computational approaches for high-dimensional cytometry data analysis is desirable. Proficiency in English is an absolute requirement. Fluency of Spanish is no needed but could be an advantage. Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills. Ability to work independently while fostering a collaborative and service-oriented team environment. Previous supervisory, leadership, or facility management experience is highly desirable. The CNIO Offers Incorporation into a Cancer Research Centre of excellence of international relevance. Gross annual salary between €44,091 and €47,481. Social benefits. Flexible compensation (Health insurance, meals, transportation, childcare). Contract linked to a project.

items.desc: Als data scientist bij Trading & Optimization werk je op het snijvlak van energie en AI, op een plek waar je werk direct effect heeft op het energienet. Jouw forecast om 13:00:00 stuurt om 13:00:01 een handelsbeslissing aan, en de impact zie je realtime terug op onze dashboards. Je bouwt niet één geïsoleerd model, maar een samenhangend geheel waarin probabilistische forecasting, optimalisatie en aansturing elkaar versterken. De feedbackloop is kort en meetbaar, wat je vandaag bouwt heeft snel impact. Je werkt in een team waar data scientists, engineers en traders dicht op elkaar zitten. Er is weinig hiërarchie en veel ruimte voor eigen initiatief, maar ook duidelijke verwachtingen over eigenaarschap: jouw modellen draaien live en je bent zelf de eerste die ingrijpt als er iets misgaat. AI-tooling zoals Claude Code is volledig ingeburgerd en versnelt je werk. Zo draagt het team direct bij aan plan Zero: elke MWh die we slimmer verhandelen of efficiënter in een batterij laden of ontladen, is een MWh die niet uit een gascentrale hoeft te komen. Jouw impact bij Zonneplan Jij ontwerpt en bouwt de modellen die onze energiehandel aansturen. Je werkt met meerdere gekoppelde systemen tegelijk: weersvoorspellingen, marktprijzen (day-ahead, intraday, onbalans), klantgedrag en het fysieke gedrag van ons VPP (Virtual Power Plant) van batterijen, laadpalen en zonnepanelen. Je denkt in samenhang en bouwt modellen die elkaar versterken. Jij brengt modellen naar productie en houdt ze scherp. Samen met engineers zorg je voor een vlekkeloze deployment. Je pakt eigenaarschap over je modellen: je monitort performance, waarborgt betrouwbaarheid en optimaliseert continu. Jij vertaalt modelkwaliteit naar commercieel resultaat. Jouw werk verlaagt direct de tradingkosten binnen ons energieportfolio en verhoogt het rendement op de Nexus-thuisbatterij. Door nauwkeurige voorspellingen kunnen we klanten een zonnebonus geven in plaats van een terugleverboete, omdat we weten wanneer hun stroom waardevol is. Jij bereidt onze apparaten voor op een toekomst zonder salderen. Door slim in te spelen op marktontwikkelingen en eigen verbruik zorg je ervoor dat klanten maximaal profiteren. Je vertaalt veranderende marktregels naar concrete modelaanpassingen die direct waarde opleveren voor onze klanten. Jij brengt nieuwe ontwikkelingen naar de praktijk. Je volgt de nieuwste ontwikkelingen in AI en machine learning en vertaalt die proactief naar concrete experimenten. Denk aan nieuwe benaderingen voor probabilistische forecasting. Liever een werkend prototype dan een slide. Dit krijg je van ons Een salaris tussen €4.000 en €6.000 bruto per maand, afhankelijk van je ervaring en senioriteit. 25 vakantiedagen (met de mogelijkheid om er meer bij te kopen) en reiskostenvergoeding. Een Claude Code Max 20x abonnement als secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarde. Je zet het in voor je dagelijkse werk en mag het ook gebruiken voor side projects en persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Een persoonlijk keuzebudget voor sport, boodschappen of iets anders dat bij je past. Vanaf dag één investeren we in jouw groei met de Zonneplan Academy, goede tools en ruimte om te blijven leren. Je kunt doorgroeien naar senior data scientist met specialisatie in energiehandel, batterij-optimalisatie of forecasting. Een pragmatische, no-nonsense werksfeer waarin korte lijnen de norm zijn. Je zit dicht op traders en engineers. Dit neem jij mee Je hebt minimaal 3 jaar ervaring als data scientist en sterke fundamenten in statistiek en machine learning, met aantoonbare ervaring in forecasting of time series. Je schrijft Python op productieniveau en hebt ervaring met het deployen en monitoren van modellen in een live omgeving. Je hebt ervaring met of affiniteit voor AI-ondersteund ontwikkelen, bijvoorbeeld met tools als Claude Code, GitHub Copilot of vergelijkbare AI-assistenten. Je denkt vanuit commerciële impact: je kunt de stap maken van een goed model naar meetbare euro's en onderbouwt je keuzes met data. Je neemt eigenaarschap over wat je bouwt. Jouw modellen draaien live en je bent de eerste die ingrijpt, optimaliseert of bijstuurt wanneer dat nodig is. Je bent nieuwsgierig en proactief: je volgt ontwikkelingen in AI en machine learning op de voet en vertaalt die naar concrete experimenten en kansen. Je spreekt de Nederlandse taal op professioneel niveau. Zo ziet het proces eruit 1. Solliciteer op deze vacature. 2. Telefonisch kennismakingsgesprek met Samer (recruiter). 3. Eerste gesprek met Maarten (direct leidinggevende van de functie) en iemand van het team. 4. Persoonlijkheids- en capaciteitentest, gevolgd door een technische casus met iemand van het team waarin je laat zien hoe je van data naar een forecastingmodel en businessimpact komt. 5. Is er een match? Dan doen we je snel een aanbod. Klaar om jouw modellen in te zetten voor plan Zero? Bij Zonneplan werken we aan één duidelijk doel: een Nederland zonder fossiele energie. Who are we? The Netherlands eScience Center is the national center for innovative software solutions in academic research. We always work at the crossroads of digital technologies and academic research with projects ranging from machine learning for climate science to GPU for high-energy physics or linked data for digital humanities. What will you do? This position sits within the Research Software Sustainability Programme (RSSP), which the eScience Center runs on behalf of Open Science NL to improve the sustainability of existing research software. You will be assigned to 2 or 3 projects funded under this programme's 2026 call. You are motivated to tackle complex research challenges using digital approaches. You enjoy working at the intersection of research and technology and take pride in enabling researchers to answer cutting-edge questions through robust and innovative software solutions. You are curious, proactive, and collaborative, and you communicate effectively with both academic researchers and technical experts. You bring a strong sense of ownership to your work, while remaining flexible and open to learning new tools, domains, and methodologies. You value software quality, sustainability, and reproducibility, and are eager to contribute to an open and inclusive research environment. Furthermore: You hold a master's degree or higher in a relevant field. You have demonstrated experience in academic research and in development of research software, methodologies, or open-source frameworks for research purposes. You have proven experience in developing research software, including testing, documenting, and applying FAIR principles to research software, and you have an interest in building sustainable software which is adopted by others. You have experience with bringing existing research software to a more robust, maintainable and reusable state, for example through refactoring, modularisation, improving scalability, or strengthening software quality. Familiarity with scientific workflows, data processing and analysis pipelines and high-performance computing infrastructure …

items.desc: The role We are seeking a highly motivated and enthusiastic Postdoctoral Research Associate for a Little Princess Trust/Children’s Cancer and Leukaemia Group funded “New Ideas” research project entitled “Using splice-switching oligonucleotides for cancer therapeutics”. The project builds on our recently published work demonstrating the spliceosomal vulnerability of neuroblastoma [Bojko etal, Cancer Letters 2024, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.canlet.2024.217263]. We propose that altering specific mRNA splicing events may selectively kill cancer cells, or sensitize them to chemotherapeutics. The applicant will deploy targeted antisense oligonucleotides to select genes for this purpose. The post will be for up to 12 months (full-time). What will you be doing? This project will require a strong understanding of gene regulation, in particular regulation by post-transcriptional mRNA splicing. You will be expected to show strong initiative and be responsible for the planning, execution, analysis and presentation of the project’s experiments. In addition to molecular/biochemical/cell biology techniques, the project may require expertise in bioinformatic analyses. You should apply if You are highly motivated to impact childhood cancer research. You hold a relevant PhD, or expect to be awarded one very soon. You need to possess high-level molecular/biochemical/cell biology practical skills, including ChIP,RNA immunoprecipitation, co-immunoprecipitation, qPCR, alternative splicing analysis, western-blotting, tissue-culture, confocal microscopy, immunocytochemistry, flow cytometry. You should also have some hands-on experience of bioinformatics for proteomics and transcriptomics Additional information Contract type: Fixed Term Contract - 12 months (Specialist skills) Work pattern: Full time / 35 hours per week Grade: I Salary: £40,704 - £45,641 per annum School/Unit: School of Biochemistry and Biomedical Sciences This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on Monday 16th November 2026 For informal queries please contact: Professor Karim Malik, Professor of Molecular Oncology via email: k.t.a.malik@bristol.ac.uk or tel: +44 (0)117-4550106 Our strategy and mission We recently launched our strategy to 2030 tying together our mission, vision and values. Grégoire, Jérome et Jérémy, ingénieurs d’affaires, vous aideront à atteindre vos objectifs et vos ambitions professionnelles, Intégrer une équipe bienveillante, toujours partante pour un footing ou un jeu de société et partager des moments conviviaux tout au long de l’année, Évoluer au sein de notre agence basée à Saint Herblain, qui valorise la proximité, l’écoute et la collaboration au sein de ses équipes ! items.desc: FALU AG in Rüti (ZH) builds and sells swab production machines that run in plants around the world. With FALU PMAS, our cloud based production monitoring and assistance system, every machine reports its state every five seconds. Customers get live dashboards, shift KPIs, downtime analytics and automatic alerts in the browser. The first customer went live in September 2026 with eight machines, and more plants are lined up. The cloud side of PMAS is built and running in production: broker, ingestion service, databases, web app. The path from the PLC inside the machine to the MQTT broker is covered by one engineer who designed and built it. With more machines and more plants coming, that one person is no longer enough. We are looking for a freelancer who adds capacity on exactly this path: PLC software, Raspberry Pi edge devices, site gateway, broker connection. This is a permanent role that we staff on a freelance basis: no project end date, a long term engagement with about 1 week of work per month, with more when a rollout is on. You will work directly with our existing integration engineer, our inhouse engineering team and the CEO. Tasks You work on everything between the machine PLC and the MQTT broker, alongside the engineer who built the current setup. Which parts you take over completely and which you share depends on your strengths. Concretely: PLC and machine side Bring the PMAS message format into the CB1 machine software (Siemens S7, TIA Portal V18 with HMI) and keep it in sync with the payload contract: cumulative counters, machine status, error codes, timestamps from the PLC clock. Decide and implement how data leaves the PLC: MQTT publishing from the PLC itself, or a read on the edge device (S7 protocol or OPC UA) that publishes on its behalf. Pick one, justify it, standardise it. Manage PLC software versions across the fleet, including safe update and rollback procedures for machines already running at customers. Ensure clock discipline on the PLCs (NTP, local time zone per plant), since every duration KPI is computed from PLC timestamps. Edge devices and site gateway Develop and maintain the software on the Raspberry Pi based edge devices next to each machine: MQTT client, buffering and store and forward during uplink outages, unique client IDs, credential handling, health reporting. Develop and maintain the site gateway: isolated machine network, routing and firewall, outbound only TLS and NTP, remote maintenance access, watchdogs, recovery from a spare device. Help turn the current setup into a provisioning process: golden image, per machine configuration, fleet wide updates without a site visit. A new machine goes from unboxing to "visible in the dashboard" in under an hour. Monitor the edge layer so that we know about a degraded device before the customer does. Broker and data contract Administer the HiveMQ Cloud clusters per customer: credentials, topic ACLs, client ID scheme, certificates. Maintain the payload contract together with the existing integration engineer. Changes are versioned and documented. Commissioning and support Onboard new customers and new machines end to end, remotely where possible and on site where needed (primarily Europe and the United States). Act as second line when "the dashboard shows nothing" or "the numbers look wrong" and the cause sits between PLC and broker. Write the documentation you would have wanted on day one: onboarding sheets, runbooks, wiring notes. Requirements Must have Siemens PLC programming in TIA Portal (SCL and LAD, S7-1200/1500 family). You can open an existing machine project, understand it and change it without breaking the machine. Industrial networking: PROFINET, VLANs, static and DHCP setups, firewalls, TLS basics. You have connected a machine to a network that was not built for it. Linux on Raspberry Pi or comparable single board computers: systemd, networking, images, headless operation, remote administration. Solid programming skills in Python or Node.js for edge software, and Git as a daily tool. MQTT in depth: versions 3.1.1 and 5.0, QoS levels, retained messages, last will, TLS, broker ACLs. Proficiency with AI coding tools is a hard requirement. You use Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or comparable tools every day, you write and maintain project instructions for them, you review their output critically, and you are measurably faster with them than without. Our code and documentation are written with and for these tools. If you see AI tools as optional, this role is not for you. Working proficiency in English (all code, commits and documentation are in English). German is a plus for the machine side. Willingness to travel to customer plants, typically a few days per quarter. Availability of at least two days per week on a permanent basis, with the option to scale up during rollouts. You work as a freelancer (own company or registered self employed) and can invoice FALU AG. Nice to have OPC UA, Snap7 or the Siemens open …

Voor verschillende enterprise-klanten ontwikkelen we geavanceerde datamodellen en algoritmes om waardevolle inzichten uit uiteenlopende datasets te halen. Daarbij maken we gebruik van moderne technologieën en cloudplatformen zoals Azure, maar we zijn platformonafhankelijk en gaan elke technische uitdaging graag aan. Wat al onze projecten gemeen hebben, is dat data een cruciale rol speelt in de besluitvorming en dat de oplossingen daadwerkelijk in productie worden ingezet. Daarom staan datakwaliteit, betrouwbaarheid en een soepele integratie centraal. Daarnaast monitoren we continu de prestaties van onze oplossingen, zodat eventuele problemen tijdig worden gesignaleerd en opgelost. Je werkt aan uiteenlopende projecten in verschillende sectoren. Daardoor krijg je de kans om verschillende businessvraagstukken en databronnen te leren kennen en zowel je technische als domeinkennis verder uit te breiden. Wat ga je doen? Samenwerken met toonaangevende klanten uit verschillende sectoren en complexe businessvraagstukken oplossen. Geavanceerde machine learning-modellen en datagedreven strategieën ontwikkelen die direct bijdragen aan betere besluitvorming. Samenwerken met multidisciplinaire teams om impactvolle oplossingen te realiseren en succesvol te integreren binnen de IT-omgeving van de klant. items.desc: Job Reference 475_26_CS_HPES_RE1 Position Research Engineer - Benchmarking (RE1) Closing Date Friday, 06 November, 2026 Reference: 475_26_CS_HPES_RE1 Job title: Research Engineer - Benchmarking (RE1) About BSC The Barcelona Supercomputing Center - Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS) is the leading supercomputing center in Spain. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over 1000 staff from 60 countries. Look At The BSC Experience BSC-CNS YouTube Channel Let's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences. If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team. Context And Mission The High-Performance Embedded Systems (HPES) Laboratory at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center aims at carrying out research on bringing HPC technologies to systems with some form of criticality, namely safety, mission and security. This includes domains such as automotive, space, avionics, robotics, manufacturing, etc. Our work is mainly done in the context of bilateral projects with several EU companies as well as several European-funded projects. For further details on the HPES Lab, please visit: https://bsc.es/discover-bsc/organisation/scientific-structure/high-performance-embedded-systems BSC is involved in several projects on the design of innovative RISC-V based CPU processor, accelerators, and MPSos. BSC is also carrying out activities related to the performance analysis of the latest commercial computing solutions in the market. As part of the Lenovo Infrastructure Deployment Services (LIDS) team, you will support the validation, benchmarking, and optimisation of large-scale HPC and AI solutions for some of Lenovo's most strategic global customers. In this role, you will execute performance testing, analyse benchmark results, and provide optimisation recommendations across cutting-edge HPC and AI environments, working closely with customers, architects, consultants, and engineering teams. Design and execute benchmarking and performance test plans across compute, storage, networking, GPUs, and AI workloads, then analyze and present results. Profile applications, identify performance bottlenecks, and provide practical optimization recommendations for HPC, AI, and GPU-accelerated environments. Work with industry-standard HPC benchmarks, AI training and inference workloads, MPI-based applications, storage testing tools, and large-scale cluster validation processes. Partner closely with customers, solution architects, technical consultants, delivery teams, and technology partners to support successful solution deployment and operational readiness. Contribute to the development of benchmarking methodologies, best practices, technical documentation, training materials, and knowledge-sharing initiatives that strengthen Lenovo’s global HPC and AI capabilities. What You Will Bring Strong experience with High Performance Computing (HPC) environments, including cluster architectures, Linux administration, job scheduling, and distributed computing. Proven ability to execute, analyse, and optimise HPC benchmarks and performance validation tests across compute, storage, and networking infrastructure. Solid knowledge of parallel computing technologies, including MPI, OpenMP, CUDA, NCCL, and GPU-accelerated applications. Experience benchmarking and tuning scientific, engineering, AI, and data analytics workloads on large-scale HPC platforms. Strong understanding of NVIDIA GPU technologies and architectures, including H100, H200, B200, and GB200/GB300. Hands-on experience with high-performance networking technologies such as InfiniBand and RoCEv2. Expertise with industry-standard benchmark suites including HPL, HPL-MxP, HPCG, IO500, MLPerf, STREAM, FIO, IOR, and NCCL tests. Knowledge of Top500, Green500, customer acceptance testing methodologies, and HPC performance benchmarking best practices. Experience working with HPC storage solutions such as Lustre, GPFS (IBM Storage Scale), BeeGFS, VAST, WEKA, or similar parallel file systems. Strong Linux skills across RHEL, Rocky Linux, and Ubuntu, combined with shell scripting for automation, benchmark execution, and performance analysis. Ability to identify performance bottlenecks, deliver optimisation recommendations, and create customer-facing benchmark reports, technical documentation, and performance studies. Excellent communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work directly with customers, architects, and engineering teams; experience with AI infrastructure benchmarking, LLMs, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Kubernetes, OpenShift, cloud HPC (Azure/AWS/GCP), Python automation, GPU profiling tools, and enterprise AI acceptance testing is highly desirable. items.desc: Fospha is dedicated to building the world's most powerful measurement solution for online retail. For over a decade, we've helped teams make smarter decisions with full-funnel marketing insights, forecasting, and optimisation. With Fospha, every team moves faster and grows smarter. About The Role We're looking for a Data Scientist to join Fospha's Data Science team in London, working within our Stream 3 workstream. Fospha builds marketing measurement products for ecommerce brands — attribution, marketing mix modelling, incrementality testing, and brand impact measurement. Our Data Science team owns the models behind all of it, from methodology through to production code. You will have the chance to work across our technical stack to make real code impacts on codebases. This role suits someone with some commercial data science experience behind them who wants to go deeper. backtesting, production bug fixes, and pipeline work, with decreasing need for step-by-step direction Debug systematically across our codebases — including repositories you're only partly familiar with, using AI tooling to get up to speed quickly Write and review production code — Python and SQL that avoids technical debt, plus reviewing AI-assisted code so it lands with minimal bugs Use our QA automation and cloud tooling effectively — running validation properly and understanding the data science parts of our AWS pipelines Communicate with clients and colleagues — explaining methodology and findings directly, with only minor assistance from senior colleagues Push for clarity up front — working directly with other teams to pin down acceptance criteria and requirements, rather than sitting blocked waiting on them Start becoming an internal data science champion — the person other teams come to on the areas you own What we're looking for Essential Some commercial data science experience — typically 1–2 years, or a strong placement/internship record alongside a quantitative degree Strong Python and SQL, with the ability to collaborate on shared code and avoid technical debt Deep knowledge of a handful of machine learning algorithms — not breadth for its own sake, but real understanding of a few methods and when they apply Able to systematically debug unfamiliar code, using AI tooling to accelerate rather than to guess while still understanding problem fully Strong AI fluency — you understand how to optimally start a task with AI, you use it to unblock cross-team dependencies, and you always QA the output for accuracy and brevity before it goes anywhere Confident completing work independently once scope is agreed Able to communicate with clients and colleagues with only minor assistance Genuine attention to detail — much of this work involves noticing when a number is wrong Nice to have Experience with AWS or comparable cloud tooling Familiarity with automated QA tooling and test coverage practices Any experience with marketing, ecommerce, or advertising data Exposure to Bayesian methods, marketing mix modelling, or experimental design Not required You do not need prior experience with marketing mix modelling, attribution methodology, incrementality testing, or Bayesian modelling. These are taught here, and we'd rather hire someone who learns fast than someone who arrives pre-loaded. How You'll Grow We run a published Data Science Career Development Framework with six levels. You'd join at Developing, where the expectations are: AI Fluency & Tooling: Understands how to optimally start all relevant tasks with AI; confident completing work independently; uses AI to push for acceptance criteria and limit cross-department dependencies; always QAs AI output for accuracy and brevity. Machine Learning & Modelling: Deep knowledge of a handful of algorithms, and familiarity with the full Fospha model suite. Engineering & Codebase: Systematically debugs issues with AI support, even in partly familiar repositories; uses supplied AWS tooling efficiently and understands the data science parts of the pipelines; uses existing QA automation effectively; avoids technical debt and collaborates well on code; reviews AI-assisted code so it ships with minimal bugs. Stakeholder & Communication: Communicates with clients and colleagues with minor assistance. Job Complexity: Undertakes moderately difficult tickets while starting to become an internal data science champion. Supervision: Receives detailed instruction, but becomes progressively less dependent on senior colleagues. items.desc: Software Developer — Build Your Own Project with an AI Coding Assistant About The Role What if you could get paid to work on the project you've been meaning to build — with a state-of-the-art AI coding assistant at your side, completely free of charge? We're looking for software developers in the Stockholm area to bring their own projects and build them using an AI-powered coding assistant. You write real code on real projects you care about. We learn from your expert judgment on how the assistant performed. You keep full ownership of everything you build. This is a fully remote, flexible contract role designed for developers who want to ship their own work — and get compensated for it. Organization: Alignerr Type: Hourly Contract Location: Fully Remote Commitment: Flexible What You'll Do Bring a software project you personally own — a side project, a tool, an open-source library, or something you've been meaning to finish Build features, fix bugs, refactor code, write docs, or do whatever your project needs — using an AI coding assistant At each step, compare two versions of the assistant's response, choose the better one, and write a brief explanation of your reasoning Work in your own environment, on your own schedule, with your own tools Who You Are A developer with a software project you personally own, stored in a git repository Comfortable working in the terminal and with git-based workflows Running macOS, Linux, or Windows with WSL2 Able to write clear, honest evaluations — you'll explain your choices in a few sentences Self-motivated and reliable when working independently Open-source maintainers are especially welcome What's Eligible Software projects that you personally and solely own Open-source projects with an approved license If your project has other maintainers, mention it in your application — we'll confirm eligibility What's Not Eligible Work owned by an employer, client, university, company, or startup Projects under NDA AI model training or evaluation projects; ML infrastructure Security exploit tooling Projects that process other people's personal data Good to Know Before starting, you'll sign short contributor terms and we'll approve your project Transcripts of your coding sessions are used to improve AI models and cannot be withdrawn after submission — this covers sessions only, not the rest of your codebase Your ratings and written feedback become part of the project's deliverables During sessions: no passwords, API keys, or other people's personal data — and you write your ratings yourself, without AI help Why You'll Love This Your project, your code — you keep full ownership of everything, including code the assistant writes for you Free AI tokens — your AI usage during sessions is fully covered, no subscription or API bill needed Paid to build what you'd build anyway — real compensation for real development work on your own project Fully remote and flexible — work from your own computer, on your own schedule Shape the future of AI-assisted coding — your expert judgment directly improves the next generation of developer tools Spots are limited — the first cohort is small and starting soon

Focused on a bold vision to deliver Smarter Technology for All, Lenovo has built on its success as the world’s largest PC company with a full-stack portfolio of AI-enabled, AI-ready, and AI-optimized devices (PCs, workstations, smartphones, tablets), infrastructure (server, storage, edge, high performance computing and software defined infrastructure), software, solutions, and services. Lenovo’s continued investment in world-changing innovation is building a more equitable, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. Lenovo is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange under Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY). This transformation together with Lenovo’s world-changing innovation is building a more inclusive, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. To find out more visit www.lenovo.com, and read about the latest news via our StoryHub. Lenovo is a global leader in AI infrastructure, high-performance computing, and data centre technologies, helping customers build and scale next-generation accelerated computing environments. As part of the Lenovo Infrastructure Deployment Services (LIDS) team, you will support the validation, benchmarking, and optimisation of large-scale HPC and AI solutions for some of Lenovo's most strategic global customers. In this role, you will execute performance testing, analyse benchmark results, and provide optimisation recommendations across cutting-edge HPC and AI environments, working closely with customers, architects, consultants, and engineering teams. You will be part of a global team supporting EMEA and worldwide projects and will report directly to the Global HPC Delivery Leader. What You Will Do Validate, benchmark, and optimize large-scale HPC and AI platforms, ensuring systems meet performance targets, customer expectations, and acceptance criteria. Design and execute benchmarking and performance test plans across compute, storage, networking, GPUs, and AI workloads, then analyze and present results. Profile applications, identify performance bottlenecks, and provide practical optimization recommendations for HPC, AI, and GPU-accelerated environments. Work with industry-standard HPC benchmarks, AI training and inference workloads, MPI-based applications, storage testing tools, and large-scale cluster validation processes. Partner closely with customers, solution architects, technical consultants, delivery teams, and technology partners to support successful solution deployment and operational readiness. Contribute to the development of benchmarking methodologies, best practices, technical documentation, training materials, and knowledge-sharing initiatives that strengthen Lenovo’s global HPC and AI capabilities. What You Will Bring Strong experience with High Performance Computing (HPC) environments, including cluster architectures, Linux administration, job scheduling, and distributed computing. Proven ability to execute, analyse, and optimise HPC benchmarks and performance validation tests across compute, storage, and networking infrastructure. Solid knowledge of parallel computing technologies, including MPI, OpenMP, CUDA, NCCL, and GPU-accelerated applications. Experience benchmarking and tuning scientific, engineering, AI, and data analytics workloads on large-scale HPC platforms. Strong understanding of NVIDIA GPU technologies and architectures, including H100, H200, B200, and GB200/GB300. Hands-on experience with high-performance networking technologies such as InfiniBand and RoCEv2. Expertise with industry-standard benchmark suites including HPL, HPL-MxP, HPCG, IO500, MLPerf, STREAM, FIO, IOR, and NCCL tests. Knowledge of Top500, Green500, customer acceptance testing methodologies, and HPC performance benchmarking best practices. Experience working with HPC storage solutions such as Lustre, GPFS (IBM Storage Scale), BeeGFS, VAST, WEKA, or similar parallel file systems. Strong Linux skills across RHEL, Rocky Linux, and Ubuntu, combined with shell scripting for automation, benchmark execution, and performance analysis. Ability to identify performance bottlenecks, deliver optimisation recommendations, and create customer-facing benchmark reports, technical documentation, and performance studies. Excellent communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work directly with customers, architects, and engineering teams; experience with AI infrastructure benchmarking, LLMs, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Kubernetes, OpenShift, cloud HPC (Azure/AWS/GCP), Python automation, GPU profiling tools, and enterprise AI acceptance testing is highly desirable.
