What is the role? We are looking for a hands-on,
items.desc: Teamwork makes the stream work. Roku is changing how the world watches TV Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers. From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines. What does the team work on? Roku TV is where embedded systems, media experiences, and intelligent software come together at massive scale. The Roku TV organization builds technology used on millions of TVs globally, and the team is already applying AI to demanding TV problems in resource-constrained environments where quality, performance, and reliability matter. As part of this team, you will help define how agentic AI systems are designed, built, and operated for Roku TV use cases. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who treats AI agent design as an engineering discipline: architecting durable systems, grounding them in the right context, integrating them with tools and services, and making them reliable in production. What is the role? We are looking for a hands-on, systems-oriented Agentic AI Engineer of roughl7 2-5yrs experience to design, build, and maintain intelligent agents and copilots that drive automation, accelerate workflows, and unlock new product and platform capabilities for Roku TV. You will own the full lifecycle of agent development—from prototyping and architecture through orchestration, evaluation, deployment, observability, and continuous improvement. You will contribute directly to Roku’s AI strategy by engineering reusable components, optimizing agent workflows, and ensuring strong real-world performance in production environments. How will I use AI at Roku? At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We’re looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they’ve used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact. We value your AI skills if have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. And you can describe projects where you shipped real work with these tools. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you. What are the responsibilities of the role? Architect, develop, and deploy AI agents and copilots for Roku TV use cases, integrating them with internal systems, tools, and services. Own end-to-end agentic systems from concept to production, including model selection, prompt and context design, retrieval strategies, backend services, and conversational interfaces. Design and implement single-agent and multi-agent orchestration patterns, including handoffs, delegation, and cooperative task execution. Build scalable RAG and context pipelines that provide high-quality grounding for AI systems and keep them aligned with evolving data sources and business logic. Implement tool-calling, function-calling, and MCP-style integrations so agents can safely take actions and interact with the systems around them. Create reusable agent templates, modular components, and paved-path patterns that accelerate adoption across teams and use cases. Establish strong evaluation, observability, and monitoring for conversation quality, task success rate, latency, cost, and overall system performance. Build safeguards that improve production readiness and reliability, including testing pipelines, controlled rollouts, drift detection, and mechanisms that prevent error amplification in multi-step workflows. Prototype quickly, run experiments, and translate successful ideas into durable, scalable software solutions. Partner closely with engineering, product, QA, infrastructure, and cross-functional teams to deliver meaningful business and customer outcomes. What experience would help someone be successful in the role at Roku? Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field. 2-5 years of experience in software engineering, AI/ML engineering, backend development, or adjacent domains, with strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to build production-grade systems. Strong proficiency in Python, plus experience with C/C++ or another systems language. …

items.desc: What can you expect? Marsh is a global leader in insurance broking and risk management, serving clients in over 130 countries. The AI Center of Excellence is a newly formed team with a singular mission: get emerging AI capabilities into the hands of Marsh engineers and business teams as fast as the technology landscape moves. We're looking for an AI Engineer who wants to live on the cutting edge of AI. You'll be the person who picks up preview-stage technologies — new LLM approaches, memory systems, agentic deployment frameworks, guardrails, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tooling — runs rapid proofs-of-concept and turns the successful ones into production-ready capabilities that the rest of Marsh can adopt. This is an individual contributor role, but you'll become the recognised subject-matter expert in one or more AI technology areas. That means coaching your peers in the AI CoE, presenting internally, and — critically — ensuring that both human engineers and autonomous AI coding agents across the enterprise are configured to use these technologies correctly and select them ahead of alternatives. We will count on you to: Run focused proofs-of-concept — typically one or two at a time — to evaluate emerging AI technologies against real Marsh use cases, moving from experiment to recommendation at speed Select and recommend technologies for adoption, producing clear guidance on when and why to use them Productionise chosen capabilities with repeatable, infrastructure-as-code deployment patterns using Crossplane across AWS, Azure, and other hyperscaler clouds, then hand operational ownership to the appropriate platform teams Direct AI coding agents (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, and others) — ensuring they are technically configured to leverage new technologies, select them appropriately, and follow Marsh standards Become a subject-matter expert in one or more AI technology domains (e.g. memory and retrieval, agent orchestration, guardrails and safety, MCP tooling) and coach peers across Marsh on those topics Engage with business units across Marsh through architecture forums, dev councils, and other channels to understand needs and feed requirements back into the PoC pipeline Share knowledge internally through blog posts, demos, and presentations — keeping the wider engineering community informed about what's coming and what's ready What you need to have: Strong software engineering experience in Python and/or TypeScript, with a track record of shipping production systems — not just prototypes Hands-on experience with AI engineering: integrating, deploying, instrumenting, and operating LLM-based systems (prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, function calling, agent frameworks, evaluation, observability) Experience writing infrastructure-as-code for cloud deployments (Crossplane preferred; Terraform, Pulumi, or CDK experience transfers well) Comfort working across multiple cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) rather than deep specialism in one Strong intellectual curiosity and high standards — you actively track emerging technology, learn quickly, and care about doing excellent work The ability to evaluate a new technology quickly and form a clear recommendation Excellent communication skills, able to explain a complex technical decision to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders What makes you stand out: Breadth of programming language experience beyond Python/TypeScript — Rust, Go, or others that demonstrate curiosity and range Familiarity with Model Context Protocol (MCP) — building or consuming MCP servers and tools Experience with Crossplane or Kubernetes-based infrastructure management Exposure to AI safety and guardrails frameworks (content filtering, prompt injection defence, output validation) Experience configuring or extending AI coding assistants (custom instructions, tool integration, workspace configuration) Background in fine-tuning or adapting foundation models What makes this role different: You'll use things before anyone else. Preview APIs, beta frameworks, technologies that don't have Stack Overflow answers yet. You'll shape technical direction. Your PoC outcomes and recommendations directly influence which technologies Marsh adopts across the enterprise. You'll onboard humans and machines. items.desc: Teamwork makes the stream work. Roku is changing how the world watches TV Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers. From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines. What does the team work on? Roku TV is where embedded systems, media experiences, and intelligent software come together at massive scale. The Roku TV organization builds technology used on millions of TVs globally, and the team is already applying AI to demanding TV problems in resource-constrained environments where quality, performance, and reliability matter. As part of this team, you will help define how agentic AI systems are designed, built, and operated for Roku TV use cases. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who treats AI agent design as an engineering discipline: architecting durable systems, grounding them in the right context, integrating them with tools and services, and making them reliable in production. What is the role? We are looking for a hands-on, systems-oriented Agentic AI Engineer of roughl7 2-5yrs experience to design, build, and maintain intelligent agents and copilots that drive automation, accelerate workflows, and unlock new product and platform capabilities for Roku TV. You will own the full lifecycle of agent development—from prototyping and architecture through orchestration, evaluation, deployment, observability, and continuous improvement. You will contribute directly to Roku’s AI strategy by engineering reusable components, optimizing agent workflows, and ensuring strong real-world performance in production environments. How will I use AI at Roku? At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We’re looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they’ve used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact. We value your AI skills if have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. And you can describe projects where you shipped real work with these tools. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you. What are the responsibilities of the role? Architect, develop, and deploy AI agents and copilots for Roku TV use cases, integrating them with internal systems, tools, and services. Own end-to-end agentic systems from concept to production, including model selection, prompt and context design, retrieval strategies, backend services, and conversational interfaces. Design and implement single-agent and multi-agent orchestration patterns, including handoffs, delegation, and cooperative task execution. Build scalable RAG and context pipelines that provide high-quality grounding for AI systems and keep them aligned with evolving data sources and business logic. Implement tool-calling, function-calling, and MCP-style integrations so agents can safely take actions and interact with the systems around them. Create reusable agent templates, modular components, and paved-path patterns that accelerate adoption across teams and use cases. Establish strong evaluation, observability, and monitoring for conversation quality, task success rate, latency, cost, and overall system performance. Build safeguards that improve production readiness and reliability, including testing pipelines, controlled rollouts, drift detection, and mechanisms that prevent error amplification in multi-step workflows. Prototype quickly, run experiments, and translate successful ideas into durable, scalable software solutions. Partner closely with engineering, product, QA, infrastructure, and cross-functional teams to deliver meaningful business and customer outcomes. What experience would help someone be successful in the role at Roku? Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field. 2-5 years of experience in software engineering, AI/ML engineering, backend development, or adjacent domains, with strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to build production-grade systems. items.desc: Wat jij mag verwachten Als AI Ops Engineer maak je deel uit van het AI-team en rapporteer je aan de Domein Product Manager . Je werkt vanuit Antwerpen aan het betrouwbaar, schaalbaar en veilig in productie brengen van AI-oplossingen. In deze rol combineer je diepgaande expertise in AIOps/MLOps met technisch leiderschap rond agentic automation. Je begeleidt data scientists bij het uitrollen van modellen naar productieomgevingen en zorgt ervoor dat AI-oplossingen voldoen aan hoge kwaliteits-, security- en governancevereisten. Je ontwerpt en bouwt betrouwbare data- en inference-pijplijnen, implementeert CI/CD-processen en zet observability op via logging, monitoring, alerts en driftdetectie. Daarnaast werk je samen met Security, Risk & Compliance om AI-oplossingen compliant by design te ontwikkelen. Je neemt een leidende rol op in de ontwikkeling van agentic oplossingen. Van proof of value tot productieontwerp en je bouwt performante oplossingen die veilig integreren met interne systemen via API's, tool use/function calling, RAG en robuuste orkestratiepatronen. Je definieert evaluatie- en testkaders, voert code reviews uit en helpt best practices binnen het team te verankeren. Naast de technische realisatie adviseer je de Product Owner en de Domein Product Manager over architectuurkeuzes, risico's, haalbaarheid en sequencing. Je draagt mee bij aan AI-governance, documentatie, standaarden en de verdere uitbouw van AI-literacy binnen de organisatie. Daarbij werk je nauw samen met architectuur, IT, data scientists en externe deliverypartners. Wat wij verwachten Masterdiploma of gelijkwaardig denkniveau in Computer Science/Engineering/AI, of aantoonbare relevante ervaring. Minstens 3 tot 5 jaar ervaring als AI/ML Engineer, MLOps Engineer of een vergelijkbare functie of sterke motivatie én bewezen basis om te groeien. Vloeiende kennis van Nederlands en Engels. Sterke kennis van AIOps/MLOps, CI/CD, Azure DevOps, Docker, containers en Infrastructure as Code (Terraform). Ervaring met model registry, feature stores, experiment tracking, monitoring, alerting en data- en inferencepijplijnen. Sterke Python-kennis. Ervaring met Azure ML, Azure OpenAI, AI Foundry, Azure AI Search, Fabric, JFrog/ACR en AKS. Kennis van agentic frameworks, RAG, Copilot Studio, DSPy, tool use/function calling en semantic caching. Kennis van security, governance, RBAC, secrets management, data privacy en de EU AI Act is een sterke troef. Kennis van Microsoft Fabric & DB / Vector DB. Waarom kiezen voor deze functie? Deze rol biedt een unieke combinatie van engineeringdiepgang en innovatie. Je helpt AI-oplossingen evolueren van prototype naar schaalbare productieomgevingen met zichtbare impact op kernprocessen. Je krijgt de kans om zowel MLOps/AIOps verder uit te bouwen als technisch richting te geven aan agentic oplossingen. Daarnaast werk je nauw samen met uiteenlopende stakeholders en draag je rechtstreeks bij aan de verdere verankering van AI binnen de organisatie. items.desc: Contexte NXP Semiconducteurs propose des connexions et des infrastructures pour un monde plus intelligent et offre des solutions pour une vie plus facile, meilleure et plus sûre. En tant que leader mondial des solutions de connectivité sécurisée pour les applications embarquées, NXP est le moteur de l'innovation pour le véhicule connecté sécurisé. L’équipe de vérification de la division DES (Drivers & Energy Systems) basée à Toulouse est en charge de vérifier les circuits intégrés à signaux mixtes pour l’automobile, et d’assurer sa conformité par rapport à la spécification du client avant sa fabrication. Nous souhaitons améliorer nos méthodologies innovantes de vérification mixte (AMS), afin de participer à cet objectif d’amélioration continue nous recherchons un stagiaire de fin d’étude sur une durée de 6 mois. Vos missions Le(a) stagiaire prendra en charge/réalisera une ou plusieurs des missions suivantes : Étude des méthodologies actuelles de modélisation AMS et analyse de modèles existants. Développement de scripts Python assistés par IA permettant la mise à jour automatique de modèles hérités vers les standards de modélisation les plus récents. Exploitation des templates générés par le flow de modélisation afin d’automatiser la migration et la maintenance des modèles existants. Construction et enrichissement d’une "Golden Library" de modèles de référence couvrant différentes catégories de fonctions analogiques et mixtes (oscillateurs, ADC, alimentations, surveillance d’alimentation, etc.). Définition de règles et de bonnes pratiques de modélisation à partir des modèles de référence développés. Évaluation et intégration de solutions d’IA générative pour accélérer la création et l’évolution des modèles comportementaux. Développement et expérimentation d’agents IA capables de générer automatiquement des modèles AMS à partir de descriptions de circuits ou de netlists Verilog-AMS. Validation des modèles générés et comparaison des performances, de la maintenabilité et de la qualité des solutions obtenues. Votre profil Niveau d’études : Bac + 5, dernière année d’école d’ingénieur en électronique Connaissances Requises En Conception de circuits électroniques numériques et analogiques Modélisation de blocs analogiques en verilogA, verilog AMS ou system verilog Bonne capacité à synthétiser les concepts et à avoir une vue système Bonne capacité de communication verbale et écrite en français et en anglais La maitrise d’un ou plusieurs outils d’EDA est un plus : Cadence Virtuoso, Cadence Xcelium Une expérience dans l’utilisation des outils d’IA générative est un plus Un bon niveau d’anglais est exigé. Context NXP Semiconductors offers connections and infrastructure for a smarter world and offers solutions for an easier, better and safer life. As a global leader in secure connectivity solutions for embedded applications, NXP is the driver of innovation for the secure connected vehicle. The verification team of the DES division (Drivers & Energy Systems) based in Toulouse is in charge of verifying integrated Analog and Mix Signals (AMS) circuits for the automobile, and to ensure its conformity with the customer’s specification before its manufacture. We wish to improve our innovative methodologies of mixed verification, in order to participate in this objective of continuous improvement we are looking for a trainee of end of study over a period of 6 months. Your Responsibilities The trainee will be responsible for and/or perform one or more of the following tasks: Study existing AMS modeling methodologies and analyze legacy behavioral models. Develop AI-assisted Python scripts to automatically migrate and update legacy models toward the latest modeling standards and methodologies. Leverage model templates generated by the current modeling flow to automate model maintenance and migration activities. Build and enrich a "Golden Library" of reference models covering several analog and mixed-signal functions (oscillators, ADCs, power supplies, power supply monitoring functions, etc.). Define modeling guidelines and best practices based on the developed reference models. Evaluate and integrate generative AI solutions to accelerate behavioral model development and maintenance. Develop and experiment with AI agents capable of automatically generating AMS models from circuit descriptions or Verilog-AMS netlists. Validate generated models and assess their quality, maintainability, and efficiency against existing solutions. Your Profile Education level: Master's degree (Bac+5), final year of an engineering school specializing in electronics. Required Knowledge And Skills Design of digital and analog electronic circuits. Modeling of analog blocks using Verilog-A, Verilog-AMS, or SystemVerilog. Strong ability to synthesize concepts and maintain a system-level perspective. Good verbal and written communication skills in both French and English. Proficiency with one or more EDA tools is a plus: Cadence Virtuoso, Cadence Xcelium. …

items.desc: We are looking for a Rotor Dynamics Specialist to join Coolbrook’s Technology & Engineering team. As a Rotor Dynamics Specialist, you are the technical authority for the rotor dynamics of the rotor, bearing, support, and drivetrain in our RDH and RDR products over the full life cycle, from technology to design to fleet support. You receive rotor geometry and masses from design, component stiffness and temperatures from stress and thermal analysis, and aerodynamic loads from aero, or commissioning and field services. You deliver critical speed and stability margins, bearing and seal requirements, balance specifications, and vibration limits. Coolbrook offers you an exciting role in an international, dynamic, growing company with a real opportunity to make an impact and make history. In this permanent role, you will preferably be based in the UK or Finland offices and report to our Engineering Manager while collaborating with multiple internal and external stakeholders. As Rotor Dynamics Specialist, your responsibilities will include: Lateral analysis: undamped critical speed maps, damped eigenvalue and stability (logarithmic decrement) analysis, and unbalance response with separation margins and amplification factors per API 684 / API 617. Torsional and transient analysis: the full train, covering motor, VFD-induced excitation, coupling, and gearbox where fitted. Includes start-up, coast-down, trip, and electrical fault cases. Rotor architecture: shaft layout, disc stacking and joints, bearing span and overhang. Includes casing, pedestal and foundation stiffness, and coupling selection, all decided together with design and stress. Bearings and seals: specify and assess tilting-pad and fixed-geometry journal and thrust bearings, squeeze-film dampers or magnetic bearings. Assess the rotor dynamic coefficients of seals (labyrinth, brush, dry gas), destabilizing cross-coupling, and the effect of thermal growth on clearances and alignment, using the temperature fields provided by the thermal analysts. Balancing: define the balancing concept and tolerances (ISO 21940), low- versus high-speed balancing, and field trim-balance procedures. Test and validation: specify vibration instrumentation (proximity probes, accelerometers, keyphasor per API 670) and alarm and trip limits. Evaluate run-up and coast-down data (Bode, polar, orbit, waterfall) and run modal impact tests on rotors and supports. Correlate models with test results. Define vibration alarm and trip limits, balancing and alignment acceptance criteria, and run-up/coast-down evaluation templates for commissioning protocols and O&M manuals. Diagnostics: lead root-cause analysis of sub-synchronous vibration, rubs, misalignment, thermal bow, and bearing distress on the test bed and at customer sites. Specifications and reviews: write the rotor dynamic design specification and the requirements for motor, coupling, and bearing suppliers. Present results in design reviews (PDR and CDR) to partners and customers. For success in this role, you will need: An MSc or PhD in mechanical or aerospace engineering, or an equivalent combination of degree and experience. Command of rotor dynamics theory, from Jeffcott rotors to multi-shaft trains, plus hydrodynamic lubrication (Reynolds equation) and bearing and seal dynamic coefficients. Capability to guide internal teams and coordinate with external engineering service providers Hands-on use of a specialist rotor dynamics code (XLTRC2/XLRotor, DyRoBeS, MADYN 2000, ARMD, SAMCEF Rotor or ANSYS Rotor Dynamics) and a general FEA package. Vibration measurement and signal processing, and a working knowledge of API 684, 617 and 670 and ISO 20816 / 21940. Desirable is: Experience with VFD-driven high-speed trains, magnetic bearings, or rotors running at high temperature. Experience with condition monitoring systems (such as Bently Nevada ADRE / System 1). Scripting in Python or MATLAB to automate analyses and post-process test data. Experience levels: For the engineer level: 2–5 years in rotor dynamics or vibration analysis, or a PhD in the field. You build and run train models with guidance and grow quickly with expert mentoring. For the advanced level: 6+ years of rotor dynamics on gas or steam turbines, aero engines, compressors, or large motor-driven trains. Includes test correlation, bearing selection, and field troubleshooting, and you can sign off margins yourself. For the senior level: 12+ years, recognized as the technical authority for rotor dynamics. You set design rules and margins, review supplier analyses, and mentor the team. At Coolbrook, we are passionate about building teams where unique perspectives and backgrounds are valued and where everyone feels equally included. If this resonates with you, we are looking forward to receiving your application. With inquiries about the role, please reach out to Dr. Mark Wilson (mark.wilson@coolbrook.com) or Dr. Frank Eulitz (frank.eulitz@coolbrook.com). About Coolbrook: …

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. Location This is a full-time position based at our HQ in central Zurich. The BLP Academy happens in person, and so does this role: you are in the room with our clients for every cohort. Your Mission You run the room. Two to three days in Zurich that set the tone for every implementation that follows. Before a project kicks off, our clients send the people who will carry it, their BLP Champions, to the BLP Academy. They learn hands-on on our platform, work through real project scenarios, and meet peers from other enterprises facing the same challenges. Across 1,300+ projects, the customer team has made the difference between a smooth and a slow implementation, so these days matter. You make them count. You welcome every participant, run and own the sessions, and set the energy in the room from the first coffee to the last evening. You bring in our BLP experts for deep dives and make sure their expertise lands. Our clients go home certified, connected and ready for their implementation, after an unforgettable few days in Zurich. And as BLP expands across Europe and North America, the Academy will grow with it, with you shaping what that looks like. That takes an unusual mix: part entertainer, part teacher, part professor, with a real curiosity for processes and AI. We care less about where you come from than about what happens when you walk into a room. You will join a fast-growing, global AI company and a team that brings real energy to everything it does. If you light up a room and make complex things simple at the same time, read on. Moderate the deep-dive sessions with BLP experts and connect their content to each participant's situation. Keep the energy high across two to three intense days, and host the evenings and everything around the program. Around each cohort Get every participant ready before they arrive, so the Academy starts with momentum on day one. Make sure every participant completes the BLP Champion Certification and goes home ready for their implementation. Collect feedback and participant NPS, and make every cohort better than the last. items.desc: Connect with Eutelsat Be part of a new era in communications, transforming connectivity with Eutelsat – the world’s first GEO-LEO integrated global satellite operator. As a leader in satellite communications, we provide global connectivity solutions - connecting businesses, communities, and governments around the world. At Eutelsat, we’re united by inclusion and diversity, striving for gender balance and social responsibility, on Earth and in Space. Why Eutelsat ? We are proud that one-third of our executive team and 60% of our board are represented by women. Sustainability at Our Core: At Eutelsat, sustainability is more than just a word; it’s woven into our strategy. We’re dedicated to balancing social, environmental, and economic growth — both on Earth and in space. Work-Life Balance: We offer flexible schedules and hybrid work options to help you balance your personal and professional life. At Eutelsat, we are committed to supporting your well-being and ensuring you have the flexibility you need to succeed both at work and at home. Ready to grow with us? Apply today and help us build a more inclusive, sustainable future in the world of satellite technology. We are looking for an experienced modem architect to become Eutelsat's technical authority on the physical layer of our next generation LEO, multi-orbit and IRIS² user terminals: a Ku and Ka band waveform that must acquire below 0 dB Es/N0, track Doppler excursions of hundreds of kilohertz with slew rates in the tens of kilohertz per second, ride through beam and satellite handovers with an interruption budget of a few tens of milliseconds, and do so within a single digit watt baseband envelope and a cost-driven silicon budget. The target is a single-chip modem module in which the programmable PHY, the protocol stack and the host processor functions share one SoC, built from vector compute engines, a RISC-V control subsystem, hardware accelerators and an on-chip NPU. Much of the detailed implementation is carried out with external engineering and silicon partners. Your role is to master that technology to the point of owning it: to hold the requirements, to model the link independently, to assess and challenge the design choices made on our behalf, and to accept or reject what is delivered on evidence. Knowing the platform hands-on is part of the job, not a formality, and so is the ability to reproduce a result yourself when a claim needs testing. This is a founding role, a pioneering one and the design authority liaising directly with the vendors and internal stakeholders. Eutelsat is building its own terminal physical layer competence and this position is where that capability starts: the models, the tooling, the test assets and the working practices are still to be created, in a programme that moves at constellation pace and relies heavily on external partners while the team is assembled. As the capability grows, this role is the natural anchor for the modem architecture group that will be built around it. What you'll do Master the platform hands-on: SDK and toolchain, micro-kernel architecture of the PHY, mapping onto signal units, scheduling and synchronisation across units, hardware abstraction layers over the FEC and signal processing engines, DMA fabric, interrupts and inter-processor communication. You should be able to build, modify, instrument and profile PHY code yourself; Own the terminal physical layer requirements and their traceability, from service and constellation constraints down to waveform, timing and modem parameters, and hold the specification stable through the programme; Assess and challenge the receive chain design: acquisition strategy and its performance below 0 dB Es/N0, CFO and SFO estimation, timing recovery, carrier phase tracking under composite LO and converter phase noise, channel estimation and interpolation, equalisation, soft demapping and LLR scaling, AGC dynamics, and the loop bandwidth and stability margins behind each of them; Verify the coding scheme and its operating point: code family and rate set, decoder …

items.desc: Build the AI capabilities that will shape the future of housing and real estate software At Zig, AI is no longer a future ambition. Across the business, it's already shaping real problems like rental payment predictions, pricing and asset management , concrete territory, not one fixed use case. This role isn't tied to a single product or country: you'll work across the whole of Zig, wherever the Group is growing. And Zig is growing with a clear ambition: to become the leading property tech company in Europe, with AI at the centre of it. So now we are ready to take the next step, and are hiring a AI Engineer. As our first dedicated AI Engineer, you will help determine how we design, evaluate and scale AI across our products. You will work directly with our Chief AI Officer and turn complex challenges in housing and real estate into dependable product capabilities. This is not a role focused on prototypes that never leave a notebook. You will build AI systems that customers can rely on, that deliver measurable value and that can be evaluated, governed and improved throughout their lifecycle. What will you do? As an AI Engineer, you will take ownership of AI capabilities from initial problem definition through to production and continuous improvement. You Will Design, build, deploy and monitor AI-powered features embedded in Zig’s existing SaaS products, while managing the lifecycle of models, prompts, datasets and releases. Develop evaluation strategies using representative datasets, reference tests, quality metrics and regression testing to demonstrate how AI systems perform before and after release. Work with Product Management, domain experts, engineers and customer-facing teams to identify valuable use cases, assess feasibility and turn business challenges into scalable solutions. Apply generative AI, agentic systems, retrieval-augmented generation and conventional machine learning, while contributing to architecture, privacy, security and AI governance. In your first months, your focus will be on delivering a working version of one of the use cases in Zig’s AI portfolio. Together with our Chief AI Officer, you will also help establish the engineering principles and working methods on which Zig’s future AI capability will be built. What do you bring? You enjoy taking ownership and turning ideas into reality. In this role, you'll have the opportunity to influence technical decisions, challenge existing approaches, and help shape the future of AI within Zig. If you're excited by building new capabilities, continuously improving them and seeing the impact of your work in the hands of customers, this role is for you . Must-haves At least three years of professional software engineering experience, including at least two years working on AI or machine learning systems that reached production and remained in active use. Strong development skills in Python or TypeScript, working proficiency in SQL and the ability to implement solutions directly in product code rather than only in notebooks. Production experience with machine learning or large language models, including prompt and system prompt design, tool or function calling and at least one live RAG or agentic system. A solid conventional machine learning background, including feature engineering, model selection, validation, calibration, experimentation and the judgement to recognise when a language model is not the right solution. Practical experience with evaluation methods and cloud-based AI workloads, combined with clear written and spoken English and the ability to explain technical trade-offs to different stakeholders. Nice-to-haves Experience with one or more of the following would be a plus: Data engineering, relational data stores and vector or hybrid search. Agent interoperability patterns such as Model Context Protocol, or practical exposure to different agent frameworks. Fine-tuning, adapter training, causal inference, uplift modelling or mentoring engineers moving into AI engineering. What do we offer? A challenging position in a fast-growing international software company, with direct access to the person shaping Zig’s AI direction. The opportunity to have a meaningful influence on our technology, architecture and product choices. Plenty of room for initiative, technical ownership, experimentation and professional development. Room to learn, experiment, and grow into an experienced AI Engineer, backed by guidance, coaching, and access to Zig Growth inclusive Udemy. Hybrid working, combining working from home with time at our Bucharest office. A competitive salary based on your knowledge and experience. The opportunity to help build and grow Zig’s AI engineering capability in the coming years. Who are we? At Zig, we build software that makes housing work, for everyone involved. For more than twenty years, we have been developing smart software for housing and real estate organizations. From our roots in the Netherlands, we have grown into a …

items.desc: A Bit About Us At Gamma, we’re more than just a leader in Unified Communications as a Service (UCaaS). We’re a fast-moving technology organisation delivering innovative voice, data, and mobile solutions across Europe. Our product and service portfolio is at the heart of what we do — powering reliable, scalable communications for thousands of businesses. Behind the scenes, our engineering teams design, build, and maintain the software systems that generate real business impact. We combine the agility of a start-up mindset with the stability of a leading European business. Collaboration, ownership, and continuous improvement define how we work — and we’re always looking for people who want to build meaningful technology at scale. Who are we looking for? Design, build, and own end‑to‑end, Snowflake‑based machine learning and advanced analytics solutions that transform telecommunications data into trusted models, insights, and predictions driving customer retention, growth, and commercial decision‑making across the business. What will you be doing day-to-day? Own the end‑to‑end machine learning lifecycle, from problem definition and exploratory analysis through model development, deployment, monitoring, and iteration, delivering production‑grade ML solutions with measurable business impact. Define, design, and continually improve business‑critical “gold” analytics data models on Snowflake, ensuring they represent consistent, trusted views of customers, products, revenue, and usage, and serve as the single analytical truth across reporting, analytics, and ML use cases. Develop, evaluate, and deploy machine learning models relevant to a telecommunications environment, including customer churn prediction, early‑warning indicators, lifetime value forecasting, segmentation, and recommendation or next‑best‑action systems. Ensure analytical datasets, gold data models, and ML outputs are secure, reliable, and performant, applying Snowflake best practices such as RBAC, query optimisation, cost‑efficient compute usage, and appropriate materialisation strategies. Work closely with product, engineering, marketing, finance, and commercial stakeholders to align on definitions, metrics, and analytical priorities, translating ambiguous business problems into well‑scoped analytics and ML solutions. Mentor and uplift the existing data squad responsible for ingestion and transformation, setting standards for analytical data modelling, data quality, and ML‑aware design, and acting as a senior technical authority across the data organisation. What You’ll Need Strong experience in data science and applied machine learning, with proven delivery of models into production environments. Strong background in machine learning, statistics, and data modelling, with hands‑on experience using Python and advanced SQL. Demonstrated experience working with modern cloud data warehouses, with Snowflake as a primary platform strongly preferred. Experience in telecommunications or subscription‑based businesses, particularly working with customer usage, billing, or CRM data, is highly desirable. Track record of mentoring engineers or analysts and leading technical standards within a data team. Kaggle profile or public GitHub projects demonstrating applied ML or analytics work are a strong plus. What do we offer you? At Gamma, we believe in work–life balance, which is why we offer 25 days of annual leave, plus an extra day off for your birthday. We also provide a volunteer day, allowing you to support a cause that matters to you. Family is important to us. With enhanced maternity and paternity pay, we support you at every stage of life. Our contributory pension scheme helps you plan for the future, with Gamma increasing contributions in line with yours. Your wellbeing comes first. We offer group income protection, life assurance (four times your salary), and private medical insurance through Vitality, which extends to your immediate family. We want you to share in our success, which is why we offer tax-efficient share save and share incentive plans. We’re also committed to sustainability, offering an Electric Vehicle scheme through Octopus and a Cycle to Work scheme, making greener travel easier. A few things to note Unfortunately, we can’t offer visa sponsorship or relocation support for this role. This role is hybrid, with office and home working flexibility.If you feel you could be a great fit for Gamma but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply — you might be exactly who we’re looking for. Gamma is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building inclusive, diverse teams where everyone can be their authentic selves. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on any protected characteristics. Recruitment agencies: We work with a trusted group of recruitment partners and are not looking to expand this network at present. Please do not send speculative CVs.

items.desc: Wir Sind In Deutschland zählt BREMER zu den führenden Unternehmen im schlüsselfertigen Industrie- und Gewerbebau. Als ganzheitlicher Anbieter der Immobilien- und Bauwirtschaft begleiten wir unsere Kunden von der Projektentwicklung über die Fertigung in eigenen Werken bis zum schlüsselfertigen Bau und den Serviceleistungen für das Gebäude im laufenden Betrieb. Das 1947 gegründete Familienunternehmen agiert an siebzehn deutschen sowie einem tschechischen und zwei polnischen Standorten und erwirtschaftet derzeit eine Betriebsleistung von ca. 1.000 Mio. EUR. Rund 1.400 Mitarbeitende setzen sich täglich mit Leidenschaft für den Kundenerfolg ein. Starten Sie bei BREMER als FULL-STACK DEVELOPER (m/w/d) und gestalten Sie den Einsatz von KI in unseren Bauprojekten und unserem Fertigteilwerk mit! Gemeinsam mit unseren Fachbereichen identifizieren Sie sinnvolle KI-Anwendungsfälle, entwickeln eigene Lösungen und integrieren neue Software in unsere Systemlandschaft. Wenn Sie fundierte Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung und im Einsatz von KI mitbringen, gerne selbstständig arbeiten und Spaß daran haben, Anwendungen und Prozesse miteinander zu verbinden, freuen wir uns darauf, Sie kennenzulernen! Ihre Aufgaben Use Cases finden: Mit den Fachbereichen und dem Fertigteilwerk identifizieren und priorisieren Sie sinnvolle KI-Anwendungsfälle Eigene Tools bauen: Sie entwickeln KI-gestützte Anwendungen und bringen sie in den produktiven Betrieb, z. B. für Dokumentenverarbeitung, Wissenssuche oder Agenten KI-Produkte begleiten: Sie unterstützen die Auswahl und Einführung von Fachsoftware und binden sie technisch an Systeme verbinden: Sie verantworten das API-Management und sorgen dafür, dass alle Anwendungen zuverlässig miteinander kommunizieren Architektur gestalten: Sie prägen unsere Systemlandschaft und KI-Roadmap und treffen technische Entscheidungen Wissen teilen: Sie bringen neue Tools in die Abteilungen und nehmen die Kolleginnen und Kollegen mit Ihr Profil Mindestens drei Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung, davon Erfahrung mit komplexen Anwendungen in Entwicklung und Betrieb Softwarearchitektur, APIs (REST, OpenAPI), Datenbanken, automatisierte Tests, CI/CD und Deployment sind für Sie Alltag Erfahrung mit der Integration heterogener Systeme, auch von Standardsoftware: Schnittstellen, Datenformate, Authentifizierung und Fehlerbehandlung Sehr gute Python-Kenntnisse, dazu Erfahrung mit TypeScript/JavaScript Praxis darin, KI-Funktionen in produktive Software zu integrieren, insbesondere LLMs, RAG, Prompting und Evaluation Sie arbeiten gern mit Fachleuten ohne IT-Hintergrund, verstehen ihre Abläufe und erklären Technik verständlich Verhandlungssichere Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse Pluspunkte Erfahrung mit API-Gateways, Integrationsplattformen/Middleware oder Event-Streaming Erfahrung mit agentischen Systemen sowie Dokumenten- und Bildverarbeitung mit multimodalen Modellen Fine-Tuning und Inference-Stacks wie vLLM, llama.cpp, ONNXRuntime oder TensorRT; Betrieb von KI auf eigener Infrastruktur Kenntnisse in Bau- oder Fertigungs-IT, z. B. ERP-Systeme, GAEB, IFC/BIM, CAD/CAM Erfahrung mit Softwareauswahl, Anbietermanagement oder Low-Code-Plattformen Kenntnisse zu KI-Governance, DSGVO und EUAI Act Studium der Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Data Science o. Solide Engineering-Grundlagen und echte Praxis mit KI sind uns wichtiger als eine vollständige Liste. items.desc: Buscamos ingeniero/a de IA aplicada. Nos interesa lo que sabes construir. ¿Has desarrollado una solución de IA que puedas enseñar, explicar y desplegar? ¿Te gustaría aplicar ese conocimiento a problemas concretos del sector industrial? En Ágere IA Companionship buscamos una persona con formación en ingeniería que quiera participar en el desarrollo de soluciones de IA, desde las primeras decisiones técnicas hasta su implementación. También consideraremos perfiles junior con proyectos verificables. Pueden ser profesionales, académicos, personales u open source. Queremos entender qué has construido, qué parte realizaste y qué aprendiste al hacerlo funcionar. Un equipo pequeño donde tu criterio contará Te integrarás en un equipo formado actualmente por cuatro ingenieros informáticos full-stack y dependerás del director de desarrollo, con quien podrás contrastar las decisiones. Aportarás conocimiento específico de IA y colaborarás con quienes desarrollan las aplicaciones e integraciones. Tu trabajo incluirá modelos comerciales y de pesos abiertos, conexión con datos y herramientas empresariales, y participación en el diseño, despliegue y mantenimiento de la infraestructura. Nos importa elegir la tecnología adecuada para cada problema. También comprobar que los resultados sean útiles, proteger los datos y entender cuánto cuesta mantener una solución funcionando. Tiempo reservado para investigar y construir nuevas soluciones El puesto tendrá una segunda área de actividad: I+D aplicada, con tiempo reservado para desarrollarla. Trabajarás junto a la Dirección General y la Dirección de Desarrollo para identificar necesidades repetidas y convertirlas en soluciones estandarizadas. El foco principal será el sector industrial. Exploraremos aplicaciones en mantenimiento, control de calidad, mejora de operaciones y gestión del conocimiento y la documentación técnica. No esperamos que domines todos estos ámbitos desde el inicio. Sí que tengas curiosidad, criterio para experimentar y capacidad para distinguir una idea interesante de una solución viable. Qué base necesitas Buscamos conocimientos prácticos de Python, aprendizaje automático, APIs, datos y despliegue. Haber trabajado con modelos comerciales y de pesos abiertos, utilizar Git y desenvolverte con Linux y Docker. Valoraremos la experiencia con herramientas como PyTorch, TensorFlow o scikit-learn, sin exigir que domines todas. También los proyectos en producción, RAG, agentes, visión artificial o datos industriales. La rama de ingeniería no es lo decisivo. Lo decisivo es que puedas demostrar los conocimientos necesarios y explicar tus decisiones. Cómo trabajaremos El trabajo será en remoto, con residencia en España y horario español. Necesitarás español e inglés como herramientas de trabajo; valoraremos el catalán. Buscamos preferentemente contratación laboral, aunque estamos abiertos a colaboración como autónomo, con dedicación parcial o completa. Habrá viajes puntuales para demos y presentaciones. La incorporación está prevista en unos dos meses. Nos gustaría conocer tu trabajo Comparte tu CV y uno o dos proyectos. Cuéntanos qué problema resuelven, cuál fue tu aportación y cómo los desplegaste. Si son confidenciales, puedes presentarlos de forma anonimizada. Indica también tu disponibilidad, la dedicación que buscas y tus expectativas retributivas.

items.desc:
Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
 About the team 
 The UI Platform team, known as Sail, builds the foundations behind Stripe’s Dashboard and many other user interfaces. Sail Services owns the systems that evaluate feature flags and experiments, ingest frontend analytics, and improve Dashboard load times for Stripe’s largest merchants.
 We build backend-for-frontend capabilities that connect Stripe’s backend systems to its UI platform. This gives product teams a consistent way to build and operate user experiences without recreating the same infrastructure.
 What you’ll do 
 As a Backend Engineer on the Sail Services team, you’ll help build and evolve the systems that power Stripe’s user interfaces. You’ll independently drive software projects from problem definition through production, working closely with other UI Platform engineers, product teams, and infrastructure partners. Your work will range from APIs and GraphQL integrations to edge systems, architectural migrations, and the tooling needed to operate them safely at scale.
 Responsibilities 
 Take end-to-end ownership of software projects, aligning on priorities and then independently scoping problems and carrying solutions through design, implementation, testing, rollout, and operation
 Design, build, and operate reliable, scalable APIs and backend systems that support Stripe’s Dashboard, mobile applications, and other user interfaces
 Help modernize Stripe’s UI architecture through incremental migrations, automated validation, shadow traffic, and carefully controlled production rollouts
 Improve the reliability, observability, performance, and operability of services on critical user paths
 Partner with frontend, backend, and infrastructure engineers to understand their needs and turn recurring problems into reusable platform capabilities
 Use AI-assisted and agentic development workflows to improve implementation, testing, validation, and delivery
 Contribute thoughtful code reviews, technical discussions, documentation, and runbooks that improve the quality of the team’s work
 Who you are 
 We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
 Minimum requirements 
 Fluency in using AI-assisted and agentic development tools as part of day-to-day software engineering, including critically reviewing, validating, and improving generated code
 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience, building, shipping, and operating production systems
 Strong knowledge of backend technologies and infrastructure, including the fundamentals of APIs, data storage, distributed systems, and production operations
 Ability to independently scope and deliver open-ended software projects, making practical technical and product tradeoffs with limited oversight
 Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, with attention to testing, maintainability, reliability, and user impact
 Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with frontend engineers, product engineers, and infrastructure partners
 Preferred qualifications 
 Experience building backend-for-frontend systems, UI platform services, developer platforms, or shared infrastructure
 Experience designing or integrating APIs, including GraphQL APIs
 Experience with high-throughput event ingestion, feature flag or experimentation systems, or other latency-sensitive platform services

items.desc:
Who we are
 About Stripe
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
 About the team
 The UI Platform team, known as Sail, builds the foundations that support Stripe’s Dashboard and many of Stripe’s other user interfaces. The Sail UI team owns Stripe’s design system, helping Stripe engineers create consistent, accessible, performant, and high-quality experiences at scale.
 We build and maintain reusable components, design tokens, theming capabilities, documentation, and developer tooling used by engineers and designers across Stripe. We are currently focused on two major projects. First, we are building Sail for Agents: the generation infrastructure, documentation systems, agent integrations, and automated quality checks that help AI coding agents build high-quality Stripe interfaces safely and consistently at scale. Second, we are evolving the visual language of the Dashboard, one of Stripe’s largest UI surfaces, while modernizing its underlying codebase.
 What you’ll do
 As a Frontend Engineer on the Sail UI team, you’ll help build and evolve Stripe’s design system and the tools that enable engineers and AI coding agents to create high-quality user interfaces. You’ll independently drive frontend projects from problem definition through rollout, working closely with designers, product engineers, and other Sail engineers. Your work will range from reusable components, themes, and documentation to agentic tooling, automated quality checks, and modernizing the foundations of Stripe’s Dashboard.
 Responsibilities
 Take end-to-end ownership of software projects, independently scoping problems and carrying solutions through design, implementation, testing, and rollout
 Build and maintain accessible, performant, and well-tested components, themes, and frontend APIs used across Stripe
 Build tooling, documentation, and automated quality checks that help engineers and AI coding agents use Sail effectively and meet Stripe’s UI quality bar
 Partner with product designers and engineers to understand their needs and turn recurring UI patterns into reusable design-system capabilities
 Help evolve the visual language of Stripe’s Dashboard while modernizing its underlying codebase and migrating legacy UI patterns
 Improve the accessibility, internationalization, observability, performance, reliability, and developer experience of the design system
 Contribute thoughtful code reviews, technical discussions, and documentation that improve the quality of the team’s work
 Who you are 
 We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 
 Minimum requirements
 Fluency in using AI-assisted and agentic development tools as part of day-to-day software engineering, including critically reviewing, validating, and improving generated code
 2+ years of professional frontend engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience, building, shipping, and debugging web applications
 Strong knowledge of modern frontend technologies and frameworks, including browser fundamentals, responsive design, and accessibility
 Ability to independently scope and deliver open-ended frontend projects, making practical technical and product tradeoffs with limited oversight
 Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, with attention to testing, maintainability, and the quality of the resulting user experience
 Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with designers, product engineers, and other partners
 Preferred qualifications 
 Experience working on a design system, frontend platform, or shared component library
 Experience with developer tooling such as build tools, package managers, codemods, lint rules, or large monorepos
 Experience building tools, integrations, or automated evaluation and quality systems for AI coding agents
 Experience using documentation, developer feedback, or adoption data to improve a developer-facing product

Ideally located between the Mediterranean sea and the Atlantic ocean and close to the Pyrenees mountains, it offers plenty of options for outdoor activities!

items.desc: Le poste Data Product & Analytics réunit deux missions : Rôle Data Product : définir et déployer l'approche Data Product de Redion afin de faire évoluer progressivement l'organisation d'une logique orientée projets et reporting vers une véritable logique Data Product, domaine par domaine. Data Business Partner pour de nouveaux domaines (les domaines existants incluent Voyage, Mobilité, Finance, Opérations). Les deux missions forment une seule et même boucle. Tout ce qui est conçu dans le cadre du rôle produit n'est pas théorique mais appliqué dans les propres domaines du/de la candidat(e). Ceux-ci servent de vitrine / de terrain d'expérimentation avant la généralisation de l'approche. Notre plateforme data d'entreprise est un levier clé de cette transformation : elle est conçue pour unifier, standardiser et sécuriser les données granulaires à travers les régions et les entités, avec pour objectifs un reporting plus rapide, une analytique à forte valeur ajoutée et une visibilité transverse entre entités. Elle repose sur une stack AWS (ex. S3 / Glue / Redshift / Bedrock) et est intégrée à l'écosystème analytique et IA du Groupe (AWS Unified Studio, Microsoft Fabric + Power BI, Nao AI Analytics). Poste et responsabilités Data Product transverse Définition du data product : définir clairement ce qu'est un data product chez Redion et en quoi il se distingue d'un rapport, d'un dataset ou d'un cas d'usage ; construire un vocabulaire commun et un ensemble de critères partagés par les équipes centrales et locales. Vision du portefeuille par domaine : cartographier l'existant par domaine (tableaux de bord, datasets, modèles, actifs IA) et accompagner les équipes dans l'identification des produits que chaque domaine devra progressivement construire. Product Operating Model : définir la méthodologie commune applicable à tous les domaines : discovery, définition et spécifications produit, roadmap et backlog, priorisation, cycle de vie de l'idéation au décommissionnement, ownership, gouvernance et mesure de la valeur. De la livraison à l'impact : s'assurer que les produits génèrent un impact mesurable : KPI d'adoption et de valeur suivis et exploités pour chaque produit ; accompagner le lancement, la présentation et l'adoption des produits. Leviers d'adoption – marketplace & expérience utilisateur : activer les leviers qui facilitent l'adoption : une marketplace permettant aux équipes centrales et locales de publier des produits que les utilisateurs peuvent trouver, comprendre, utiliser en confiance et auxquels ils peuvent accéder ; et une pratique systématique consistant à se mettre à la place des utilisateurs, en testant à quel point il est réellement intuitif de trouver, utiliser et partager ces produits, afin d'améliorer continuellement cette expérience. Gouvernance produit & coaching : piloter la gouvernance des data products et accompagner les équipes data, au niveau central et local, dans les pratiques produit, en s'appuyant sur ses propres domaines comme exemples concrets. Data Business Partner – Nouveaux domaines Partenariat : être l'interlocuteur data principal des parties prenantes métier ; instaurer la confiance, comprendre leurs processus et leurs décisions ; transformer les problématiques métier (et pas uniquement les demandes) en data products et en cas d'usage. items.desc: Build something monumental for Healthcare! At Tandem Health we’re reimagining healthcare by putting clinicians first. Our platform - designed by clinicians, for clinicians - is built on deep insight into real-world pain points, with intuitive medical notes and workflows that truly support patient care. We’re a fast-scaling health-tech company backed by top investors and expanding globally. We move fast, stay curious, and believe building something that matters starts with an extraordinary team. If you're passionate about impact and innovation, we'd love to meet you! About the Role Help make Tandem work reliably in the IT environments where clinicians use it. As our IT Solutions Engineer , you’ll combine hands-on technical investigation with customer ownership, working directly with hospital and clinic IT teams and the engineers who build our product. Your remit spans Tandem’s products: app deployment, virtual desktops, browsers, integrations, sign-in and audio setups. When something goes wrong, the cause can sit anywhere between our product, a device and the customer’s IT environment. You’ll bring the right people together, find the cause and stay with the issue until the fix works for the customer. You’ll be the one clear technical owner for customer IT teams from first report to resolution, while the relevant engineering team owns the product fix and you provide the evidence and verify the outcome. You do need strong enterprise IT fundamentals, a methodical approach and the ability to lead an investigation across systems and teams. You’ll work closely with Product, Medical Operations and Customer Success across our markets. Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll turn what you learn into better diagnostics, setup guidance and product improvements that prevent repeat problems and help Medical Operations and Customer Success solve more on their own. What You'll Do Lead complex post-sales technical investigations with customer IT teams and partners, keeping ownership of communication and next steps through resolution. Troubleshoot across Windows clients, app deployment, virtual desktops, browser and network policies, integrations, sign-in and audio devices, involving specialists where needed. Use logs, environment checks and test setups to isolate causes and give the relevant engineering team actionable reproductions of product issues, not open-ended escalations. Coordinate fixes across teams, track progress and verify that they work in the customer’s environment. Support go-live readiness by reviewing customer environments with Enablement, Medical Operations and Customer Success and flagging technical risks early. Turn recurring issues into troubleshooting guides, scripts, diagnostics and product improvements so they stop coming back and colleagues can solve more problems independently. What You Bring Hands-on experience in a customer-facing technical role, such as post-sales solutions engineering, technical support engineering or IT infrastructure, ideally in B2B SaaS or healthcare IT. Hands-on Citrix experience, including policies, virtual channels and device redirection; experience with IGEL, VMware Horizon, Azure Virtual Desktop or Windows 365 is also valuable. Strong Windows and enterprise IT fundamentals, including software deployment, devices and drivers, group policies and Remote Desktop, plus working knowledge of browsers and networking. A methodical approach to unfamiliar problems: form a hypothesis, test it, read the logs and document what you find. Basic scripting, for example PowerShell or Python, to check environments, automate tests or analyse logs. Clear communication with IT administrators, clinicians and engineers, and the ability to coordinate an investigation across teams without losing ownership. Patience and persistence with problems that take more than one call to solve. Working proficiency in English. Bonus Points Experience with EHR systems, healthcare IT or integrations between clinical systems. Experience with audio: microphones, dictation hardware such as Philips SpeechMike, conference systems or room acoustics. Knowledge of browser and network setups, such as extension policies, microphone permissions, proxies and firewalls. Experience with macOS, iOS or Android in managed environments. Experience with enterprise sign-in, such as Microsoft Entra ID and SSO. Experience building with agentic engineering. Additional European languages, for example German, French. Location We believe the best ideas happen when we’re together. This role is based in our vibrant HQ at Kungsgatan 12-14 in the heart of Stockholm where you will work primarily from our office to collaborate, connect, and build our culture. How to Apply We adopt a continuous selection process, so please make sure to apply with your CV in English. Our interview process consists of 4 stages: Screening interview with Talent Acquisition Follow-up interview with one of our Team Leads Home case and presentation at our office …

The Data Flow Specialist role sits within the Data Value Office (DVO) for the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) organization of GSK’s Research & Development (R&D) function. This role is focused on delivering data-flows-as-product, compliance-as-code, and governance built into the pipeline (instead of bolted-on). You will turn scattered systems and sources into modular, reusable, end-to-end flows in one consistent format that can be used to its full potential throughout GSK’s R&D divisions. Your mission is to make R&D data visible, trusted and automation-ready (by default) so teams can decide faster and scale agentic solutions with confidence (whilst keeping the human expert in the loop). Integrate diverse data flows such as protocol development, DSUR and clinical trial IHD into a unified machine readable format for consistent implementation and a genuine end-to-end data ecosystem. Ensure deliverables are appropriately quality controlled, documented and, where required, able to be handed over to function leads and the R&D Tech team for scale implementation. Provide coaching and peer review to ensure the team's work reflects industry best practice for data flow creation activities, including data standards. However, the Company plans to relocate its offices to Cambridge, UK. The location of this role will therefore subsequently change to Cambridge UK, in accordance with timelines to be set by the Company. The relocation is currently proposed to take effect by early 2029. About GSK: At GSK, we have bold ambitions for patients, aiming to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade. Our R&D focuses on discovering and delivering vaccines and medicines, combining our understanding of the immune system with cutting-edge technology to transform people’s lives. GSK fosters a culture ambitious for patients, accountable for impact, and committed to doing the right thing, making sure that we focus our efforts on accelerating significant assets that meet patients’ needs and have the highest probability of success. We’re uniting science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together. Find out more - our approach to R&D: https://www.gsk.com/en-gb/innovation/ APPLICATION CLOSING DATE – Monday 9 th of November 2026 (COB). Expertise in data-flow design and orchestration (including pre-processing, integrating, contextualising and governing data and systems into end-to-end workflows). Proficiency in integrating multiple data sources and systems into unified, reusable data-flows. Knowledge / experience of metadata ecosystems and building agentic solutions. items.desc:
1. The company, its business and its ambition
 The ambition. Fabriq is bringing European industry into the 21st century: making factories more competitive and frontline teams more autonomous. This is not only a software play, it is the industrial relocalisation project.
 The business. Fabriq is the SaaS platform that replaces the whiteboards and Excel spreadsheets still running 80% of industrial sites. Operators, team leads and plant managers track real-time KPIs (safety, quality, lead time, productivity), surface and solve shop-floor problems, run their daily routines and collaborate across teams in one place. The long-term ambition is to become the Operating System of every production floor.
 The proof. 
 700+ industrial sites equipped across 43+ countries.
 Reference customers such as Safran, Airbus, Renault, Scania, LVMH, Andros, Bel, Merck and Lonza.
 Profitable since late 2024, then €22M raised in June 2025 with Expedition Capital to accelerate in the US, the UK and DACH.
 A team of ~130 people, and an AI roadmap that is already in customers’ hands rather than on a slide.
 2. The role
 Context : You join the AI team, a two-person unit led by Jean (Product Lead) alongside Halim, Senior Engineer who has built much of the Fabriq product. This team operates as a prototyping squad at the front edge of the company: it tests new ideas, measures market appetite and decides whether Fabriq goes there. Products are in alpha, cycles are short, the roadmap is directional. The team also works weekly with Octave, co-founder, which gives you direct exposure to the strategic decisions.
 Objective : Become Halim’s pair and second engineer on AI, reach full autonomy on the stack and the customer context within 6 months, and take Fabriq’s AI products from alpha to something industrial teams rely on every day.
 Challenges : 
 Taking AI prototypes to production quality. Conversational and voice-driven agents, plugged into real industrial data and used by real teams on the floor. You take them from alpha to something people rely on daily: answer quality, reliability, and the cost per interaction that decides whether a use case scales or gets dropped.
 Prototyping to convince. Part of the roadmap is co-built with partner customers, which means it is sold before it is built. Specs move as customers shape them, timelines are tight, and you build fast to prove a use case is worth pursuing. Testing a lot and abandoning a lot is part of the deal.
 Agentic engineering from scratch. No Mastra, no LangGraph, no off-the-shelf framework. Everything is hand-built in TypeScript and Deno on top of frontier models called through AWS Bedrock. When the team needs something like agent memory compaction, you design it yourself. This is genuinely custom, sparsely documented territory, and that is precisely the technical interest of the role.
 Setting the technical direction with Halim. You are the second engineer, not an extra pair of hands: code reviews, architecture debates, and the freedom to arrive with your own proposals rather than waiting for a ticket.
 Your first 3 months are dedicated to ramping up on the Fabriq stack and product, contributing to the AI features already in the hands of beta customers, and shipping your first POCs.

Job Description The company, its business and its ambition The ambition. Fabriq is bringing European industry into the 21st century: making factories more competitive and frontline teams more autonomous. This is not only a software play, it is the industrial relocalisation project. The business. Fabriq is the SaaS platform that replaces the whiteboards and Excel spreadsheets still running 80% of industrial sites. Operators, team leads and plant managers track real-time KPIs (safety, quality, lead time, productivity), surface and solve shop-floor problems, run their daily routines and collaborate across teams in one place. The long-term ambition is to become the Operating System of every production floor. The proof. 700+ industrial sites equipped across 43+ countries. Reference customers such as Safran, Airbus, Renault, Scania, LVMH, Andros, Bel, Merck and Lonza. Profitable since late 2024, then €22M raised in June 2025 with Expedition Capital to accelerate in the US, the UK and DACH. A team of ~130 people, and an AI roadmap that is already in customers' hands rather than on a slide. The role Context : You join the AI team, a two-person unit led by Jean (Product Lead) alongside Halim, Senior Engineer who has built much of the Fabriq product. This team operates as a prototyping squad at the front edge of the company: it tests new ideas, measures market appetite and decides whether Fabriq goes there. Products are in alpha, cycles are short, the roadmap is directional. The team also works weekly with Octave, co-founder, which gives you direct exposure to the strategic decisions. Objective : Become Halim's pair and second engineer on AI, reach full autonomy on the stack and the customer context within 6 months, and take Fabriq's AI products from alpha to something industrial teams rely on every day. Challenges Taking AI prototypes to production quality. Conversational and voice-driven agents, plugged into real industrial data and used by real teams on the floor. You take them from alpha to something people rely on daily: answer quality, reliability, and the cost per interaction that decides whether a use case scales or gets dropped. Prototyping to convince. Part of the roadmap is co-built with partner customers, which means it is sold before it is built. Specs move as customers shape them, timelines are tight, and you build fast to prove a use case is worth pursuing. Testing a lot and abandoning a lot is part of the deal. Agentic engineering from scratch. No Mastra, no LangGraph, no off-the-shelf framework. Everything is hand-built in TypeScript and Deno on top of frontier models called through AWS Bedrock. When the team needs something like agent memory compaction, you design it yourself. This is genuinely custom, sparsely documented territory, and that is precisely the technical interest of the role. Setting the technical direction with Halim. You are the second engineer, not an extra pair of hands: code reviews, architecture debates, and the freedom to arrive with your own proposals rather than waiting for a ticket. Your first 3 months are dedicated to ramping up on the Fabriq stack and product, contributing to the AI features already in the hands of beta customers, and shipping your first POCs. Preferred Experience Skills and experience Must-haves Software engineering depth: 4 to 5 years minimum. Real craftsmanship, clean design decisions, and the ability to explain the architecture trade-offs you made and why. Daily hands-on use of AI to build software. Having never used AI to develop is a deal-breaker on this role. Comfort with ambiguity. You move forward, decide and ship when nothing is specified in advance, and you adapt when the roadmap shifts. Builder mindset with evidence. Concrete examples of things you built from zero, prototyped, tested and iterated on. Nice-to-haves (optional) A first hands-on experience with agentic systems. Expertise is welcome when it is real : a strong engineer with genuine curiosity and early agentic work beats a self-declared two-year agentic expert who cannot explain concretely what they built. A data background. The testing logic differs from pure software: working on datasets and analysing where a system succeeds and where it fails is a plus, …
